# The Coq Reference Manual, Release 8.19.0

*Converted from the published Sphinx HTML manual at <https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/>.*

# Introduction and Contents

This is the reference manual of Coq. Coq is an interactive theorem prover. It lets you formalize mathematical concepts and then helps you interactively generate machine-checked proofs of theorems. Machine checking gives users much more confidence that the proofs are correct compared to human-generated and -checked proofs. Coq has been used in a number of flagship verification projects, including the [CompCert verified C compiler](http://compcert.inria.fr/), and has served to verify the proof of the [four color theorem](https://github.com/math-comp/fourcolor) (among many other mathematical formalizations).

Users generate proofs by entering a series of tactics that constitute steps in the proof. There are many built-in tactics, some of which are elementary, while others implement complex decision procedures (such as [`lia`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/micromega.html#coq:tacn.lia), a decision procedure for linear integer arithmetic). [Ltac](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#ltac) and its planned replacement, [Ltac2](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac2.html#ltac2), provide languages to define new tactics by combining existing tactics with looping and conditional constructs. These permit automation of large parts of proofs and sometimes entire proofs. Furthermore, users can add novel tactics or functionality by creating Coq plugins using OCaml.

The Coq kernel, a small part of Coq, does the final verification that the tactic-generated proof is valid. Usually the tactic-generated proof is indeed correct, but delegating proof verification to the kernel means that even if a tactic is buggy, it won't be able to introduce an incorrect proof into the system.

Finally, Coq also supports extraction of verified programs to programming languages such as OCaml and Haskell. This provides a way of executing Coq code efficiently and can be used to create verified software libraries.

To learn Coq, beginners are advised to first start with a tutorial / book. Several such tutorials / books are listed at <https://coq.inria.fr/documentation>.

This manual is organized in three main parts, plus an appendix:

- **The first part presents the specification language of Coq**, that allows to define programs and state mathematical theorems. [Core language](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/index.html#core-language) presents the language that the kernel of Coq understands. [Language extensions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/index.html#extensions) presents the richer language, with notations, implicits, etc. that a user can use and which is translated down to the language of the kernel by means of an "elaboration process".

- **The second part presents proof mode**, the central feature of Coq. [Basic proof writing](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/index.html#writing-proofs) introduces this interactive mode and the available proof languages. [Automatic solvers and programmable tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/index.html#automatic-tactics) presents some more advanced tactics, while [Creating new tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/creating-tactics/index.html#writing-tactics) is about the languages that allow a user to combine tactics together and develop new ones.

- **The third part shows how to use Coq in practice.** [Libraries and plugins](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/index.html#libraries) presents some of the essential reusable blocks from the ecosystem and some particularly important extensions such as the program extraction mechanism. [Command-line and graphical tools](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/tools/index.html#tools) documents important tools that a user needs to build a Coq project.

- In the appendix, [History and recent changes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/appendix/history-and-changes/index.html#history-and-changes) presents the history of Coq and changes in recent releases. This is an important reference if you upgrade the version of Coq that you use. The various [indexes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/appendix/indexes/index.html#indexes) are very useful to **quickly browse the manual and find what you are looking for.** They are often the main entry point to the manual.

# Core language

At the heart of the Coq proof assistant is the Coq kernel. While users have access to a language with many convenient features such as [notations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#syntax-extensions-and-notation-scopes), [implicit arguments](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/implicit-arguments.html#implicitarguments), etc. (presented in the [next chapter](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/index.html#extensions)), those features are translated into the core language (the Calculus of Inductive Constructions) that the kernel understands, which we present here. Furthermore, while users can build proofs interactively using tactics (see Chapter [Basic proof writing](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/index.html#writing-proofs)), the role of these tactics is to incrementally build a "proof term" which the kernel will verify. More precisely, a proof term is a [term](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-term) of the Calculus of Inductive Constructions whose [type](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-type) corresponds to a theorem statement. The kernel is a type checker which verifies that terms have their expected types.

This separation between the kernel on one hand and the [elaboration engine](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/index.html#extensions) and [tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/index.html#writing-proofs) on the other follows what is known as the de Bruijn criterion (keeping a small and well delimited trusted code base within a proof assistant which can be much more complex). This separation makes it necessary to trust only a smaller, critical component (the kernel) instead of the entire system. In particular, users may rely on external plugins that provide advanced and complex tactics without fear of these tactics being buggy, because the kernel will have to check their output.

# Basic notions and conventions

This section provides some essential notions and conventions for reading the manual.

We start by explaining the syntax and lexical conventions used in the manual. Then, we present the essential vocabulary necessary to read the rest of the manual. Other terms are defined throughout the manual. The reader may refer to the [glossary index](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/std-glossindex.html#glossary-index) for a complete list of defined terms. Finally, we describe the various types of settings that Coq provides.

## Syntax and lexical conventions

### Syntax conventions

The syntax described in this documentation is equivalent to that accepted by the Coq parser, but the grammar has been edited to improve readability and presentation.

In the grammar presented in this manual, the terminal symbols are black (e.g. `forall`), whereas the nonterminals are green, italic and hyperlinked (e.g. [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)). Some syntax is represented graphically using the following kinds of blocks:

`item?`  
An optional item.

`item+`  
A list of one or more items.

`item*`  
An optional list of items.

`item+s`  
A list of one or more items separated by "s" (e.g. `item`<sub>`1`</sub>` s item`<sub>`2`</sub>` s item`<sub>`3`</sub>).

`item*s`  
An optional list of items separated by "s".

`item`<sub>`1`</sub>`item`<sub>`2`</sub>`...`  
Alternatives (either `item`<sub>`1`</sub> or `item`<sub>`2`</sub> or ...).

[Precedence levels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_operations) that are implemented in the Coq parser are shown in the documentation by appending the level to the nonterminal name (as in [`term100`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term100) or [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3)).

Note

Coq uses an extensible parser. Plugins and the [notation system](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#syntax-extensions-and-notation-scopes) can extend the syntax at run time. Some notations are defined in the [prelude](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#term-prelude), which is loaded by default. The documented grammar doesn't include these notations. Precedence levels not used by the base grammar are omitted from the documentation, even though they could still be populated by notations or plugins.

Furthermore, some parsing rules are only activated in certain contexts ([proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#proofhandling), [custom entries](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#custom-entries)...).

Warning

Given the complexity of these parsing rules, it would be extremely difficult to create an external program that can properly parse a Coq document. Therefore, tool writers are advised to delegate parsing to Coq, by communicating with it, for instance through [SerAPI](https://github.com/ejgallego/coq-serapi).

See also

[`Print Grammar`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Grammar)

### Lexical conventions

Blanks  
Space, newline and horizontal tab are considered blanks. Blanks are ignored but they separate tokens.

Comments  
Comments are enclosed between `(*` and `*)`. They can be nested. They can contain any character. However, embedded [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string) literals must be correctly closed. Comments are treated as blanks.

Identifiers  
Identifiers, written [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), are sequences of letters, digits, `_` and `'`, that do not start with a digit or `'`. That is, they are recognized by the following grammar (except that the string `_` is reserved; it is not a valid identifier):

``` ebnf
ident                    ::=     first_letter subsequent_letter *
first_letter             ::=     a .. z  A .. Z  _  unicode_letter
subsequent_letter        ::=     first_letter  digit  '  unicode_id_part
```

All characters are meaningful. In particular, identifiers are case-sensitive. `unicode_letter` non-exhaustively includes Latin, Greek, Gothic, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew, Georgian, Hangul, Hiragana and Katakana characters, CJK ideographs, mathematical letter-like symbols and non-breaking space. `unicode_id_part` non-exhaustively includes symbols for prime letters and subscripts.

Numbers  
Numbers are sequences of digits with an optional fractional part and exponent, optionally preceded by a minus sign. Hexadecimal numbers start with `0x` or `0X`. [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer)s are signed numbers without fraction or exponent parts. [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)s are non-negative integers. Underscores embedded in the digits are ignored, for example `1_000_000` is the same as `1000000`.

``` ebnf
number                   ::=     - ? decnat . digit  _ + ? e  E +  - ? decnat ?
                         |       - ? hexnat . hexdigit  _ + ? p  P +  - ? decnat ?
integer                  ::=     bigint
bigint                   ::=     - ? bignat
natural                  ::=     bignat
bignat                   ::=     decnat  hexnat
decnat                   ::=     digit digit  _ *
digit                    ::=     0 .. 9
hexnat                   ::=     0x  0X hexdigit hexdigit  _ *
hexdigit                 ::=     0 .. 9  a .. f  A .. F
```

`number`, [`bigint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bigint) and [`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat), which are used in [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)s, generally have no range limitation. [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) and [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural), which are used as arguments in tactics and commands, are limited to the range that fits into an OCaml integer (63-bit integers on most architectures).

The [standard library](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#thecoqlibrary) provides a few [interpretations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#id8) for [`number`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-number). Some of these interpretations support exponential notation for decimal numbers, for example `5.02e-6` means 5.02×10<sup>-6</sup>; and base 2 exponential notation for hexadecimal numbers denoted by `p` or `P`, for example `0xAp12` means 10×2<sup>12</sup>. The [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) mechanism lets the user define custom parsers and printers for [`number`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-number).

By default, numbers are interpreted as `nat`s, which is a unary representation. For example, `3` is represented as `S (S (S O))`. While this is a convenient representation for doing proofs, computing with large `nat`s can lead to stack overflows or running out of memory. You can explicitly specify a different interpretation to avoid this problem. For example, `1000000%Z` is a more efficient binary representation of that number as an integer. See [Notation scopes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#scopes) and [`term_scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-term_scope).

> Example: Stack overflow with `nat`
>
> ``` coq
> Fail Eval compute in 100000 + 100000. (* gives a stack overflow (not shown) *)
> The command has indeed failed with message:
> To avoid stack overflow, large numbers in nat are interpreted as applications
> of Nat.of_num_uint. [abstract-large-number,numbers,default]
>
> Require Import ZArith. (* for definition of Z *)
>
> Eval compute in (1000000000000000000000000000000000 + 1)%Z.
>      = 1000000000000000000000000000000001%Z
>      : Z
> ```

Strings  
Strings begin and end with `"` (double quote). Use `""` to represent a double quote character within a string. In the grammar, strings are identified with `string`.

The [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) mechanism offers the user a way to define custom parsers and printers for [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string).

<!-- -->

Keywords  
The following character sequences are keywords defined in the main Coq grammar that cannot be used as identifiers (even when starting Coq with the `-noinit` command-line flag):

    _ Axiom CoFixpoint Definition Fixpoint Hypothesis Parameter Prop
    SProp Set Theorem Type Variable as at cofix else end
    fix for forall fun if in let match return then where with

The following are keywords defined in notations or plugins loaded in the [prelude](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#term-prelude):

    by exists exists2 using

Note that loading additional modules or plugins may expand the set of reserved keywords.

[`Print Keywords`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Keywords) can be used to print the current keywords and tokens.

Other tokens  
The following character sequences are tokens defined in the main Coq grammar (even when starting Coq with the `-noinit` command-line flag):

    ! #[ % & ' ( () ) * + , - ->
    . .( .. ... / : ::= := :> ; < <+ <- <:
    <<: <= = => > >-> >= ? @ @{ [ ] _
    `( `{ { {| | }

The following character sequences are tokens defined in notations or plugins loaded in the [prelude](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#term-prelude):

    ** |- || ->

Note that loading additional modules or plugins may expand the set of defined tokens.

> When multiple tokens match the beginning of a sequence of characters, the longest matching token not cutting a subsequence of contiguous letters in the middle is used. Occasionally you may need to insert spaces to separate tokens. For example, if `~` and `~~` are both defined as tokens, the inputs `~ ~` and `~~` generate different tokens, whereas if `~~` is not defined, then the two inputs are equivalent. Also, if `~` and `~_h` are both defined as tokens, the input `~_ho` is interpreted as `~ _ho` rather than `~_h o` so as not to cut the identifier-like subsequence `ho`. Contrastingly, if only `~_h` is defined as a token, then `~_ho` is an error because no token can be found that includes the whole subsequence `ho` without cutting it in the middle. Finally, if all of `~`, `~_h` and `~_ho` are defined as tokens, the input `~_ho` is interpreted using the longest match rule, i.e. as the token `~_ho`.

## Essential vocabulary

This section presents the most essential notions to understand the rest of the Coq manual: [terms](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-term) and [types](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-type) on the one hand, [commands](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-command) and [tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic) on the other hand.

term  
Terms are the basic expressions of Coq. Terms can represent mathematical expressions, propositions and proofs, but also executable programs and program types.

Here is the top-level syntax of terms. Each of the listed constructs is presented in a dedicated section. Some of these constructs (like [`term_forall_or_fun`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-term_forall_or_fun)) are part of the core language that the kernel of Coq understands and are therefore described in [this chapter](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/index.html#core-language), while others (like [`term_if`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/match.html#grammar-token-term_if)) are language extensions that are presented in [the next chapter](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/index.html#extensions).

``` ebnf
term                     ::=     term100
term100                  ::=     term_cast
                         |       term10
term10                   ::=     term_application
                         |       term_forall_or_fun
                         |       term_let
                         |       term_fix
                         |       term_cofix
                         |       term_if
                         |       one_term
one_term                 ::=     term_explicit
                         |       term1
term1                    ::=     term_projection
                         |       term_scope
                         |       term0
term0                    ::=     qualid_annotated
                         |       sort
                         |       number_or_string
                         |       term_evar
                         |       term_match
                         |       term_record
                         |       term_generalizing
                         |       [ | term * ; | term : type ? | ] univ_annot ?
                         |       term_ltac
                         |       ( term )
qualid_annotated         ::=     qualid univ_annot ?
```

Note

Many [commands](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-command) and [tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic) use [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (in the syntax of their arguments) rather than [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). The former need to be enclosed in parentheses unless they're very simple, such as a single identifier. This avoids confusing a space-separated list of terms or identifiers with a [`term_application`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-term_application).

type  
To be valid and accepted by the Coq kernel, a term needs an associated type. We express this relationship by “\\x\\ *of type* \\T\\”, which we write as “\\x:T\\”. Informally, “\\x:T\\” can be thought as “\\x\\ *belongs to* \\T\\”.

The Coq kernel is a type checker: it verifies that a term has the expected type by applying a set of typing rules (see [Typing rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/cic.html#id6)). If that's indeed the case, we say that the term is well-typed.

A special feature of the Coq language is that types can depend on terms (we say that the language is [dependently-typed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependent_type)). Because of this, types and terms share a common syntax. All types are [terms](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-term), but not all terms are types. The syntactic aliases [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) and [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) are used to make clear when the provided [term](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-term) must semantically be a type:

``` ebnf
type                     ::=     term
one_type                 ::=     one_term
```

Intuitively, types may be viewed as sets containing terms. We say that a type is inhabited if it contains at least one term (i.e. if we can find a term which is associated with this type). We call such terms inhabitants. Note that deciding whether a type is inhabited is [undecidable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undecidable_problem).

Formally, types can be used to construct logical foundations for mathematics alternative to the standard ["set theory"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_theory): we call such logical foundations ["type theories"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_theory). Coq is based on the Calculus of Inductive Constructions, which is a particular instance of type theory.

sentence  
Coq documents are made of a series of sentences that contain [commands](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-command) or [tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic), generally terminated with a period and optionally decorated with [attributes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-attribute).

``` ebnf
document                 ::=     sentence *
sentence                 ::=     attributes ? command .
                         |       attributes ? natural : ? query_command .
                         |       attributes ? toplevel_selector : ? ltac_expr .  ...
                         |       control_command
```

[`ltac_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr) syntax supports both simple and compound [tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic). For example: `split` is a simple tactic while `split; auto` combines two simple tactics.

command  
A `command` can be used to modify the state of a Coq document, for instance by declaring a new object, or to get information about the current state.

By convention, command names begin with uppercase letters. Commands appear in the HTML documentation in blue or gray boxes after the label "Command". In the pdf, they appear after the boldface label "Command:". Commands are listed in the [Command index](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/coq-cmdindex.html#command-index). Example:

*Command* `Comments one_termstringnatural*`  
Prints "Comments ok" and does not change the state of the document.

tactic  
A `tactic` specifies how to transform the current proof state as a step in creating a proof. They are syntactically valid only when Coq is in [proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-proof-mode), such as after a [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) command and before any subsequent proof-terminating command such as [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed). See [Proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#proofhandling) for more on proof mode.

By convention, tactic names begin with lowercase letters. Tactic appear in the HTML documentation in blue or gray boxes after the label "Tactic". In the pdf, they appear after the boldface label "Tactic:". Tactics are listed in the [Tactic index](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/coq-tacindex.html#tactic-index).

## Settings

There are several mechanisms for changing the behavior of Coq. The [attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-attribute) mechanism is used to modify the default behavior of a [sentence](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-sentence) or to attach information to Coq objects. The [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag), [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) and [table](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-table) mechanisms are used to modify the behavior of Coq more globally in a document or project.

### Attributes

An attribute is used to modify the default behavior of a sentence or to attach information to a Coq object. Syntactically, most commands and tactics can be decorated with attributes (cf. [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence)), but attributes not supported by the command or tactic will trigger [`This command does not support this attribute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:warn.This-command-does-not-support-this-attribute). There is also a command [`Attributes`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Attributes) to assign attributes to a whole document.

``` ebnf
attributes               ::=     #[ attribute * , ] * legacy_attr *
attribute                ::=     ident attr_value ?
attr_value               ::=     = string
                         |       = ident
                         |       ( attribute + , )
legacy_attr              ::=     Local  Global
                         |       Polymorphic  Monomorphic
                         |       Cumulative  NonCumulative
                         |       Private
                         |       Program
```

The order of top-level attributes doesn't affect their meaning. `#[foo,bar]`, `#[bar,foo]`, `#[foo]#[bar]` and `#[bar]#[foo]` are equivalent.

Boolean attributes take the form [`ident`<sub>`attr`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`= yesno?`. When the `yesno` value is omitted, the default is `yes`.

The legacy attributes ([`legacy_attr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-legacy_attr)) provide an older, alternate syntax for certain attributes. They are equivalent to new attributes as follows:

| Legacy attribute | New attribute |
|----|----|
| `Local` | [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) |
| `Global` | [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) |
| `Polymorphic`, `Monomorphic` | [`universes(polymorphic)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#coq:attr.universes(polymorphic)) |
| `Cumulative`, `NonCumulative` | [`universes(cumulative)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#coq:attr.universes(cumulative)) |
| `Private` | [`private(matching)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/variants.html#coq:attr.private(matching)) |
| `Program` | [`program`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/program.html#coq:attr.program) |

Attributes appear in the HTML documentation in blue or gray boxes after the label "Attribute". In the pdf, they appear after the boldface label "Attribute:". Attributes are listed in the [Attribute index](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/coq-attrindex.html#attribute-index).

*Warning* `This command does not support this attribute: ident.`  
This warning is configured to behave as an error by default. You may turn it into a normal warning by using the [`Warnings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Warnings) option:

``` coq
Set Warnings "unsupported-attributes".
Toplevel input, characters 3-6:
> #[ foo ] Comments.
>    ^^^
Warning: This command does not support this attribute: foo.
[unsupported-attributes,parsing,default]
```

#### Generic attributes

The following attribute is supported by every command:

*Attribute* `warnings = string`  
Sets the given warning string locally for the command. After the command finishes the warning state is reset to what it was before the command. For instance if the current warning state is `some-warnings,-other-warning`,

``` coq
#[warnings="+other-warning"] Command.
```

is equivalent to

``` coq
Set Warnings "+other-warning".
Command.
Set Warnings "some-warnings,-other-warning".
```

and `other-warning` is an error while executing the command.

Consequently, using this attribute around an [`Import`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:cmd.Import) command will prevent it from changing the warning state.

See also [`Warnings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Warnings) for the concrete syntax to use inside the quoted string.

<!-- -->

*Attribute* `warning = string`  
Alias of [`warnings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:attr.warnings).

#### Document-level attributes

*Command* `Attributes attribute+,`  
Associates attributes with the document. When compiled with `coqc` (see Section [Coq commands](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/practical-tools/coq-commands.html#thecoqcommands)), the attributes are associated with the compiled file and may have an effect when the file is loaded with [`Require`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Require). Supported attributes include [`deprecated`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/writing.html#coq:attr.deprecated).

### Flags, Options and Tables

The following types of settings can be used to change the behavior of Coq in subsequent commands and tactics (see [Locality attributes supported by Set and Unset](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#set-unset-scope-qualifiers) for a more precise description of the scope of these settings):

- A flag has a boolean value, such as [`Universe Polymorphism`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#coq:flag.Universe-Polymorphism).

- An option generally has a numeric or string value, such as [`Firstorder Depth`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/logic.html#coq:opt.Firstorder-Depth).

- A table contains a set of [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string)s or [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)s.

- In addition, some commands provide settings, such as [`Extraction Language`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/extraction.html#coq:cmd.Extraction-Language).

``` ebnf
setting_name             ::=     ident +
```

> Flags, options and tables are identified by a series of identifiers. By convention, each of the identifiers start with an initial capital letter.

Flags, options and tables appear in the HTML documentation in blue or gray boxes after the labels "Flag", "Option" and "Table". In the pdf, they appear after a boldface label. They are listed in the [Flags, options and tables index](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/coq-optindex.html#options-index).

*Command* `Set setting_name integerstring?`  
If [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is a flag, no value may be provided; the flag is set to on. If [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is an option, a value of the appropriate type must be provided; the option is set to the specified value.

This command supports the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local), [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) and [`export`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.export) attributes. They are described [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#set-unset-scope-qualifiers).

*Warning* `There is no flag or option with this name: "setting_name".`  
This warning message can be raised by [`Set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Set) and [`Unset`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Unset) when [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is unknown. It is a warning rather than an error because this helps library authors produce Coq code that is compatible with several Coq versions. To preserve the same behavior, they may need to set some compatibility flags or options that did not exist in previous Coq versions.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Unset setting_name`  
If [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is a flag, it is set to off. If [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is an option, it is set to its default value.

This command supports the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local), [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) and [`export`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.export) attributes. They are described [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#set-unset-scope-qualifiers).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Add setting_name qualidstring+`  
Adds the specified values to the table [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Remove setting_name qualidstring+`  
Removes the specified value from the table [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Test setting_name for qualidstring+?`  
If [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is a flag or option, prints its current value. If [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is a table: if the `for` clause is specified, reports whether the table contains each specified value, otherwise this is equivalent to [`Print Table`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Print-Table). The `for` clause is not valid for flags and options.

*Error* `There is no flag, option or table with this name: "setting_name".`  
This error message is raised when calling the [`Test`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Test) command (without the `for` clause), or the [`Print Table`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Print-Table) command, for an unknown [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name).

*Error* `There is no qualid-valued table with this name: "setting_name".`\
*Error* `There is no string-valued table with this name: "setting_name".`  
These error messages are raised when calling the [`Add`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Add) or [`Remove`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Remove) commands, or the [`Test`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Test) command with the `for` clause, if [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name) is unknown or does not have the right type.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Options`  
Prints the current value of all flags and options, and the names of all tables.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Table setting_name`  
Prints the values in the table [`setting_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-setting_name).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Tables`  
A synonym for [`Print Options`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Print-Options).

#### Locality attributes supported by [`Set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Set) and [`Unset`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Unset)

The [`Set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Set) and [`Unset`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Unset) commands support the mutually exclusive [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local), [`export`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.export) and [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) locality attributes.

If no attribute is specified, the original value of the flag or option is restored at the end of the current module but it is *not* restored at the end of the current section.

Newly opened modules and sections inherit the current settings.

Note

We discourage using the [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) locality attribute with the [`Set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Set) and [`Unset`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Unset) commands. If your goal is to define project-wide settings, you should rather use the command-line arguments `-set` and `-unset` for setting flags and options (see [Command line options](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/practical-tools/coq-commands.html#command-line-options)).

# Sorts

``` ebnf
sort                     ::=     Set
                         |       Prop
                         |       SProp
                         |       Type
                         |       Type @{ _ }
                         |       Type @{ qualid | ? universe }
universe                 ::=     max ( universe_expr + , )
                         |       universe_expr
universe_expr            ::=     universe_name + natural ?
```

The types of types are called sorts.

All sorts have a type and there is an infinite well-founded typing hierarchy of sorts whose base sorts are \\\SProp\\, \\\Prop\\ and \\\Set\\.

The sort \\\Prop\\ intends to be the type of logical propositions. If \\M\\ is a logical proposition then it denotes the class of terms representing proofs of \\M\\. An object \\m\\ belonging to \\M\\ witnesses the fact that \\M\\ is provable. An object of type \\\Prop\\ is called a proposition. We denote propositions by [`form`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#grammar-token-form). This constitutes a semantic subclass of the syntactic class [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

The sort \\\SProp\\ is like \\\Prop\\ but the propositions in \\\SProp\\ are known to have irrelevant proofs (all proofs are equal). Objects of type \\\SProp\\ are called strict propositions. See [SProp (proof irrelevant propositions)](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/sprop.html#sprop) for information about using \\\SProp\\, and [\[GCST19\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#gilbert-popl2019) for meta theoretical considerations.

The sort \\\Set\\ intends to be the type of small sets. This includes data types such as booleans and naturals, but also products, subsets, and function types over these data types. We denote specifications (program types) by [`specif`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#grammar-token-specif). This constitutes a semantic subclass of the syntactic class [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

\\\SProp\\, \\\Prop\\ and \\\Set\\ themselves can be manipulated as ordinary terms. Consequently they also have a type. Because assuming simply that \\\Set\\ has type \\\Set\\ leads to an inconsistent theory [\[Coq86\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#coq86), the language of CIC has infinitely many sorts. There are, in addition to the base sorts, a hierarchy of universes \\\Type(i)\\ for any integer \\i ≥ 1\\.

Like \\\Set\\, all of the sorts \\\Type(i)\\ contain small sets such as booleans, natural numbers, as well as products, subsets and function types over small sets. But, unlike \\\Set\\, they also contain large sets, namely the sorts \\\Set\\ and \\\Type(j)\\ for \\j\<i\\, and all products, subsets and function types over these sorts.

Formally, we call \\\Sort\\ the set of sorts which is defined by:

\\\Sort \equiv \\\SProp,\Prop,\Set,\Type(i)\\\|\\ i~∈ ℕ\\\\

Their properties, such as \\\Prop:\Type(1)\\, \\\Set:\Type(1)\\, and \\\Type(i):\Type(i+1)\\, are described in [Subtyping rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/cic.html#subtyping-rules).

**Algebraic universes** In practice, the Type hierarchy is implemented using algebraic universes, which appear in the syntax `Type@{`[`universe`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sorts.html#grammar-token-universe)`}`. An algebraic universe \\u\\ is either a variable, a successor of an algebraic universe (an expression \\u+1\\), an upper bound of algebraic universes (an expression \\\max(u_1 ,...,u_n )\\), or the base universe \\\Set\\.

A graph of constraints between the universe variables is maintained globally. To ensure the existence of a mapping of the universes to the positive integers, the graph of constraints must remain acyclic. Typing expressions that violate the acyclicity of the graph of constraints results in a [`Universe inconsistency`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#coq:exn.Universe-inconsistency) error.

The user does not have to mention explicitly the universe \\u\\ when referring to the universe `Type@{u}`. One only writes `Type`. The system itself generates for each instance of `Type` a new variable for the universe and checks that the constraints between these indexes can be solved. From the user point of view we consequently have \\\Type:\Type\\. We shall make precise in the typing rules the constraints between the indices.

The syntax `Type@{`[`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` | `[`universe`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sorts.html#grammar-token-universe)`}` is used with [Polymorphic Universes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#polymorphicuniverses) when quantifying over all sorts including \\\Prop\\ and \\\SProp\\.

See also

[Printing universes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#printing-universes), [Explicit Universes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#explicit-universes).

# Functions and assumptions

## Binders

``` ebnf
open_binders             ::=     name + : type
                         |       binder +
name                     ::=     _
                         |       ident
binder                   ::=     name
                         |       ( name + : type )
                         |       ( name : type ? := term )
                         |       implicit_binders
                         |       generalizing_binder
                         |       ( name : type | term )
                         |       ' pattern0
```

Various constructions such as `fun`, `forall`, `fix` and `cofix` *bind* variables. A binding is represented by an identifier. If the binding variable is not used in the expression, the identifier can be replaced by the symbol `_`. When the type of a bound variable cannot be synthesized by the system, it can be specified with the notation `(`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)`)`. There is also a notation for a sequence of binding variables sharing the same type: `(`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+ : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)`)`. A binder can also be any pattern prefixed by a quote, e.g. `'(x,y)`.

Some constructions allow the binding of a variable to value. This is called a “let-binder”. The entry [`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder) of the grammar accepts either an assumption binder as defined above or a let-binder. The notation in the latter case is `(`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)`. In a let-binder, only one variable can be introduced at the same time. It is also possible to give the type of the variable as follows: `(`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)`.

Lists of [`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)s are allowed. In the case of `fun` and `forall`, it is intended that at least one binder of the list is an assumption otherwise fun and forall gets identical. Moreover, parentheses can be omitted in the case of a single sequence of bindings sharing the same type (e.g.: `fun (x y z : A) => t` can be shortened in `fun x y z : A => t`).

## Functions (fun) and function types (forall)

``` ebnf
term_forall_or_fun       ::=     forall open_binders , type
                         |       fun open_binders => term
```

The expression `fun `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` => `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) defines the *abstraction* of the variable [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), of type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type), over the term [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). It denotes a function of the variable [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) that evaluates to the expression [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) (e.g. `fun x : A => x` denotes the identity function on type `A`). The keyword `fun` can be followed by several binders as given in Section [Binders](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#binders). Functions over several variables are equivalent to an iteration of one-variable functions. For instance the expression `fun `[`ident`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+ : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` => `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) denotes the same function as `fun `[`ident`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` =>+ `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). If a let-binder occurs in the list of binders, it is expanded to a let-in definition (see Section [Let-in definitions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#let-in)).

The expression `forall `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)`, `[`type`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) denotes the product type (or *product*) of the variable [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) of type [`type`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) over the type [`type`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type). If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is used in [`type`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type), then we say the expression is a dependent product, and otherwise a non-dependent product.

The intention behind a dependent product `forall x : A, B` is twofold. It denotes either the universal quantification of the variable `x` of type `A` in the proposition `B` or the functional dependent product from `A` to `B` (a construction usually written \\\Pi\_{x:A}.B\\ in set theory).

Non-dependent product types have a special notation: `A -> B` stands for `forall _ : A, B`. *Non-dependent product* is used to denote both propositional implication and function types.

These terms are also useful:

- `n : nat` is a dependent premise of `forall n:nat, n + 0 = n` because `n` appears both in the binder of the `forall` and in the quantified statement `n + 0 = n`. Note that if `n` isn't used in the statement, Coq considers it a non-dependent premise. Similarly, `let n := ... in `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is a dependent premise only if `n` is used in [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

- `A` and `B` are non-dependent premises (or, often, just "premises") of `A -> B -> C` because they don't appear in a `forall` binder. `C` is the *conclusion* of the type, which is a second meaning for the term [conclusion](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-conclusion). (As noted, `A -> B` is notation for the term `forall _ : A, B`; the wildcard `_` can't be referred to in the quantified statement.)

As for abstractions, `forall` is followed by a binder list, and products over several variables are equivalent to an iteration of one-variable products.

## Function application

``` ebnf
term_application         ::=     term1 arg +
                         |       @ qualid_annotated term1 +
arg                      ::=     ( ident := term )
                         |       ( natural := term )
                         |       term1
```

[`term1`<sub>`fun`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1)` `[`term1`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1) denotes applying the function [`term1`<sub>`fun`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1) to [`term1`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1).

[`term1`<sub>`fun`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1)` `[`term1`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1)`+` denotes applying [`term1`<sub>`fun`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1) to the arguments [`term1`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1). It is equivalent to `( … ( `[`term1`<sub>`fun`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1)` `[`term1`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1)` ) … ) `[`term1`<sub>`n`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1): associativity is to the left.

The `@ `[`qualid_annotated`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-qualid_annotated)` `[`term1`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term1)`+` form requires specifying all arguments, including implicit ones. Otherwise, implicit arguments need not be given. See [Implicit arguments](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/implicit-arguments.html#implicitarguments).

The notations `(`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)` and `(`[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)` for arguments are used for making explicit the value of implicit arguments. See [Explicit applications](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/implicit-arguments.html#explicit-applications).

## Assumptions

Assumptions extend the global environment with axioms, parameters, hypotheses or variables. An assumption binds an [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) to a [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type). It is accepted by Coq only if [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) is a correct type in the global environment before the declaration and if [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) was not previously defined in the same module. This [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) is considered to be the type (or specification, or statement) assumed by [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and we say that [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) has type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type).

*Command* `assumption_token Inline ( natural )?? ( assumpt )+assumpt`  
``` ebnf
assumption_token         ::=     Axiom  Axioms
                         |       Conjecture  Conjectures
                         |       Parameter  Parameters
                         |       Hypothesis  Hypotheses
                         |       Variable  Variables
assumpt                  ::=     ident_decl + of_type
ident_decl               ::=     ident univ_decl ?
of_type                  ::=     :  :> type
```

These commands bind one or more [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)(s) to specified [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)(s) as their specifications in the global environment. The fact asserted by [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) (or, equivalently, the existence of an object of this type) is accepted as a postulate. They accept the [`program`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/program.html#coq:attr.program) and [`deprecated`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/writing.html#coq:attr.deprecated) attributes.

[`Axiom`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Axiom), [`Conjecture`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Conjecture), [`Parameter`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Parameter) and their plural forms are equivalent. They can take the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) [attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-attribute), which makes the defined [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s accessible by [`Import`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:cmd.Import) and its variants only through their fully qualified names.

Similarly, [`Hypothesis`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Hypothesis), [`Variable`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Variable) and their plural forms are equivalent. Outside of a section, these are equivalent to `Local Parameter`. Inside a section, the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s defined are only accessible within the section. When the current section is closed, the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)(s) become undefined and every object depending on them will be explicitly parameterized (i.e., the variables are *discharged*). See Section [Sections](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sections.html#section-mechanism).

`:>`  
If specified, [`ident_decl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-ident_decl) is automatically declared as a coercion to the class of its type. See [Implicit Coercions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#coercions).

The `Inline` clause is only relevant inside functors. See [`Module`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:cmd.Module).

Example: Simple assumptions

``` coq
Parameter X Y : Set.
```

*Error* `ident already exists.`  

<!-- -->

*Warning* `ident is declared as a local axiom`  
Warning generated when using [`Variable`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Variable) or its equivalent instead of `Local Parameter` or its equivalent.

Note

We advise using the commands [`Axiom`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Axiom), [`Conjecture`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Conjecture) and [`Hypothesis`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Hypothesis) (and their plural forms) for logical postulates (i.e. when the assertion [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) is of sort `Prop`), and to use the commands [`Parameter`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Parameter) and [`Variable`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Variable) (and their plural forms) in other cases (corresponding to the declaration of an abstract object of the given type).

# Definitions

## Let-in definitions

``` ebnf
term_let                 ::=     let name : type ? := term in term
                         |       let name binder + : type ? := term in term
                         |       destructuring_let
```

`let `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` in `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) represents the local binding of the variable [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) to the value [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) in [`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

`let `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` `[`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)`+ := `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` in `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is an abbreviation for `let `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := fun `[`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)`+ => `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` in `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

See also

Extensions of the `let ... in ...` syntax are described in [Irrefutable patterns: the destructuring let variants](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/match.html#irrefutable-patterns).

## Type cast

``` ebnf
term_cast                ::=     term10 : type
                         |       term10 <: type
                         |       term10 <<: type
                         |       term10 :> type
```

The expression [`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) is a type cast expression. It enforces the type of [`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10) to be [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type).

[`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10)` <: `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) specifies that the virtual machine will be used to type check that [`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10) has type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) (see [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute)).

[`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10)` <<: `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) specifies that compilation to OCaml will be used to type check that [`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10) has type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) (see [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute)).

[`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10)` :> `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) enforces the type of [`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10) to be [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) without leaving a trace in the produced value. This is a volatile cast.

If a scope is [bound](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#localinterpretationrulesfornotations) to [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) then [`term10`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term10) is interpreted in that scope.

## Top-level definitions

Definitions extend the global environment by associating names to terms. A definition can be seen as a way to give a meaning to a name or as a way to abbreviate a term. In any case, the name can later be replaced at any time by its definition.

The operation of unfolding a name into its definition is called [delta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-delta-reduction). A definition is accepted by the system if and only if the defined term is well-typed in the current context of the definition and if the name is not already used. The name defined by the definition is called a constant and the term it refers to is its body. A definition has a type, which is the type of its [body](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#term-body).

A formal presentation of constants and environments is given in Section [Typing rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/cic.html#id6).

*Command* `DefinitionExample ident_decl def_body`  
``` ebnf
def_body                 ::=     binder * : type ? := reduce ? term
                         |       binder * : type
reduce                   ::=     Eval red_expr in
```

These commands bind [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) to the name [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the global environment, provided that [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is well-typed. They can take the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) [attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-attribute), which makes the defined [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) accessible by [`Import`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:cmd.Import) and its variants only through their fully qualified names. If [`reduce`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#grammar-token-reduce) is present then [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is bound to the result of the specified computation on [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

These commands also support the [`universes(polymorphic)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/universe-polymorphism.html#coq:attr.universes(polymorphic)), [`program`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/program.html#coq:attr.program) (see [Program Definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/program.html#program-definition)), [`canonical`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/canonical.html#coq:attr.canonical), [`bypass_check(universes)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:attr.bypass_check(universes)), [`bypass_check(guard)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:attr.bypass_check(guard)), [`deprecated`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/writing.html#coq:attr.deprecated) and [`using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:attr.using) attributes.

If [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is omitted, [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) is required and Coq enters proof mode. This can be used to define a term incrementally, in particular by relying on the [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) tactic. In this case, the proof should be terminated with [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined) in order to define a [constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#term-constant) for which the computational behavior is relevant. See [Entering and exiting proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#proof-editing-mode).

The form `Definition `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) checks that the type of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is definitionally equal to [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type), and registers [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) as being of type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type), and bound to value [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

The form `Definition `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` `[`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)`* : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is equivalent to `Definition `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : forall `[`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)`*, `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` := fun `[`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)`* => `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

See also

[`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque), [`Transparent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Transparent), [`unfold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.unfold).

*Error* `ident already exists.`  

*Error* `The term term has type type while it is expected to have type type'.`  

## Assertions and proofs

An assertion states a proposition (or a type) for which the proof (or an inhabitant of the type) is interactively built using [tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic). Assertions cause Coq to enter [proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-proof-mode) (see [Proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#proofhandling)). Common tactics are described in the [Basic proof writing](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/index.html#writing-proofs) chapter. The basic assertion command is:

*Command* `thm_token ident_decl binder* : type with ident_decl binder* : type*`  
``` ebnf
thm_token                ::=     Theorem
                         |       Lemma
                         |       Fact
                         |       Remark
                         |       Corollary
                         |       Proposition
                         |       Property
```

After the statement is asserted, Coq needs a proof. Once a proof of [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) under the assumptions represented by [`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)s is given and validated, the proof is generalized into a proof of `forall `[`binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-binder)`*, `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) and the theorem is bound to the name [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the global environment.

These commands accept the [`program`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/program.html#coq:attr.program) attribute. See [Program Lemma](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/program.html#program-lemma).

Forms using the `with` clause are useful for theorems that are proved by simultaneous induction over a mutually inductive assumption, or that assert mutually dependent statements in some mutual coinductive type. It is equivalent to [`Fixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#coq:cmd.Fixpoint) or [`CoFixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/coinductive.html#coq:cmd.CoFixpoint) but using tactics to build the proof of the statements (or the [body](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#term-body) of the specification, depending on the point of view). The inductive or coinductive types on which the induction or coinduction has to be done is assumed to be unambiguous and is guessed by the system.

Like in a [`Fixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#coq:cmd.Fixpoint) or [`CoFixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/coinductive.html#coq:cmd.CoFixpoint) definition, the induction hypotheses have to be used on *structurally smaller* arguments (for a [`Fixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#coq:cmd.Fixpoint)) or be *guarded by a constructor* (for a [`CoFixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/coinductive.html#coq:cmd.CoFixpoint)). The verification that recursive proof arguments are correct is done only at the time of registering the lemma in the global environment. To know if the use of induction hypotheses is correct at some time of the interactive development of a proof, use the command [`Guarded`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Guarded).

This command accepts the [`bypass_check(universes)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:attr.bypass_check(universes)), [`bypass_check(guard)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:attr.bypass_check(guard)), [`deprecated`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/writing.html#coq:attr.deprecated), and [`using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:attr.using) attributes.

*Error* `The term term has type type which should be Set, Prop or Type.`  

*Error* `ident already exists.`  
The name you provided is already defined. You have then to choose another name.

*Error* `Nested proofs are discouraged and not allowed by default. This error probably means that you forgot to close the last "Proof." with "Qed." or "Defined.". If you really intended to use nested proofs, you can do so by turning the "Nested Proofs Allowed" flag on.`  
You are asserting a new statement when you're already in proof mode. This feature, called nested proofs, is disabled by default. To activate it, turn the [`Nested Proofs Allowed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:flag.Nested-Proofs-Allowed) flag on.

Proofs start with the keyword [`Proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof). Then Coq enters the proof mode until the proof is completed. In proof mode, the user primarily enters tactics (see [Basic proof writing](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/index.html#writing-proofs)).
