The level can otherwise be indicated explicitly by using `constr at level n` for some `n`, or `constr at next level`.

Conversely, custom entries can be used to parse sub-expressions of the main grammar, or from another custom entry as is the case in

``` coq
Notation "[ e ]" := e (e custom expr at level 2).
```

to indicate that `e` has to be parsed at level `2` of the grammar associated with the custom entry `expr`. The level can be omitted, as in

``` coq
Notation "[ e ]" := e (e custom expr).
```

in which case Coq infer it. If the sub-expression is at a border of the notation (as e.g. `x` and `y` in `x + y`), the level is determined by the associativity. If the sub-expression is not at the border of the notation (as e.g. `e` in `"[ e ]`), the level is inferred to be the highest level used for the entry. In particular, this level depends on the highest level existing in the entry at the time of use of the notation.

In the absence of an explicit entry for parsing or printing a sub-expression of a notation in a custom entry, the default is to consider that this sub-expression is parsed or printed in the same custom entry where the notation is defined. In particular, if `x at level n` is used for a sub-expression of a notation defined in custom entry `foo`, it shall be understood the same as `x custom foo at level n`.

In general, rules are required to be *productive* on the right-hand side, i.e. that they are bound to an expression which is not reduced to a single variable. If the rule is not productive on the right-hand side, as it is the case above for

``` coq
Notation "( x )" := x (in custom expr at level 0, x at level 2).
```

and

``` coq
Notation "{ x }" := x (in custom expr at level 0, x constr).
```

it is used as a *grammar coercion* which means that it is used to parse or print an expression which is not available in the current grammar at the current level of parsing or printing for this grammar but which is available in another grammar or in another level of the current grammar. For instance,

``` coq
Notation "( x )" := x (in custom expr at level 0, x at level 2).
```

tells that parentheses can be inserted to parse or print an expression declared at level `2` of `expr` whenever this expression is expected to be used as a subterm at level 0 or 1. This allows for instance to parse and print `Add x y` as a subterm of `Mul (Add x y) z` using the syntax `(x + y) z`. Similarly,

``` coq
Notation "{ x }" := x (in custom expr at level 0, x constr).
```

gives a way to let any arbitrary expression which is not handled by the custom entry `expr` be parsed or printed by the main grammar of term up to the insertion of a pair of curly brackets.

Another special situation is when parsing global references or identifiers. To indicate that a custom entry should parse identifiers, use the following form:

``` coq
Notation "x" := x (in custom expr at level 0, x ident).
```

Similarly, to indicate that a custom entry should parse global references (i.e. qualified or unqualified identifiers), use the following form:

``` coq
Notation "x" := x (in custom expr at level 0, x global).
```

*Command* `Print Custom Grammar ident`  
This displays the state of the grammar for terms associated with the custom entry [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

### Syntax

Here are the syntax elements used by the various notation commands.

> ``` ebnf
> syntax_modifier          ::=     at level natural
>                          |       in custom ident at level natural ?
>                          |       ident + , at level  in scope ident
>                          |       ident at level binder_interp ?
>                          |       ident explicit_subentry
>                          |       ident binder_interp
>                          |       left associativity
>                          |       right associativity
>                          |       no associativity
>                          |       only parsing
>                          |       format string
>                          |       only printing
> explicit_subentry        ::=     ident
>                          |       name
>                          |       global
>                          |       bigint
>                          |       strict pattern at level natural ?
>                          |       binder
>                          |       closed binder
>                          |       constr at level ? binder_interp ?
>                          |       custom ident at level ? binder_interp ?
>                          |       pattern at level natural ?
> binder_interp            ::=     as ident
>                          |       as name
>                          |       as pattern
>                          |       as strict pattern
> level                    ::=     level natural
>                          |       next level
> ```

Note that `_` by itself is a valid [`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name) but is not a valid [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

Note

No typing of the denoted expression is performed at definition time. Type checking is done only at the time of use of the notation.

Note

Some examples of Notation may be found in the files composing the initial state of Coq (see directory `$COQLIB/theories/Init`).

Note

The notation `"{ x }"` has a special status in the main grammars of terms and patterns so that complex notations of the form `"x + { y }"` or `"x * { y }"` can be nested with correct precedences. Especially, every notation involving a pattern of the form `"{ x }"` is parsed as a notation where the pattern `"{ x }"` has been simply replaced by `"x"` and the curly braces are parsed separately. E.g. `"y + { z }"` is not parsed as a term of the given form but as a term of the form `"y + z"` where `z` has been parsed using the rule parsing `"{ x }"`. Especially, level and precedences for a rule including patterns of the form `"{ x }"` are relative not to the textual notation but to the notation where the curly braces have been removed (e.g. the level and the associativity given to some notation, say `"{ y } & { z }"` in fact applies to the underlying `"{ x }"`-free rule which is `"y & z"`).

Note

Notations such as `"( p | q )"` (or starting with `"( x | "`, more generally) are deprecated as they conflict with the syntax for nested disjunctive patterns (see [Extended pattern matching](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/match.html#extendedpatternmatching)), and are not honored in pattern expressions.

*Warning* `Use of string Notation is deprecated as it is inconsistent with pattern syntax.`  
This warning is disabled by default to avoid spurious diagnostics due to legacy notation in the Coq standard library. It can be turned on with the `-w disj-pattern-notation` flag.

<!-- -->

*Error* `Unknown custom entry: ident.`  
Occurs when [`Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Notation) or [`Print Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Notation) can't find the custom entry given by the user.

## Notation scopes

A notation scope is a set of notations for terms with their interpretations. Notation scopes provide a weak, purely syntactic form of notation overloading: a symbol may refer to different definitions depending on which notation scopes are currently open. For instance, the infix symbol `+` can be used to refer to distinct definitions of the addition operator, such as for natural numbers, integers or reals. Notation scopes can include an interpretation for numbers and strings with the [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) and [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) commands.

> ``` ebnf
> scope                    ::=     scope_name
>                          |       scope_key
> scope_name               ::=     ident
> scope_key                ::=     ident
> ```

Each notation scope has a single [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name), which by convention ends with the suffix "\_scope", as in "nat_scope". One or more [`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key)s (delimiting keys) may be associated with a notation scope with the [`Delimit Scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Delimit-Scope) command. Most commands use [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name); [`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key)s are used within [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)s.

*Command* `Declare Scope scope_name`  
Declares a new notation scope. Note that the initial state of Coq declares the following notation scopes: `core_scope`, `type_scope`, `function_scope`, `nat_scope`, `bool_scope`, `list_scope`, `dec_int_scope`, `dec_uint_scope`.

Use commands such as [`Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Notation) to add notations to the scope.

<!-- -->

*Error* `Scope names should not start with an underscore.`  
Scope names starting with an underscore would make the `%_` syntax ambiguous.

### Global interpretation rules for notations

At any time, the interpretation of a notation for a term is done within a *stack* of notation scopes and [lonely notations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#term-lonely-notation). If a notation is defined in multiple scopes, Coq uses the interpretation from the most recently opened notation scope or declared lonely notation.

Note that "stack" is a misleading name. Each scope or lonely notation can only appear in the stack once. New items are pushed onto the top of the stack, except that adding a item that's already in the stack moves it to the top of the stack instead. Scopes are removed by name (e.g. by [`Close Scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Close-Scope)) wherever they are in the stack, rather than through "pop" operations.

Use the [`Print Visibility`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Visibility) command to display the current notation scope stack.

*Command* `Open Scope scope`  
Adds a scope to the notation scope stack. If the scope is already present, the command moves it to the top of the stack.

If the command appears in a section: By default, the scope is only added within the section. Specifying [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) marks the scope for export as part of the current module. Specifying [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) behaves like the default.

If the command does not appear in a section: By default, the scope marks the scope for export as part of the current module. Specifying [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) prevents exporting the scope. Specifying [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) behaves like the default.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Close Scope scope`  
Removes a scope from the notation scope stack.

If the command appears in a section: By default, the scope is only removed within the section. Specifying [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) marks the scope removal for export as part of the current module. Specifying [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) behaves like the default.

If the command does not appear in a section: By default, the scope marks the scope removal for export as part of the current module. Specifying [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) prevents exporting the removal. Specifying [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) behaves like the default.

### Local interpretation rules for notations

In addition to the global rules of interpretation of notations, some ways to change the interpretation of subterms are available.

#### Opening a notation scope locally

``` ebnf
term_scope               ::=     term0 % scope_key
                         |       term0 % _ scope_key
```

The notation scope stack can be locally extended within a [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) with the syntax `(`[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)%`[`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key) (or simply [`term0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term0)`%`[`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key) for atomic terms).

In this case, [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is interpreted in the scope stack extended with the scope bound to [`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key).

The term [`term0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term0)`%_`[`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key) is interpreted similarly to [`term0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term0)`%`[`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key) except that the scope stack is only temporarily extended for the head of [`term0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term0), rather than all its subterms.

*Command* `Delimit Scope scope_name with scope_key`  
Binds the delimiting key [`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key) to a scope.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Undelimit Scope scope_name`  
Removes the delimiting keys associated with a scope.

<!-- -->

*Error* `Scope delimiters should not start with an underscore.`  
Scope delimiters starting with an underscore would make the `%_` syntax ambiguous.

The arguments of an [abbreviation](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#abbreviations) can be interpreted in a scope stack locally extended with a given scope by using the modifier [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+, in scope `[`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name).s

#### Binding types or coercion classes to notation scopes

*Command* `Bind Scope scope_name with coercion_class+`  
Binds the notation scope [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name) to the type or coercion class [`coercion_class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#grammar-token-coercion_class). When bound, arguments of that type for any function will be interpreted in that scope by default. This default can be overridden for individual functions with the [`Arguments`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#coq:cmd.Arguments) command. See [Binding arguments to scopes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#binding-to-scope) for details. The association may be convenient when a notation scope is naturally associated with a [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) (e.g. `nat` and the natural numbers).

Whether the argument of a function has some type `type` is determined statically. For instance, if `f` is a polymorphic function of type `forall X:Type, X -> X` and type `t` is bound to a scope `scope`, then `a` of type `t` in `f t a` is not recognized as an argument to be interpreted in scope `scope`.

In explicit [casts](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#type-cast) [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` : `[`coercion_class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#grammar-token-coercion_class), the `term` is interpreted in the [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name) associated with [`coercion_class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#grammar-token-coercion_class).

This command supports the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local), [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global), [`add_top`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:attr.add_top) and [`add_bottom`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:attr.add_bottom) attributes.

*Attribute* `add_top`\
*Attribute* `add_bottom`  
These [attributes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-attribute) allow adding additional bindings at the top or bottom of the stack of already declared bindings. In absence of such attributes, any new binding clears the previous ones. This makes it possible to bind multiple scopes to the same [`coercion_class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#grammar-token-coercion_class).

Example: Binding scopes to a type

Let's declare two scopes with a notation in each and an arbitrary function on type `bool`.

``` coq
Declare Scope T_scope.
```

By default, the argument of `f` is interpreted in the currently opened scopes.

``` coq
Open Scope T_scope.
f true
     : bool
f false
     : bool
```

This can be changed by binding scopes to the type `bool`.

``` coq
Bind Scope T_scope with bool.
f true
     : bool
```

When multiple scopes are attached to a type, notations are interpreted in the first scope containing them, from the top of the stack.

``` coq
#[add_top] Bind Scope F_scope with bool.
f false
     : bool
f (negb false)
     : bool
```

Bindings for functions can be displayed with the [`About`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.About) command.

``` coq
About f.
f : bool -> bool

f is not universe polymorphic
Arguments f _%F_scope%T_scope%bool_scope
Expands to: Constant Top.f
```

Bindings are also used in casts.

``` coq
Close Scope F_scope.
true
     : bool
false : bool
     : bool
```

Note

Such stacks of scopes can be handy to share notations between multiple types. For instance, the scope `T_scope` above could contain many generic notations used for both the `bool` and `nat` types, while the scope `F_scope` could override some of these notations specifically for `bool` and another `F'_scope` could override them specifically for `nat`, which could then be bound to `%F'_scope%T_scope`.

Note

When active, a bound scope has effect on all defined functions (even if they are defined after the [`Bind Scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Bind-Scope) directive), except if argument scopes were assigned explicitly using the [`Arguments`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#coq:cmd.Arguments) command.

Note

The scopes `type_scope` and `function_scope` also have a local effect on interpretation. See the next section.

### The `type_scope` notation scope

The scope `type_scope` has a special status. It is a primitive interpretation scope which is temporarily activated each time a subterm of an expression is expected to be a type. It is delimited by the key `type`, and bound to the coercion class `Sortclass`. It is also used in certain situations where an expression is statically known to be a type, including the conclusion and the type of hypotheses within an Ltac goal match (see [Pattern matching on goals and hypotheses: match goal](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#ltac-match-goal)), the statement of a theorem, the type of a definition, the type of a binder, the domain and codomain of implication, the codomain of products, and more generally any type argument of a declared or defined constant.

### The `function_scope` notation scope

The scope `function_scope` also has a special status. It is temporarily activated each time the argument of a global reference is recognized to be a `Funclass` instance, i.e., of type `forall x:A, B` or `A -> B`.

### Notation scopes used in the standard library of Coq

We give an overview of the scopes used in the standard library of Coq. For a complete list of notations in each scope, use the commands [`Print Scopes`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Scopes) or [`Print Scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Scope).

`type_scope`  
This scope includes infix \* for product types and infix + for sum types. It is delimited by the key `type`, and bound to the coercion class `Sortclass`, as described above.

`function_scope`  
This scope is delimited by the key `function`, and bound to the coercion class `Funclass`, as described above.

`nat_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on type nat. Positive integer numbers in this scope are mapped to their canonical representent built from `O` and `S`. The scope is delimited by the key `nat`, and bound to the type `nat` (see above).

`N_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on type `N` (binary natural numbers). It is delimited by the key `N` and comes with an interpretation for numbers as closed terms of type `N`.

`Z_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on type `Z` (binary integer numbers). It is delimited by the key `Z` and comes with an interpretation for numbers as closed terms of type `Z`.

`positive_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on type `positive` (binary strictly positive numbers). It is delimited by key `positive` and comes with an interpretation for numbers as closed terms of type `positive`.

`Q_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on type `Q` (rational numbers defined as fractions of an integer and a strictly positive integer modulo the equality of the numerator- denominator cross-product) and comes with an interpretation for numbers as closed terms of type `Q`.

`Qc_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on the type `Qc` of rational numbers defined as the type of irreducible fractions of an integer and a strictly positive integer.

`R_scope`  
This scope includes the standard arithmetical operators and relations on type `R` (axiomatic real numbers). It is delimited by the key `R` and comes with an interpretation for numbers using the `IZR` morphism from binary integer numbers to `R` and `Z.pow_pos` for potential exponent parts.

`bool_scope`  
This scope includes notations for the boolean operators. It is delimited by the key `bool`, and bound to the type `bool` (see above).

`list_scope`  
This scope includes notations for the list operators. It is delimited by the key `list`, and bound to the type `list` (see above).

`core_scope`  
This scope includes the notation for pairs. It is delimited by the key `core`.

`string_scope`  
This scope includes notation for strings as elements of the type string. Special characters and escaping follow Coq conventions on strings (see [Lexical conventions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#lexical-conventions)). Especially, there is no convention to visualize non printable characters of a string. The file `String.v` shows an example that contains quotes, a newline and a beep (i.e. the ASCII character of code 7).

`char_scope`  
This scope includes interpretation for all strings of the form `"c"` where `c` is an ASCII character, or of the form `"nnn"` where nnn is a three-digit number (possibly with leading 0s), or of the form `""""`. Their respective denotations are the ASCII code of `c`, the decimal ASCII code `nnn`, or the ascii code of the character `"` (i.e. the ASCII code 34), all of them being represented in the type `ascii`.

### Displaying information about scopes

*Command* `Print Visibility scope_name?`  
Displays the current notation scope stack. The top of the stack is displayed last. Notations in scopes whose interpretation is hidden by the same notation in a more recently opened scope are not displayed. Hence each notation is displayed only once.

If [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name) is specified, displays the current notation scope stack as if the scope [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name) is pushed on top of the stack. This is useful to see how a subterm occurring locally in the scope is interpreted.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Scopes`  
Displays, for each existing notation scope, all accessible notations (whether or not currently in the notation scope stack), the most-recently defined delimiting key and the class the notation scope is bound to. The display also includes [lonely notations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#term-lonely-notation).

Use the [`Print Visibility`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Print-Visibility) command to display the current notation scope stack.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Scope scope_name`  
Displays all notations defined in the notation scope [`scope_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_name). It also displays the delimiting key and the class to which the scope is bound, if any.

## Abbreviations

*Command* `Notation ident identparm* := one_term ( syntax_modifier+, )?`  
Defines an abbreviation [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with the parameters [`ident`<sub>`parm`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

This command supports the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) attribute, which limits the notation to the current module.

An *abbreviation* is a name, possibly applied to arguments, that denotes a (presumably) more complex expression. Here are examples:

``` coq
Notation Nlist := (list nat).

Check 1 :: 2 :: 3 :: nil.
1 :: 2 :: 3 :: nil
     : Nlist

Notation reflexive R := (forall x, R x x).

Check forall A:Prop, A <-> A.
reflexive iff
     : Prop
reflexive iff
     : Prop

Notation Plus1 B := (Nat.add B 1).

Compute (Plus1 3).
     = 4
     : nat
```

An abbreviation expects no precedence nor associativity, since it is parsed as an usual application. Abbreviations are used as much as possible by the Coq printers unless the modifier `(only parsing)` is given.

An abbreviation is bound to an absolute name as an ordinary definition is and it also can be referred to by a qualified name.

Abbreviations are syntactic in the sense that they are bound to expressions which are not typed at the time of the definition of the abbreviation but at the time they are used. Especially, abbreviations can be bound to terms with holes (i.e. with “`_`”). For example:

``` coq
Definition explicit_id (A:Set) (a:A) := a.

Notation id := (explicit_id _).

Check (id 0).
id 0
     : nat
```

Abbreviations disappear when a section is closed. No typing of the denoted expression is performed at definition time. Type checking is done only at the time of use of the abbreviation.

Like for notations, if the right-hand side of an abbreviation is a partially applied constant, the abbreviation inherits the implicit arguments and notation scopes of the constant. As an exception, if the right-hand side is just of the form `@`[`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid), this conventionally stops the inheritance of implicit arguments.

Like for notations, it is possible to bind binders in abbreviations. Here is an example:

``` coq
Definition force2 q (P:nat*nat -> Prop) :=
  (forall n', n' >= fst q -> forall p', p' >= snd q -> P q).
```

## Numbers and strings

``` ebnf
number_or_string         ::=     number
                         |       string
```

Numbers and strings have no predefined semantics in the calculus. They are merely notations that can be bound to objects through the notation mechanism. Initially, numbers are bound to `nat`, Peano’s representation of natural numbers (see [Datatypes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#datatypes)).

Note

Negative integers are not at the same level as [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural), for this would make precedence unnatural.

### Number notations

*Command* `Number Notation qualidtype qualidparse qualidprint ( number_modifier+, )? : scope_name`  
``` ebnf
number_modifier          ::=     warning after bignat
                         |       abstract after bignat
                         |       number_string_via
number_string_via        ::=     via qualid mapping [ qualid => qualid  [ qualid ] => qualid + , ]
```

Customizes the way number literals are parsed and printed within the current [notation scope](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#term-notation-scope).

> [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)  
> the name of an inductive type, while [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) and [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should be the names of the parsing and printing functions, respectively. The parsing function [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should have one of the following types:
>
> > - `Number.int -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Number.int -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Number.uint -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Number.uint -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Z -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Z -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `PrimInt63.pos_neg_int63 -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `PrimInt63.pos_neg_int63 -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `PrimFloat.float -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `PrimFloat.float -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Number.number -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > - `Number.number -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
>
> And the printing function [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should have one of the following types:
>
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> Number.int`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option Number.int`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> Number.uint`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option Number.uint`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> Z`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option Z`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> PrimInt63.pos_neg_int63`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option PrimInt63.pos_neg_int63`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> PrimFloat.float`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option PrimFloat.float`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> Number.number`
> >
> > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option Number.number`
>
> When parsing, the application of the parsing function [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) to the number will be fully reduced, and universes of the resulting term will be refreshed.
>
> Note that only fully-reduced ground terms (terms containing only function application, constructors, inductive type families, sorts, primitive integers, primitive floats, primitive arrays and type constants for primitive types) will be considered for printing.
>
> Note
>
> Instead of an inductive type, [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) can be `PrimInt63.int` or `PrimFloat.float`, in which case [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) takes `PrimInt63.int_wrapper` or `PrimFloat.float_wrapper` as input instead of `PrimInt63.int` or `PrimFloat.float`. See below for an [example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#example-number-notation-primitive-int).
>
> Note
>
> When `PrimFloat.float` is used as input type of [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid), only numerical values will be parsed this way, (no infinities nor NaN). Similarly, printers [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) with output type `PrimFloat.float` or `option PrimFloat.float` are ignored when they return non numerical values.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> `via `[`qualid`<sub>`ind`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` mapping [ `[`qualid`<sub>`constant`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` => `[`qualid`<sub>`constructor`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)`+, ]`  
> When using this option, [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) no longer needs to be an inductive type and is instead mapped to the inductive type [`qualid`<sub>`ind`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) according to the provided list of pairs, whose first component [`qualid`<sub>`constant`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) is a constant of type [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) (or a function of type `_ ->* `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)) and the second a constructor of type [`qualid`<sub>`ind`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid). The type [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) is then replaced by [`qualid`<sub>`ind`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) in the above parser and printer types.
>
> When [`qualid`<sub>`constant`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) is surrounded by square brackets, all the implicit arguments of [`qualid`<sub>`constant`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) (whether maximally inserted or not) are ignored when translating to [`qualid`<sub>`constructor`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) (i.e., before applying [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)) and replaced with implicit argument holes `_` when translating from [`qualid`<sub>`constructor`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) to [`qualid`<sub>`constant`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) (after [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)). See below for an [example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#example-number-notation-implicit-args).
>
> Note
>
> The implicit status of the arguments is considered only at notation declaration time, any further modification of this status has no impact on the previously declared notations.
>
> Note
>
> In case of multiple implicit options (for instance `Arguments eq_refl {A}%_type_scope {x}, [_] _`), an argument is considered implicit when it is implicit in any of the options.
>
> Note
>
> To use a [`sort`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sorts.html#grammar-token-sort) as the target type [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid), use an [abbreviation](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#abbreviations) as in the [example below](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#example-number-notation-non-inductive).
>
> `warning after `[`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat)  
> displays a warning message about a possible stack overflow when calling [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) to parse a literal larger than [`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat).
>
> *Warning* `Stack overflow or segmentation fault happens when working with large numbers in type (threshold may vary depending on your system limits and on the command executed).`  
> When a [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) is registered in the current scope with `(warning after `[`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat)`)`, this warning is emitted when parsing a number greater than or equal to [`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat).
>
> `abstract after `[`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat)  
> returns `(`[`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` m)` when parsing a literal `m` that's greater than [`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat) rather than reducing it to a normal form. Here `m` will be a `Number.int`, `Number.uint`, `Z` or `Number.number`, depending on the type of the parsing function [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid). This allows for a more compact representation of literals in types such as `nat`, and limits parse failures due to stack overflow. Note that a warning will be emitted when an integer larger than [`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat) is parsed. Note that `(abstract after `[`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat)`)` has no effect when [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) lands in an `option` type.
>
> *Warning* `To avoid stack overflow, large numbers in type are interpreted as applications of qualidparse.`  
> When a [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) is registered in the current scope with `(abstract after `[`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat)`)`, this warning is emitted when parsing a number greater than or equal to [`bignat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-bignat). Typically, this indicates that the fully computed representation of numbers can be so large that non-tail-recursive OCaml functions run out of stack space when trying to walk them.
>
> *Warning* `The 'abstract after' directive has no effect when the parsing function (qualidparse) targets an option type.`  
> As noted above, the `(abstract after `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`)` directive has no effect when [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) lands in an `option` type.
>
> *Error* `'via' and 'abstract' cannot be used together.`  
> With the `abstract after` option, the parser function [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) does not reduce large numbers to a normal form, which prevents doing the translation given in the `mapping` list.

*Error* `Cannot interpret this number as a value of type type`  
The number notation registered for [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) does not support the given number. This error is given when the interpretation function returns `None`, or if the interpretation is registered only for integers or non-negative integers, and the given number has a fractional or exponent part or is negative.

*Error* `overflow in int63 literal bigint`  
The constant's absolute value is too big to fit into a 63-bit integer `PrimInt63.int`.

*Error* `qualidparse should go from Number.int to type or (option type). Instead of Number.int, the types Number.uint or Z or PrimInt63.pos_neg_int63 or PrimFloat.float or Number.number could be used (you may need to require BinNums or Number or PrimInt63 or PrimFloat first).`  
The parsing function given to the [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) command is not of the right type.

*Error* `qualidprint should go from type to Number.int or (option Number.int). Instead of Number.int, the types Number.uint or Z or PrimInt63.pos_neg_int63 or Number.number could be used (you may need to require BinNums or Number or PrimInt63 first).`  
The printing function given to the [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) command is not of the right type.

*Error* `Unexpected term term while parsing a number notation.`  
Parsing functions must always return ground terms, made up of function application, constructors, inductive type families, sorts and primitive integers. Parsing functions may not return terms containing axioms, bare (co)fixpoints, lambdas, etc.

*Error* `Unexpected non-option term term while parsing a number notation.`  
Parsing functions expected to return an `option` must always return a concrete `Some` or `None` when applied to a concrete number expressed as a (hexa)decimal. They may not return opaque constants.

*Error* `Multiple 'via' options.`  
At most one `via` option can be given.

*Error* `Multiple 'warning after' or 'abstract after' options.`  
At most one `warning after` or `abstract after` option can be given.

### String notations

*Command* `String Notation qualidtype qualidparse qualidprint ( number_string_via )? : scope_name`  
> Allows the user to customize how strings are parsed and printed.
>
> > [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)  
> > the name of an inductive type, while [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) and [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should be the names of the parsing and printing functions, respectively. The parsing function [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should have one of the following types:
> >
> > > - `Byte.byte -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> > >
> > > - `Byte.byte -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> > >
> > > - `list Byte.byte -> `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> > >
> > > - `list Byte.byte -> option `[`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)
> >
> > The printing function [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should have one of the following types:
> >
> > > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> Byte.byte`
> > >
> > > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option Byte.byte`
> > >
> > > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> list Byte.byte`
> > >
> > > - [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` -> option (list Byte.byte)`
> >
> > When parsing, the application of the parsing function [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) to the string will be fully reduced, and universes of the resulting term will be refreshed.
> >
> > Note that only fully-reduced ground terms (terms containing only function application, constructors, inductive type families, sorts, primitive integers, primitive floats, primitive arrays and type constants for primitive types) will be considered for printing.
> >
> > `via `[`qualid`<sub>`ind`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` mapping [ `[`qualid`<sub>`constant`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)` => `[`qualid`<sub>`constructor`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)`+, ]`  
> > works as for [number notations above](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#number-string-via).

*Error* `Cannot interpret this string as a value of type type`  
> The string notation registered for [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) does not support the given string. This error is given when the interpretation function returns `None`.

*Error* `qualidparse should go from Byte.byte or (list Byte.byte) to type or (option type).`  
The parsing function given to the [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) command is not of the right type.

*Error* `qualidprint should go from type to Byte.byte or (option Byte.byte) or (list Byte.byte) or (option (list Byte.byte)).`  
The printing function given to the [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) command is not of the right type.

*Error* `Unexpected term term while parsing a string notation.`  
Parsing functions must always return ground terms, made up of function application, constructors, inductive type families, sorts and primitive integers. Parsing functions may not return terms containing axioms, bare (co)fixpoints, lambdas, etc.

*Error* `Unexpected non-option term term while parsing a string notation.`  
Parsing functions expected to return an `option` must always return a concrete `Some` or `None` when applied to a concrete string expressed as a decimal. They may not return opaque constants.

Note

Number or string notations for parameterized inductive types can be added by declaring an [abbreviation](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#abbreviations) for the inductive which instantiates all parameters. See [example below](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#example-string-notation-parameterized-inductive).

The following errors apply to both string and number notations:

> *Error* `type is not an inductive type.`  
> String and number notations can only be declared for inductive types. Declare string or numeral notations for non-inductive types using [`number_string_via`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-number_string_via).
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `qualid was already mapped to qualid and cannot be remapped to qualid`  
> Duplicates are not allowed in the `mapping` list.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Missing mapping for constructor qualid`  
> A mapping should be provided for [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) in the `mapping` list.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Warning* `type was already mapped to type, mapping it also to type might yield ill typed terms when using the notation.`  
> Two pairs in the `mapping` list associate types that might be incompatible.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Warning* `Type of qualid seems incompatible with the type of qualid. Expected type is: type instead of type. This might yield ill typed terms when using the notation.`  
> A mapping given in the `mapping` list associates a constant with a seemingly incompatible constructor.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Cannot interpret in scope_name because qualid could not be found in the current environment.`  
> The inductive type used to register the string or number notation is no longer available in the environment. Most likely, this is because the notation was declared inside a functor for an inductive type inside the functor. This use case is not currently supported.
>
> Alternatively, you might be trying to use a primitive token notation from a plugin which forgot to specify which module you must `Require` for access to that notation.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Syntax error: [prim:reference] expected after 'Notation' (in [vernac:command]).`  
> The type passed to [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) or [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) must be a single qualified identifier.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Syntax error: [prim:reference] expected after [prim:reference] (in [vernac:command]).`  
> Both functions passed to [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) or [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) must be single qualified identifiers.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `qualid is bound to a notation that does not denote a reference.`  
> Identifiers passed to [`String Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.String-Notation) or [`Number Notation`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Number-Notation) must be global references, or notations which evaluate to single qualified identifiers.

Example: Number Notation for radix 3

The following example parses and prints natural numbers whose digits are `0`, `1` or `2` as terms of the following inductive type encoding radix 3 numbers.

``` coq
Inductive radix3 : Set :=
  | x0 : radix3
  | x3 : radix3 -> radix3
  | x3p1 : radix3 -> radix3
  | x3p2 : radix3 -> radix3.
```

We first define a parsing function

``` coq
Definition of_uint_dec (u : Decimal.uint) : option radix3 :=
  let fix f u := match u with
    | Decimal.Nil => Some x0
    | Decimal.D0 u => match f u with Some u => Some (x3 u) | None => None end
    | Decimal.D1 u => match f u with Some u => Some (x3p1 u) | None => None end
    | Decimal.D2 u => match f u with Some u => Some (x3p2 u) | None => None end
    | _ => None end in
  f (Decimal.rev u).
```

and a printing function

``` coq
Definition to_uint_dec (x : radix3) : Decimal.uint :=
  let fix f x := match x with
    | x0 => Decimal.Nil
    | x3 x => Decimal.D0 (f x)
    | x3p1 x => Decimal.D1 (f x)
    | x3p2 x => Decimal.D2 (f x) end in
  Decimal.rev (f x).
```

before declaring the notation

``` coq
Declare Scope radix3_scope.
```

We can check the printer

``` coq
Check x3p2 (x3p1 x0).
12
     : radix3
```

and the parser

``` coq
Set Printing All.
x3 (x3p2 (x3p1 x0))
     : radix3
```

Digits other than `0`, `1` and `2` are rejected.

``` coq
Check 3.
Toplevel input, characters 6-7:
> Check 3.
>       ^
Error: Cannot interpret this number as a value of type radix3
```

Example: Number Notation for primitive integers

This shows the use of the primitive integers `PrimInt63.int` as [`qualid`<sub>`type`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid). It is the way parsing and printing of primitive integers are actually implemented in `PrimInt63.v`.

``` coq
Require Import PrimInt63.
```

Example: Number Notation for a non-inductive type

The following example encodes the terms in the form `sum unit ( ... (sum unit unit) ... )` as the number of units in the term. For instance `sum unit (sum unit unit)` is encoded as `3` while `unit` is `1` and `0` stands for `Empty_set`. The inductive `I` will be used as [`qualid`<sub>`ind`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid).

``` coq
Inductive I := Iempty : I | Iunit : I | Isum : I -> I -> I.
```

We then define [`qualid`<sub>`parse`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) and [`qualid`<sub>`print`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)

``` coq
Definition of_uint (x : Number.uint) : I :=
  let fix f n := match n with
    | O => Iempty | S O => Iunit
    | S n => Isum Iunit (f n) end in
  f (Nat.of_num_uint x).
```

the number notation itself

``` coq
Notation nSet := Set (only parsing).
```

and check the printer

``` coq
Local Open Scope type_scope.
3
     : Set
```

and the parser

``` coq
Set Printing All.
sum unit (sum unit unit)
     : Set
```

Example: Number Notation with implicit arguments

The following example parses and prints natural numbers between `0` and `n-1` as terms of type `Fin.t n`.

``` coq
Require Import Vector.
Inductive t : nat -> Set :=
    F1 : forall n : nat, Fin.t (S n)
  | FS : forall n : nat, Fin.t n -> Fin.t (S n).

Arguments Fin.t _%nat_scope
Arguments Fin.F1 {n}%nat_scope
Arguments Fin.FS {n}%nat_scope _
```

Note the implicit arguments of `Fin.F1` and `Fin.FS`, which won't appear in the corresponding inductive type.

``` coq
Inductive I := I1 : I | IS : I -> I.
```

Now `2` is parsed as `Fin.FS (Fin.FS Fin.F1)`, that is `@Fin.FS _ (@Fin.FS _ (@Fin.F1 _))`.

``` coq
Check 2.
2
     : Fin.t (S (S (S ?n)))
where
?n : [ |- nat]
```

which can be of type `Fin.t 3` (numbers `0`, `1` and `2`)

``` coq
Check 2 : Fin.t 3.
2 : Fin.t 3
     : Fin.t 3
```

but cannot be of type `Fin.t 2` (only `0` and `1`)

``` coq
Check 2 : Fin.t 2.
Toplevel input, characters 6-7:
> Check 2 : Fin.t 2.
>       ^
Error:
The term "2" has type "Fin.t (S (S (S ?n)))"
while it is expected to have type "Fin.t 2".
```

Example: String Notation with a parameterized inductive type

The parameter `Byte.byte` for the parameterized inductive type `list` is given through an [abbreviation](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#abbreviations).

``` coq
Notation string := (list Byte.byte) (only parsing).

Check "abc"%list.
"abc"%list
     : list Byte.byte
```

## Tactic Notations

Tactic notations allow customizing the syntax of tactics.

*Command* `Tactic Notation ( at level natural )? ltac_production_item+ := ltac_expr`  
``` ebnf
ltac_production_item     ::=     string
                         |       ident ( ident , string ? ) ?
```

Defines a *tactic notation*, which extends the parsing and pretty-printing of tactics.

This command supports the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) attribute, which limits the notation to the current module.

> [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)  
> The parsing precedence to assign to the notation. This information is particularly relevant for notations for tacticals. Levels can be in the range 0 .. 5 (default is 5).
>
> [`ltac_production_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-ltac_production_item)`+`  
> The notation syntax. Notations for simple tactics should begin with a [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string). Note that `Tactic Notation foo := idtac` is not valid; it should be `Tactic Notation "foo" := idtac`.
>
> [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string)  
> represents a literal value in the notation
>
> [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)  
> is the name of a grammar nonterminal listed in the table below. In a few cases, to maintain backward compatibility, the name differs from the nonterminal name used elsewhere in the documentation.
>
> `( `[`ident`<sub>`parm`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` , `[`string`<sub>`s`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string)`? )`  
> [`ident`<sub>`parm`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is the parameter name associated with [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). The [`string`<sub>`s`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string) is the separator string to use when [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) specifies a list with separators (i.e. [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) ends with `_list_sep`).
>
> [`ltac_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr)  
> The tactic expression to substitute for the notation. [`ident`<sub>`parm`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) tokens appearing in [`ltac_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr) are substituted with the associated nonterminal value.

For example, the following command defines a notation with a single parameter `x`.

``` coq
Tactic Notation "destruct_with_eqn" constr(x) := destruct x eqn:?.
```

For a complex example, examine the 16 `Tactic Notation "setoid_replace"`s defined in `$COQLIB/theories/Classes/SetoidTactics.v`, which are designed to accept any subset of 4 optional parameters.

The nonterminals that can specified in the tactic notation are:

> 

| Specified [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) | Parsed as | Interpreted as | as in tactic |
|----|----|----|----|
| `ident` | [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) | a user-given name | [`intro`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intro) |
| `simple_intropattern` | [`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern) | an introduction pattern | [`assert`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.assert) `as` |
| `hyp` | [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) | a hypothesis defined in context | [`clear`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.clear) |
| `reference` | [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) | a qualified identifier | name of an `L`<sub>tac</sub>-defined tactic |
| `smart_global` | [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) | a global reference of term | [`unfold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.unfold), [`with_strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.with_strategy) |
| `constr` | [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) | a term | [`exact`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact) |
| `uconstr` | [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) | an untyped term | [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) |
| `integer` | [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) | an integer |  |
| `int_or_var` | [`int_or_var`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-int_or_var) | an integer | [`do`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.do) |
| `strategy_level` | [`strategy_level`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-strategy_level) | a strategy level |  |
| `strategy_level_or_var` | [`strategy_level_or_var`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-strategy_level_or_var) | a strategy level | [`with_strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.with_strategy) |
| `tactic` | [`ltac_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr) | a tactic |  |
| `tactic`*n* (*n* in 0..5) | [`ltac_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr)*n* | a tactic at level *n* |  |
| *entry*`_list` | `entry*` | a list of how *entry* is interpreted |  |
| `ne_`*entry*`_list` | `entry+` | a list of how *entry* is interpreted |  |
| *entry*`_list_sep` | `entry*s` | a list of how *entry* is interpreted |  |
| `ne_`*entry*`_list_sep` | `entry+s` | a list of how *entry* is interpreted |  |

Note

In order to be bound in tactic definitions, each syntactic entry for argument type must include the case of a simple `L`<sub>tac</sub> identifier as part of what it parses. This is naturally the case for `ident`, `simple_intropattern`, `reference`, `constr`, ... but not for `integer` nor for `strategy_level`. This is the reason for introducing special entries `int_or_var` and `strategy_level_or_var` which evaluate to integers or strategy levels only, respectively, but which syntactically includes identifiers in order to be usable in tactic definitions.

Note

The *entry*`_list*` and `ne_`*entry*`_list*` entries can be used in primitive tactics or in other notations at places where a list of the underlying entry can be used: entry is either `constr`, `hyp`, `integer`, `reference`, `strategy_level`, `strategy_level_or_var`, or `int_or_var`.

Footnotes

[1](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#id3)  
which are the levels effectively chosen in the current implementation of Coq

[2](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#id4)  
Coq accepts notations declared as nonassociative but the parser on which Coq is built, namely Camlp5, currently does not implement `no associativity` and replaces it with `left associativity`; hence it is the same for Coq: `no associativity` is in fact `left associativity` for the purposes of parsing

# Setting properties of a function's arguments

*Command* `Arguments reference arg_specs* , implicits_alt** : args_modifier+,?`  
``` ebnf
arg_specs                ::=     argument_spec
                         |       /
                         |       &
                         |       ( argument_spec + ) % scope  % _ scope *
                         |       [ argument_spec + ] % scope  % _ scope *
                         |       { argument_spec + } % scope  % _ scope *
argument_spec            ::=     ! ? name % scope  % _ scope *
implicits_alt            ::=     name
                         |       [ name + ]
                         |       { name + }
args_modifier            ::=     simpl nomatch
                         |       simpl never
                         |       default implicits
                         |       clear implicits
                         |       clear scopes
                         |       clear bidirectionality hint
                         |       rename
                         |       assert
                         |       extra scopes
                         |       clear scopes and implicits
                         |       clear implicits and scopes
```

Specifies properties of the arguments of a function after the function has already been defined. It gives fine-grained control over the elaboration process (i.e. the translation of Gallina language extensions into the core language used by the kernel). The command's effects include:

- Making arguments implicit. Afterward, [implicit arguments](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/implicit-arguments.html#term-implicit-argument) must be omitted in any expression that applies [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference).

- Declaring that some arguments of a given function should be interpreted in a given [notation scope](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#term-notation-scope).

- Affecting when the [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) and [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) tactics unfold the function. See [Effects of Arguments on unfolding](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#args-effect-on-unfolding).

- Providing bidirectionality hints. See [Bidirectionality hints](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#bidirectionality-hints).

This command supports the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) and [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) attributes. Default behavior is to limit the effect to the current section but also to extend their effect outside the current module or library file. Applying [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) limits the effect of the command to the current module if it's not in a section. Applying [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) within a section extends the effect outside the current sections and current module in which the command appears.

> `/`  
> the function will be unfolded only if it's applied to at least the arguments appearing before the `/`. See [Effects of Arguments on unfolding](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#args-effect-on-unfolding).
>
> *Error* `The / modifier may only occur once.`  
>
> `&`  
> tells the type checking algorithm to first type check the arguments before the `&` and then to propagate information from that typing context to type check the remaining arguments. See [Bidirectionality hints](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#bidirectionality-hints).
>
> *Error* `The & modifier may only occur once.`  
>
> `( `[`argument_spec`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#grammar-token-argument_spec)`+ ) %_ `[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*`  
> `(`[`name`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` `[`name`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` ...)%`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*` is shorthand for [`name`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)`%`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`* `[`name`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)`%`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`* ...`
>
> `[ `[`argument_spec`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#grammar-token-argument_spec)`+ ] %_ `[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*`  
> declares the enclosed names as implicit, non-maximally inserted. `[`[`name`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` `[`name`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` ... ]%_`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*` is equivalent to `[`[`name`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)`]%_`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`* [`[`name`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)`]%_`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`* ...`
>
> `{ `[`argument_spec`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#grammar-token-argument_spec)`+ } %_ `[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*`  
> declares the enclosed names as implicit, maximally inserted. `{`[`name`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` `[`name`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` ... }%_`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*` is equivalent to `{`[`name`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)`}%_`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`* {`[`name`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)`}%_`[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`* ...`
>
> `!`  
> the function will be unfolded only if all the arguments marked with `!` evaluate to constructors. See [Effects of Arguments on unfolding](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#args-effect-on-unfolding).
>
> [`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` %_ `[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope)`*`  
> a *formal parameter* of the function [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) (i.e. the parameter name used in the function definition). Unless `rename` is specified, the list of [`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)s must be a prefix of the formal parameters, including all implicit arguments. `_` can be used to skip over a formal parameter. This construct declares [`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name) as non-implicit if `clear implicits` is specified or any other [`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name) in the [`Arguments`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#coq:cmd.Arguments) command is declared implicit. [`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope) can be either scope names or their delimiting keys. When multiple scopes are present, notations are interpreted in the leftmost scope containing them. See [Binding arguments to scopes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#binding-to-scope).
>
> Deprecated since version 8.19: The `% `[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope) syntax is deprecated in favor of the currently equivalent `%_ `[`scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope). It will be reused in future versions with the same semantics as in terms.
>
> *Error* `To rename arguments the 'rename' flag must be specified.`  
>
> *Error* `Flag 'rename' expected to rename name into name.`  
>
> *Error* `Arguments of section variables such as name may not be renamed.`  
>
> `clear implicits`  
> makes all implicit arguments into explicit arguments
>
> *Error* `The 'clear implicits' flag must be omitted if implicit annotations are given.`  
>
> `default implicits`  
> automatically determine the implicit arguments of the object. See [Automatic declaration of implicit arguments](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#auto-decl-implicit-args).
>
> *Error* `The 'default implicits' flag is incompatible with implicit annotations.`  
>
> `rename`  
> rename implicit arguments for the object. See the example [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#renaming-implicit-arguments).
>
> `assert`  
> assert that the object has the expected number of arguments with the expected names. See the example here: [Renaming implicit arguments](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#renaming-implicit-arguments).
>
