When [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is provided, that name can be used by OCaml code, typically in a plugin, to access the full path of the external file via the API `ComExtraDeps.query_extra_dep`.

> *Warning* `File ... found twice in ...`  
> The file is found in more than once in the top directories associated with the given [`dirpath`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-dirpath). In this case the first occurrence is selected.

## Backtracking

The backtracking commands described in this section can only be used interactively, they cannot be part of a Coq file loaded via `Load` or compiled by `coqc`.

*Command* `Reset ident`  
This command removes all the objects in the environment since [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) was introduced, including [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) may be the name of a defined or declared object as well as the name of a section. One cannot reset over the name of a module or of an object inside a module.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Reset Initial`  
Goes back to the initial state, just after the start of the interactive session.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Back natural?`  
Undoes all the effects of the last [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)` `[`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence)s. If [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is not specified, the command undoes one sentence. Sentences read from a `.v` file via a [`Load`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Load) are considered a single sentence. While [`Back`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Back) can undo tactics and commands executed within proof mode, once you exit proof mode, such as with [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed), all the statements executed within are thereafter considered a single sentence. [`Back`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Back) immediately following [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) gets you back to the state just after the statement of the proof.

*Error* `Invalid backtrack.`  
The user wants to undo more commands than available in the history.

<!-- -->

*Command* `BackTo natural`  
This command brings back the system to the state labeled [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural), forgetting the effect of all commands executed after this state. The state label is an integer which grows after each successful command. It is displayed in the prompt when in -emacs mode. Just as [`Back`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Back) (see above), the [`BackTo`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.BackTo) command now handles proof states. For that, it may have to undo some extra commands and end on a state [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`′ ≤ `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) if necessary.

## Quitting and debugging

*Command* `Quit`  
Causes Coq to exit. Valid only in coqtop.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Drop`  
This command temporarily enters the OCaml toplevel. It is a debug facility used by Coq’s implementers. Valid only in the bytecode version of coqtop. The OCaml command:

    #use "include";;

adds the right loadpaths and loads some toplevel printers for all abstract types of Coq- section_path, identifiers, terms, judgments, …. You can also use the file base_include instead, that loads only the pretty-printers for section_paths and identifiers. You can return back to Coq with the command:

    go();;

Warning

1.  It only works with the bytecode version of Coq (i.e. `coqtop.byte`, see Section `interactive-use`).

2.  You must have compiled Coq from the source package and set the environment variable COQTOP to the root of your copy of the sources (see Section `customization-by-environment-variables`).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Time sentence`  
Executes [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) and displays the time needed to execute it.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Instructions sentence`  
Executes [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) and displays the number of CPU instructions needed to execute it. This command is currently only supported on Linux systems, but does not fail on unsupported sustems, where it instead prints an error message in the place of the instruction count.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Redirect string sentence`  
Executes [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence), redirecting its output to the file "[`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string).out".

<!-- -->

*Command* `Timeout natural sentence`  
Executes [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence). If the operation has not terminated after [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) seconds, then it is interrupted and an error message is displayed.

*Option* `Default Timeout natural`  
When this [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) is set, each [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) is treated as if it was prefixed with [`Timeout`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Timeout) [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural), except for [`Timeout`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Timeout) commands themselves. If unset, no timeout is applied.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Fail sentence`  
For debugging scripts, sometimes it is desirable to know whether a command or a tactic fails. If [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) fails, then `Fail `[`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) succeeds (except for anomalies or for critical failures such as "stack overflow"), without changing the proof state. In interactive mode, the system prints a message confirming the failure.

*Error* `The command has not failed!`  
If the given [`command`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-command) succeeds, then `Fail `[`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) fails with this error message.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Succeed sentence`  
If [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) succeeds, then `Succeed `[`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) succeeds without changing the proof state. If [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) fails, then `Succeed `[`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) fails showing the error message for [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence). In interactive mode, the system prints the message `The command has succeeded and its effects have been reverted.` confirming the success. This command can be useful for writing tests.

Note

[`Time`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Time), [`Redirect`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Redirect), [`Timeout`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Timeout), [`Fail`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Fail) and [`Succeed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Succeed) are `control_command`s. For these commands, attributes and goal selectors, when specified, are part of the [`sentence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-sentence) argument, and thus come after the control command prefix and before the inner command or tactic. For example: `Time #[ local ] Definition foo := 0.` or `Fail Timeout 10 all: auto.`

## Controlling display

*Flag* `Silent`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) controls the normal displaying.

<!-- -->

*Option* `Warnings "-+? ident+,"`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) configures the display of warnings. The [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s are warning or category names. Adding `-` in front of a warning or category disables it, adding `+` makes it an error.

Warning name and categories are printed between brackets when the warning is displayed (the warning name appears first). Warnings can belong to multiple categories. The special category `all` contains all warnings, and the special category `default` contains the warnings enabled by default.

Coq defines a set of core warning categories, which may be extended by plugins, so this list is not exhaustive. The core categories are: `automation`, `bytecode-compiler`, `coercions`, `deprecated`, `extraction`, `filesystem`, `fixpoints`, `fragile`, `funind`, `implicits`, `ltac`, `ltac2`, `native-compiler`, `numbers`, `parsing`, `pedantic`, `records`, `ssr`, `syntax`, `tactics`, `vernacular`.

The flags are interpreted from left to right, so in case of an overlap, the flags on the right have higher priority, meaning that `A,-A` is equivalent to `-A`.

See also the [`warnings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:attr.warnings) attribute, which can be used to configure the display of warnings for a single command.

<!-- -->

*Option* `Debug "-? ident+,"`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) configures the display of debug messages. Each [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) enables debug messages for that component, while `-`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) disables messages for the component. `all` activates or deactivates all other components. `backtrace` controls printing of error backtraces.

[`Test`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Test) `Debug` displays the list of components and their enabled/disabled state.

<!-- -->

*Option* `Printing Width natural`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) sets which left-aligned part of the width of the screen is used for display. At the time of writing this documentation, the default value is 78.

<!-- -->

*Option* `Printing Depth natural`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) controls the nesting depth of the formatter used for pretty- printing. Beyond this depth, display of subterms is replaced by dots. At the time of writing this documentation, the default value is 50.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Printing Compact Contexts`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) controls the compact display mode for goals contexts. When on, the printer tries to reduce the vertical size of goals contexts by putting several variables (even if of different types) on the same line provided it does not exceed the printing width (see [`Printing Width`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Printing-Width)). At the time of writing this documentation, it is off by default.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Printing Unfocused`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) controls whether unfocused goals are displayed. Such goals are created by focusing other goals with [bullets](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#bullets) or [curly braces](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#curly-braces). It is off by default.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Printing Dependent Evars Line`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) controls the printing of the “(dependent evars: …)” information after each tactic. The information is used by the Prooftree tool in Proof General. (<https://askra.de/software/prooftree>)

## Printing constructions in full

*Flag* `Printing All`  
Coercions, implicit arguments, the type of pattern matching, but also notations (see [Syntax extensions and notation scopes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#syntax-extensions-and-notation-scopes)) can obfuscate the behavior of some tactics (typically the tactics applying to occurrences of subterms are sensitive to the implicit arguments). Turning this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) on deactivates all high-level printing features such as coercions, implicit arguments, returned type of pattern matching, notations and various syntactic sugar for pattern matching or record projections. Otherwise said, [`Printing All`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Printing-All) includes the effects of the flags [`Printing Implicit`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/implicit-arguments.html#coq:flag.Printing-Implicit), [`Printing Coercions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#coq:flag.Printing-Coercions), [`Printing Synth`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/match.html#coq:flag.Printing-Synth), [`Printing Projections`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/records.html#coq:flag.Printing-Projections), and [`Printing Notations`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:flag.Printing-Notations). To reactivate the high-level printing features, use the command `Unset Printing All`.

Note

In some cases, setting [`Printing All`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Printing-All) may display terms that are so big they become very hard to read. One technique to work around this is use [`Undelimit Scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Undelimit-Scope) and/or [`Close Scope`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#coq:cmd.Close-Scope) to turn off the printing of notations bound to particular scope(s). This can be useful when notations in a given scope are getting in the way of understanding a goal, but turning off all notations with [`Printing All`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Printing-All) would make the goal unreadable.

## Controlling Typing Flags

*Flag* `Guard Checking`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) can be used to enable/disable the guard checking of fixpoints. Warning: this can break the consistency of the system, use at your own risk. Decreasing argument can still be specified: the decrease is not checked anymore but it still affects the reduction of the term. Unchecked fixpoints are printed by [`Print Assumptions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Print-Assumptions).

<!-- -->

*Attribute* `bypass_check(guard= yesno?)`  
This [boolean attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-boolean-attribute) is similar to the [`Guard Checking`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Guard-Checking) flag, but on a per-declaration basis. Disable guard checking locally with `bypass_check(guard)`.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Positivity Checking`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) can be used to enable/disable the positivity checking of inductive types and the productivity checking of coinductive types. Warning: this can break the consistency of the system, use at your own risk. Unchecked (co)inductive types are printed by [`Print Assumptions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Print-Assumptions).

<!-- -->

*Attribute* `bypass_check(positivity= yesno?)`  
This [boolean attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-boolean-attribute) is similar to the [`Positivity Checking`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Positivity-Checking) flag, but on a per-declaration basis. Disable positivity checking locally with `bypass_check(positivity)`.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Universe Checking`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) can be used to enable/disable the checking of universes, providing a form of "type in type". Warning: this breaks the consistency of the system, use at your own risk. Constants relying on "type in type" are printed by [`Print Assumptions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Print-Assumptions). It has the same effect as `-type-in-type` command line argument (see [Command line options](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/practical-tools/coq-commands.html#command-line-options)).

<!-- -->

*Attribute* `bypass_check(universes= yesno?)`  
This [boolean attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-boolean-attribute) is similar to the [`Universe Checking`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Universe-Checking) flag, but on a per-declaration basis. Disable universe checking locally with `bypass_check(universes)`.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Typing Flags`  
Print the status of the three typing flags: guard checking, positivity checking and universe checking.

Example

``` coq
Unset Guard Checking.
check_guarded: false
check_positive: true
check_universes: true
definitional uip: false
f is defined
f is recursively defined (guarded on 1st argument)
ackermann is defined
ackermann is recursively defined (guarded on 1st argument)
Axioms:
ackermann is assumed to be guarded.
```

Note that the proper way to define the Ackermann function is to use an inner fixpoint:

``` coq
Fixpoint ack m :=
  fix ackm n :=
  match m with
  | 0 => S n
  | S m' =>
    match n with
    | 0 => ack m' 1
    | S n' => ack m' (ackm n')
    end
  end.
ack is defined
ack is recursively defined (guarded on 1st argument)
```

Typing flags may not be changed while inside sections.

## Internal registration commands

Due to their internal nature, the commands that are presented in this section are not for general use. They are meant to appear only in standard libraries and in support libraries of plug-ins.

### Exposing constants to OCaml libraries

*Command* `Register qualid1 as qualid2`  
Makes the constant [`qualid`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) accessible to OCaml libraries under the name [`qualid`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid). The constant can then be dynamically located in OCaml code by calling `Coqlib.lib_ref "`[`qualid`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid)`"`. The OCaml code doesn't need to know where the constant is defined (what file, module, library, etc.).

As a special case, when the first segment of [`qualid`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) is `kernel`, the constant is exposed to the kernel. For instance, the `PrimInt63` module features the following declaration:

``` coq
Register bool as kernel.ind_bool.
```

This makes the kernel aware of the `bool` type, which is used, for example, to define the return type of the `#int63_eq` primitive.

See also

[Primitive Integers](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/primitive.html#primitive-integers)

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Registered`  

### Inlining hints for the fast reduction machines

*Command* `Register Inline qualid`  
Gives a hint to the reduction machines (VM and native) that the body of the constant [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) should be inlined in the generated code.

### Registering primitive operations

*Command* `Primitive ident_decl : term? := #ident`  
Makes the primitive type or primitive operator `#`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) defined in OCaml accessible in Coq commands and tactics. For internal use by implementors of Coq's standard library or standard library replacements. No space is allowed after the `#`. Invalid values give a syntax error.

For example, the standard library files `PrimInt63.v` and `PrimFloat.v` use [`Primitive`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Primitive) to support, respectively, the features described in [Primitive Integers](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/primitive.html#primitive-integers) and [Primitive Floats](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/primitive.html#primitive-floats).

The types associated with an operator must be declared to the kernel before declaring operations that use the type. Do this with [`Primitive`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Primitive) for primitive types and [`Register`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Register) with the `kernel` prefix for other types. For example, in `PrimInt63.v`, `#int63_type` must be declared before the associated operations.

*Error* `The type ident must be registered before this construction can be typechecked.`  
The type must be defined with [`Primitive`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Primitive) command before this [`Primitive`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Primitive) command (declaring an operation using the type) will succeed.

# Basic proof writing

Coq is an interactive theorem prover, or proof assistant, which means that proofs can be constructed interactively through a dialog between the user and the assistant. The building blocks for this dialog are tactics which the user will use to represent steps in the proof of a theorem.

The first section presents the proof mode (the core mechanism of the dialog between the user and the proof assistant). Then, several sections describe the available tactics. The last section covers the SSReflect proof language, which provides a consistent alternative set of tactics to the standard basic tactics.

Additional tactics are documented in the next chapter [Automatic solvers and programmable tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/index.html#automatic-tactics).

- [Proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html)
- [Tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html)
- [Reasoning with equalities](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html)
- [Reasoning with inductive types](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html)
- [The SSReflect proof language](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html)

# Proof mode

Proof mode is used to prove theorems. Coq enters proof mode when you begin a proof, such as with the [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) command. It exits proof mode when you complete a proof, such as with the [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) command. Tactics, which are available only in proof mode, incrementally transform incomplete proofs to eventually generate a complete proof.

When you run Coq interactively, such as through CoqIDE, Proof General or coqtop, Coq shows the current proof state (the incomplete proof) as you enter tactics. This information isn't shown when you run Coq in batch mode with `coqc`.

## Proof State

The proof state consists of one or more unproven goals. Each goal has a conclusion (the statement that is to be proven) and a local context, which contains named [hypotheses](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-hypothesis) (which are propositions), variables and local definitions that can be used in proving the conclusion. The proof may also use *constants* from the [global environment](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-global-environment) such as definitions and proven theorems.

(Note that *conclusion* is also used to refer to the last part of an implication. For example, in `A -> B -> C`, `A` and `B` are [premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-premise) and `C` is the conclusion.)

The term "goal" may refer to an entire goal or to the conclusion of a goal, depending on the context.

The conclusion appears below a line and the local context appears above the line. The conclusion is a type. Each item in the local context begins with a name and ends, after a colon, with an associated type. Local definitions are shown in the form `n := 0 : nat`, for example, in which `nat` is the type of `0`.

The local context of a goal contains items specific to the goal as well as section-local variables and hypotheses (see [Assumptions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#gallina-assumptions)) defined in the current [section](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sections.html#section-mechanism). The latter are included in the initial proof state. Items in the local context are ordered; an item can only refer to items that appear before it. (A more mathematical description of the *local context* is [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/cic.html#local-context).)

The global environment has definitions and proven theorems that are global in scope. (A more mathematical description of the *global environment* is [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/cic.html#global-environment).)

When you begin proving a theorem, the proof state shows the statement of the theorem below the line and often nothing in the local context:

``` coq
1 goal

  ============================
  forall n m : nat, n > m -> P 1 /\ P 2
```

After applying the [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) [tactic](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic), we see hypotheses above the line. The names of variables (`n` and `m`) and hypotheses (`H`) appear before a colon, followed by their type. The type doesn't have to be a provable statement. For example, `0 = 1` and `False` are both valid and useful types.

``` coq
intros.
1 goal

  n, m : nat
  H : n > m
  ============================
  P 1 /\ P 2
```

Some tactics, such as [`split`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.split), create new goals, which may be referred to as subgoals for clarity. Goals are numbered from 1 to N at each step of the proof to permit applying a tactic to specific goals. The local context is only shown for the first goal.

``` coq
split.
2 goals

  n, m : nat
  H : n > m
  ============================
  P 1

goal 2 is:
 P 2
```

"Variables" may refer specifically to local context items introduced from `forall` variables for which the type of their type is `Set` or `Type`. "Hypotheses" refers to items that are [propositions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sorts.html#term-proposition), for which the type of their type is `Prop` or `SProp`, but these terms are also used interchangeably.

``` coq
type of n : nat
type of nat : Set
type of H : (n > m)
type of (n > m) : Prop
```

A proof script, consisting of the tactics that are applied to prove a theorem, is often informally referred to as a "proof". The real proof, whether complete or incomplete, is the associated term, the proof term, which users may occasionally want to examine. (This is based on the *Curry-Howard isomorphism* [\[How80\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#how80)[\[Bar81\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#bar81)[\[GLT89\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#gir89)[\[Hue89\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#h89), which is a correspondence between between proofs and terms and between [propositions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sorts.html#term-proposition) and types of λ-calculus. The isomorphism is also sometimes called the "propositions-as-types correspondence".)

The [`Show Proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Show-Proof) command displays the incomplete proof term before you've completed the proof. For example, here's the proof term after using the [`split`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.split) tactic above:

``` coq
Show Proof.
(fun (n m : nat) (H : n > m) => conj ?Goal ?Goal0)
```

The incomplete parts, the goals, are represented by [existential variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#term-existential-variable) with names that begin with `?Goal`. (Note that some existential variables are not goals.) The [`Show Existentials`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Show-Existentials) command shows each existential with the hypotheses and conclusion for the associated goal.

``` coq
Show Existentials.
Existential 1 = ?Goal : [n : nat  m : nat  H : n > m |- P 1]
Existential 2 = ?Goal0 : [n : nat  m : nat  H : n > m |- P 2]
```

Users can control which goals are displayed in the context by [focusing](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-focus) goals. Focusing lets the user (initially) pick a single goal to work on. Focusing operations can be nested.

Tactics such as [`eapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eapply) create existential variables as placeholders for undetermined variables that become [shelved](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-shelved) goals. Shelved goals are not shown in the context by default, but they can be unshelved to make them visible. Other tactics may automatically resolve these goals (whether shelved or not); the purpose of shelving is to hide goals that the user usually doesn't need to think about. See [Existential variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#existential-variables) and [this example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#automatic-evar-resolution).

Coq's kernel verifies the correctness of proof terms when it exits proof mode by checking that the proof term is [well-typed](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-well-typed) and that its type is the same as the theorem statement.

After a proof is completed, [`Print`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Print) `<theorem_name>` shows the proof term and its type. The type appears after the colon (`forall ...`), as for this theorem from Coq's standard library:

``` coq
Print proj1.
Fetching opaque proofs from disk for Coq.Init.Logic
proj1 =
fun (A B : Prop) (H : A /\ B) =>
match H with
| conj x x0 => (fun (H0 : A) (_ : B) => H0) x x0
end
     : forall A B : Prop, A /\ B -> A

Arguments proj1 [A B]%type_scope _
```

Note

Many tactics accept [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)s as arguments and frequently refer to them with wording such as "the type of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)". When [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is the name of a theorem or lemma, this wording refers to the type of the proof term, which is what's given in the [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) statement. When [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is the name of a hypothesis, the wording refers to the type shown in the context for the hypothesis (i.e., after the colon). For terms that are more complex than just an [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), you can use [`Check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Check) [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) to display their type.

## Entering and exiting proof mode

Coq enters [proof mode](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-proof-mode) when you begin a proof through commands such as [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) or [`Goal`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Goal). Coq user interfaces usually have a way to indicate that you're in proof mode.

[Tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-tactic) are available only in proof mode (currently they give syntax errors outside of proof mode). Most [commands](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-command) can be used both in and out of proof mode, but some commands only work in or outside of proof mode.

When the proof is completed, you can exit proof mode with commands such as [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed), [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined) and [`Save`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Save).

*Command* `Goal type`  
Asserts an unnamed proposition. This is intended for quick tests that a proposition is provable. If the proof is eventually completed and validated, you can assign a name with the [`Save`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Save) or [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined) commands. If no name is given, the name will be `Unnamed_thm` (or, if that name is already defined, a variant of that).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Qed`  
Passes a completed [proof term](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-proof-term) to Coq's kernel to check that the proof term is [well-typed](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-well-typed) and to verify that its type matches the theorem statement. If it's verified, the proof term is added to the global environment as an [opaque](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-opaque) constant using the declared name from the original goal.

It's very rare for a proof term to fail verification. Generally this indicates a bug in a tactic you used or that you misused some unsafe tactics.

*Error* `Attempt to save an incomplete proof.`  

*Error* `No focused proof (No proof-editing in progress).`  
You tried to use a proof mode command such as [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) outside of proof mode.

Note

Sometimes an error occurs when building the proof term, because tactics do not enforce completely the term construction constraints.

The user should also be aware of the fact that since the proof term is completely rechecked at this point, one may have to wait a while when the proof is large. In some exceptional cases one may even incur a memory overflow.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Save ident`  
Similar to [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed), except that the proof term is added to the global context with the name [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), which overrides any name provided by the [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) command or its variants.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Defined ident?`  
Similar to [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) and [`Save`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Save), except the proof is made [transparent](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-transparent), which means that its content can be explicitly used for type checking and that it can be unfolded in conversion tactics (see [Applying conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#applyingconversionrules), [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque), [`Transparent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Transparent)). If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is specified, the proof is defined with the given name, which overrides any name provided by the [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) command or its variants.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Admitted`  
This command is available in proof mode to give up the current proof and declare the initial goal as an axiom.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Abort All?`  
Aborts the current proof. If the current proof is a nested proof, the previous proof becomes current. If `All` is given, all nested proofs are aborted. See [`Nested Proofs Allowed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:flag.Nested-Proofs-Allowed).

`All`  
Aborts all current proofs.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Proof term`  
This command applies in proof mode. It is equivalent to `exact `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`. Qed.` That is, you have to give the full proof in one gulp, as a proof term (see Section [Applying theorems](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#applyingtheorems)).

Warning

Use of this command is discouraged. In particular, it doesn't work in Proof General because it must immediately follow the command that opened proof mode, but Proof General inserts [`Unset`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#coq:cmd.Unset) [`Silent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Silent) before it (see [Proof General issue \#498](https://github.com/ProofGeneral/PG/issues/498)).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Proof`  
Is a no-op which is useful to delimit the sequence of tactic commands which start a proof, after a [`Theorem`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Theorem) command. It is a good practice to use [`Proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof) as an opening parenthesis, closed in the script with a closing [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed).

See also

[`Proof with`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/auto.html#coq:cmd.Proof-with)

<!-- -->

*Command* `Proof using section_var_expr with ltac_expr?`  
``` ebnf
section_var_expr         ::=     starred_ident_ref *
                         |       - ? section_var_expr50
section_var_expr50       ::=     section_var_expr0 - section_var_expr0
                         |       section_var_expr0 + section_var_expr0
                         |       section_var_expr0
section_var_expr0        ::=     starred_ident_ref
                         |       ()
                         |       ( section_var_expr ) * ?
starred_ident_ref        ::=     ident * ?
                         |       Type * ?
                         |       All
```

Opens proof mode, declaring the set of [section](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sections.html#section-mechanism) variables (see [Assumptions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#gallina-assumptions)) used by the proof. These [proof annotations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/parallel-proof-processing.html#proof-annotations) are useful to enable asynchronous processing of proofs. This [example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#example-print-using) shows how they work. The [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) command verifies that the set of section variables used in the proof is a subset of the declared ones.

The set of declared variables is closed under type dependency. For example, if `T` is a variable and `a` is a variable of type `T`, then the commands `Proof using a` and `Proof using T a` are equivalent.

The set of declared variables always includes the variables used by the statement. In other words `Proof using e` is equivalent to `Proof using Type + e` for any declaration expression `e`.

`- `[`section_var_expr50`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr50)  
Use all section variables except those specified by [`section_var_expr50`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr50)

[`section_var_expr0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr0)` + `[`section_var_expr0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr0)  
Use section variables from the union of both collections. See [Name a set of section hypotheses for Proof using](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#nameaset) to see how to form a named collection.

[`section_var_expr0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr0)` - `[`section_var_expr0`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr0)  
Use section variables which are in the first collection but not in the second one.

`*?`  
Use the transitive closure of the specified collection.

`Type`  
Use only section variables occurring in the statement. Specifying `*` uses the forward transitive closure of all the section variables occurring in the statement. For example, if the variable `H` has type `p < 5` then `H` is in `p*` since `p` occurs in the type of `H`.

`All`  
Use all section variables.

*Warning* `ident is both name of a Collection and Variable, Collection ident takes precedence over Variable.`  
If a specified name is ambiguous (it could be either a [`Collection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Collection) or a [`Variable`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Variable)), then it is assumed to be a [`Collection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Collection) name.

*Warning* `Variable All is shadowed by Collection named All containing all variables.`  
This is variant of the previous warning for the **All** collection.

See also

[Setting implicit automation tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/auto.html#tactics-implicit-automation)

<!-- -->

*Attribute* `using`  
This [attribute](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-attribute) can be applied to the [`Definition`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Definition), [`Example`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Example), [`Fixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#coq:cmd.Fixpoint) and [`CoFixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/coinductive.html#coq:cmd.CoFixpoint) commands as well as to [`Lemma`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Lemma) and its variants. It takes a [`section_var_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr), in quotes, as its value. This is equivalent to specifying the same [`section_var_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr) in [`Proof using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof-using).

Example

``` coq
Section Test.
n is declared
Hn is declared
1 goal

  n : nat
  Hn : n <> 0
  ============================
  0 < n

Abort.
```

> Example: Declaring section variables
>
> When a [section](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sections.html#section-mechanism) is closed with [`End`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sections.html#coq:cmd.End), section variables declared with [`Proof using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof-using) are added to the theorem as additional variables. You can see the effect on the theorem's statement with commands such as [`Check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Check), [`Print`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Print) and [`About`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.About) after the section is closed. Currently there is no command that shows the section variables associated with a theorem before the section is closed.
>
> Adding the unnecessary section variable `radixNotZero` changes how `foo'` can be applied.
>
> ``` coq
> Require Import ZArith.
>
> Print foo'. (* Doesn't show radixNotZero yet *)
> foo' = eq_refl
>      : 0 = 0
>
> foo' uses section variables radix radixNotZero.
> foo = eq_refl
>      : 0 = 0
> foo' =
> fun (radix : Z) (_ : (0 < radix)%Z) => eq_refl
>      : forall radix : Z, (0 < radix)%Z -> 0 = 0
>
> Arguments foo' radix%Z_scope radixNotZero
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   0 = 0
>
> Fail apply foo'. (* Fails because of the extra variable *)
>
> apply (foo' 5). (* Can be used if the extra variable is provided explicitly *)
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   (0 < 5)%Z
> ```

### Proof using options

The following options modify the behavior of `Proof using`.

*Option* `Default Proof Using "section_var_expr"`  
Set this [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) to use [`section_var_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr) as the default `Proof using` value. E.g. `Set Default Proof Using "a b"` will complete all `Proof` commands not followed by a `using` part with `using a b`.

Note that [`section_var_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-section_var_expr) isn't validated immediately. An invalid value will generate an error on a subsequent [`Proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof) or [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) command.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Suggest Proof Using`  
When this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) is on, [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) suggests a `using` annotation if the user did not provide one.

### Name a set of section hypotheses for `Proof using`

*Command* `Collection ident := section_var_expr`  
This can be used to name a set of section hypotheses, with the purpose of making `Proof using` annotations more compact.

Example

Define the collection named `Some` containing `x`, `y` and `z`:

    Collection Some := x y z.

Define the collection named `Fewer` containing only `x` and `y`:

    Collection Fewer := Some - z

Define the collection named `Many` containing the set union or set difference of `Fewer` and `Some`:

    Collection Many := Fewer + Some
    Collection Many := Fewer - Some

Define the collection named `Many` containing the set difference of `Fewer` and the unnamed collection `x y`:

    Collection Many := Fewer - (x y)

Deprecated since version 8.15: Redefining a collection, defining a collection with the same name as a variable, and invoking the [`Proof using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof-using) command when collection and variable names overlap are deprecated. See the warnings below and in the [`Proof using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof-using) command.

*Error* `"All" is a predefined collection containing all variables. It can't be redefined.`  
When issuing a [`Proof using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof-using) command, **All** used as a collection name always means "use all variables".

*Warning* `New Collection definition of ident shadows the previous one.`  
Redefining a [`Collection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Collection) overwrites the previous definition.

*Warning* `ident was already a defined Variable, the name ident will refer to Collection when executing "Proof using" command.`  
The [`Proof using`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof-using) command allows specifying both [`Collection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Collection) and [`Variable`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#coq:cmd.Variable) names. In case of ambiguity, a name is assumed to be Collection name.

## Proof modes

When entering proof mode through commands such as [`Goal`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Goal) and [`Proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Proof), Coq picks by default the `L`<sub>tac</sub> mode. Nonetheless, there exist other proof modes shipped in the standard Coq installation, and furthermore some plugins define their own proof modes. The default proof mode used when opening a proof can be changed using the following option.

*Option* `Default Proof Mode string`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) selects the proof mode to use when starting a proof. Depending on the proof mode, various syntactic constructs are allowed when writing a proof. All proof modes support commands; the proof mode determines which tactic language and set of tactic definitions are available. The possible option values are:

`"Classic"`  
Activates the `L`<sub>tac</sub> language and the tactics with the syntax documented in this manual. Some tactics are not available until the associated plugin is loaded, such as `SSR` or `micromega`. This proof mode is set when the [prelude](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#term-prelude) is loaded.

`"Noedit"`  
No tactic language is activated at all. This is the default when the [prelude](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/coq-library.html#term-prelude) is not loaded, e.g. through the `-noinit` option for `coqc`.

`"Ltac2"`  
Activates the Ltac2 language and the Ltac2-specific variants of the documented tactics. This value is only available after [`Requiring`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Require) Ltac2. [`Importing`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:cmd.Import) Ltac2 sets this mode.

Some external plugins also define their own proof mode, which can be activated with this command.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Proof Mode string`  
Sets the proof mode within the current proof.

## Managing goals

*Command* `Undo To? natural?`  
Cancels the effect of the last [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) commands or tactics. The `To `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) form goes back to the specified state number. If [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is not specified, the command goes back one command or tactic.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Restart`  
Restores the proof to the original goal.

*Error* `No focused proof to restart.`  

### Focusing goals

Focusing lets you limit the context display to (initially) a single goal. If a tactic creates additional goals from a focused goal, the subgoals are also focused. The two focusing constructs are [curly braces](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#curly-braces) (`{` and `}`) and [bullets](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#bullets) (e.g. `-`, `+` or `*`). These constructs can be nested.

#### Curly braces

*Tactic* `natural[ ident ] :? {`\
*Tactic* `}`  
`{` (without a terminating period) focuses on the first goal. The subproof can only be unfocused when it has been fully solved (*i.e.*, when there is no focused goal left). Unfocusing is then handled by `}` (again, without a terminating period). See also an example in the next section.

Note that when a focused goal is proved a message is displayed together with a suggestion about the right bullet or `}` to unfocus it or focus the next goal.

[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`:`  
Focuses on the [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)-th goal to prove.

> `[ `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` ]: {`  
> Focuses on the goal named [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) even if the goal is not in focus. Goals are [existential variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#term-existential-variable), which don't have names by default. You can give a name to a goal by using `refine ?[`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`]`.
>
> Example: Working with named goals
>
> ``` coq
> Ltac name_goal name := refine ?[name]. (* for convenience *)
>
> Goal forall n, n + 0 = n.
> 1 goal (?Goal)
>
>   ============================
>   forall n : nat, n + 0 = n
> 2 goals, goal 1 (?base)
>
>   ============================
>   0 + 0 = 0
>
> goal 2 (?step) is:
>  S n + 0 = S n
> 1 goal (?base)
>
>   ============================
>   0 + 0 = 0
>
> This subproof is complete, but there are some unfocused goals.
> Try unfocusing with "}".
>
> 1 goal
>
> goal 1 (?step) is:
>  S n + 0 = S n
>
> }
> ```
>
> This can also be a way of focusing on a shelved goal, for instance:
>
> ``` coq
> Goal exists n : nat, n = n.
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   exists n : nat, n = n
> 1 focused goal (shelved: 1)
>
>   ============================
>   ?x = ?x
> All the remaining goals are on the shelf.
>
> 1 goal
>
> goal 1 is:
>  nat
> No more goals.
> ```
>
> *Error* `This proof is focused, but cannot be unfocused this way.`  
> You are trying to use `}` but the current subproof has not been fully solved.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `No such goal (natural).`  
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `No such goal (ident).`  
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Brackets do not support multi-goal selectors.`  
> Brackets are used to focus on a single goal given either by its position or by its name if it has one.
>
> See also
>
> The error messages for bullets below.

#### Bullets

Alternatively, proofs can be structured with bullets instead of `{` and `}`. The first use of a bullet `b` focuses on the first goal `g`. The same bullet can't be used again until the proof of `g` is completed, then the next goal must be focused with another `b`. Thus, all the goals present just before the first use of the bullet must be focused with the same bullet `b`. See the example below.

Different bullets can be used to nest levels. The scope of each bullet is limited to the enclosing `{` and `}`, so bullets can be reused as further nesting levels provided they are delimited by curly braces. A `bullet` is made from `-`, `+` or `*` characters (with no spaces and no period afterward):

*Tactic* `-+++*+`  

When a focused goal is proved, Coq displays a message suggesting use of `}` or the correct matching bullet to unfocus the goal or focus the next subgoal.

Note

In Proof General (`Emacs` interface to Coq), you must use bullets with the priority ordering shown above to have correct indentation. For example `-` must be the outer bullet and `+` the inner one in the example below.

Example: Use of bullets

For the sake of brevity, the output for this example is summarized in comments. Note that the tactic following a bullet is frequently put on the same line with the bullet. Observe that this proof still works even if all the bullets in it are omitted.

``` coq
Goal (1=1 /\ 2=2) /\ 3=3.
```

*Error* `Wrong bullet bullet1: Current bullet bullet2 is not finished.`  
Before using bullet [`bullet`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-bullet) again, you should first finish proving the current focused goal. Note that [`bullet`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-bullet) and [`bullet`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-bullet) may be the same.

<!-- -->

*Error* `Wrong bullet bullet1: Bullet bullet2 is mandatory here.`  
You must put [`bullet`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-bullet) to focus on the next goal. No other bullet is allowed here.

<!-- -->

*Error* `No such goal. Focus next goal with bullet bullet.`  
You tried to apply a tactic but no goals were under focus. Using [`bullet`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#grammar-token-bullet) is mandatory here.

<!-- -->

*Error* `No such goal. Try unfocusing with }.`  
You just finished a goal focused by `{`, you must unfocus it with `}`.

Note

Use [`Default Goal Selector`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:opt.Default-Goal-Selector) with the `!` selector to force the use of focusing mechanisms (bullets, braces) and goal selectors so that it is always explicit to which goal(s) a tactic is applied.

*Option* `Bullet Behavior "None""Strict Subproofs"`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) controls the bullet behavior and can take two possible values:

- "None": this makes bullets inactive.

- "Strict Subproofs": this makes bullets active (this is the default behavior).

#### Other focusing commands

*Command* `Unfocused`  
Succeeds if there are no unfocused goals. Otherwise the command fails.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Focus natural?`  
Focuses the attention on the first goal to prove or, if [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is specified, the [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)-th. The printing of the other goals is suspended until the focused goal is solved or unfocused.

Deprecated since version 8.8: Prefer the use of bullets or focusing braces with a goal selector (see above).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Unfocus`  
Restores to focus the goals that were suspended by the last [`Focus`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Focus) command.

Deprecated since version 8.8.

### Shelving goals

Goals can be shelved so they are no longer displayed in the proof state. Shelved goals can be unshelved with the [`Unshelve`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Unshelve) command, which makes all shelved goals visible in the proof state. You can use the goal selector `[ `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` ]: {` to focus on a single shelved goal (see [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#focus-shelved-goal)). Currently there's no single command or tactic that unshelves goals by name.

*Tactic* `shelve`  
Moves the focused goals to the shelf. They will no longer be displayed in the context. The [`Show Existentials`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Show-Existentials) command will still show these goals, which will be marked "(shelved)".

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `shelve_unifiable`  
Shelves only the goals under focus that are mentioned in other goals. Goals that appear in the type of other goals can be solved by unification.

Example: shelve_unifiable

``` coq
Goal exists n, n=0.
1 goal

  ============================
  exists n : nat, n = 0
1 focused goal (shelved: 1)

  ============================
  ?Goal = 0
No more goals.
```

<!-- -->

*Command* `Unshelve`  
This command moves all the goals on the shelf (see [`shelve`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.shelve)) from the shelf into focus, by appending them to the end of the current list of focused goals.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `unshelve ltac_expr1`  
Performs [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic), then unshelves existential variables added to the shelf by the execution of [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic), prepending them to the current goal.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `admit`\
*Tactic* `give_up`  
Allows skipping a subgoal to permit further progress on the rest of the proof. The selected goals are removed from the context. They are not solved and cannot be solved later in the proof. Since the goals are not solved, the proof cannot be closed with [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) but only with [`Admitted`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Admitted).

### Reordering goals

*Tactic* `cycle int_or_var`  
Reorders the selected goals so that the first [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) goals appear after the other selected goals. If [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) is negative, it puts the last [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) goals at the beginning of the list. The tactic is only useful with a goal selector, most commonly `all:`. Note that other selectors reorder goals; `1,3: cycle 1` is not equivalent to `all: cycle 1`. See [`… : … (goal selector)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.…-:-…-(goal-selector)).

Example: cycle

``` coq
Goal P 1 /\ P 2 /\ P 3 /\ P 4 /\ P 5.
```

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `swap int_or_var int_or_var`  
Exchanges the position of the specified goals. Negative values for [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) indicate counting goals backward from the end of the list of selected goals. Goals are indexed from 1. The tactic is only useful with a goal selector, most commonly `all:`. Note that other selectors reorder goals; `1,3: swap 1 3` is not equivalent to `all: swap 1 3`. See [`… : … (goal selector)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.…-:-…-(goal-selector)).

Example: swap

``` coq
Goal P 1 /\ P 2 /\ P 3 /\ P 4 /\ P 5.
```

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `revgoals`  
Reverses the order of the selected goals. The tactic is only useful with a goal selector, most commonly `all :`. Note that other selectors reorder goals; `1,3: revgoals` is not equivalent to `all: revgoals`. See [`… : … (goal selector)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.…-:-…-(goal-selector)).

Example: revgoals

``` coq
Goal P 1 /\ P 2 /\ P 3 /\ P 4 /\ P 5.
```

## Proving a subgoal as a separate lemma: abstract

*Tactic* `abstract ltac_expr2 using identname?`  
Does a [`solve`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.solve) `[ `[`ltac_expr2`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr2)` ]` and saves the subproof as an auxiliary lemma. if [`ident`<sub>`name`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is specified, the lemma is saved with that name; otherwise the lemma is saved with the name [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`_subproof`[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`?` where [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is the name of the current goal (e.g. the theorem name) and [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is chosen to get a fresh name. If the proof is closed with [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed), the auxiliary lemma is inlined in the final proof term.

This is useful with tactics such as [`discriminate`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.discriminate) that generate huge proof terms with many intermediate goals. It can significantly reduce peak memory use. In most cases it doesn't have a significant impact on run time. One case in which it can reduce run time is when a tactic `foo` is known to always pass type checking when it succeeds, such as in reflective proofs. In this case, the idiom "[`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract) [`exact_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact_no_check) `foo`" will save half the type checking type time compared to "[`exact`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact) `foo`".

[`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract) is an [`l3_tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-l3_tactic).

Warning

The abstract tactic, while very useful, still has some known limitations. See [\#9146](https://github.com/coq/coq/issues/9146) for more details. We recommend caution when using it in some "non-standard" contexts. In particular, `abstract` doesn't work properly when used inside quotations `ltac:(...)`. If used as part of typeclass resolution, it may produce incorrect terms when in polymorphic universe mode.

Warning

Provide [`ident`<sub>`name`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) at your own risk; explicitly named and reused subterms don’t play well with asynchronous proofs.

*Tactic* `transparent_abstract ltac_expr3 using ident?`  
Like [`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract), but save the subproof in a transparent lemma with a name in the form [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`_subterm`[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`?`.

Warning

Use this feature at your own risk; building computationally relevant terms with tactics is fragile, and explicitly named and reused subterms don’t play well with asynchronous proofs.

*Error* `Proof is not complete.`  

## Requesting information

*Command* `Show identnatural?`  
Displays the current goals.

[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)  
Display only the [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)-th goal.

[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)  
Displays the named goal [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). This is useful in particular to display a shelved goal but only works if the corresponding existential variable has been named by the user (see [Existential variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#existential-variables)) as in the following example.

Example

``` coq
Goal exists n, n = 0.
1 goal

  ============================
  exists n : nat, n = 0
1 focused goal (shelved: 1)

  ============================
  ?n = 0
goal n is:

  ============================
  nat
```

*Error* `No focused proof.`  

*Error* `No such goal.`  

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Proof Diffs removed??`  
Displays the proof term generated by the tactics that have been applied so far. If the proof is incomplete, the term will contain holes, which correspond to subterms which are still to be constructed. Each hole is an existential variable, which appears as a question mark followed by an identifier.

Specifying “Diffs” highlights the difference between the current and previous proof step. By default, the command shows the output once with additions highlighted. Including “removed” shows the output twice: once showing removals and once showing additions. It does not examine the [`Diffs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:opt.Diffs) option. See ["Show Proof" differences](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#id9).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Conjectures`  
Prints the names of all the theorems that are currently being proved. As it is possible to start proving a previous lemma during the proof of a theorem, there may be multiple names.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Intro`  
If the current goal begins by at least one product, prints the name of the first product as it would be generated by an anonymous [`intro`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intro). The aim of this command is to ease the writing of more robust scripts. For example, with an appropriate Proof General macro, it is possible to transform any anonymous [`intro`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intro) into a qualified one such as `intro y13`. In the case of a non-product goal, it prints nothing.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Intros`  
Similar to the previous command. Simulates the naming process of [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Existentials`  
Displays all open goals / existential variables in the current proof along with the context and type of each variable.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Match qualid`  
Displays a template of the Gallina [`match`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/variants.html#grammar-token-term_match) construct with a branch for each constructor of the type [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid). This is used internally by [company-coq](https://github.com/cpitclaudel/company-coq).

Example

``` coq
Show Match nat.
match # with
 | O =>
 | S x =>
 end
```

*Error* `Unknown inductive type.`  

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Universes`  
Displays the set of all universe constraints and its normalized form at the current stage of the proof, useful for debugging universe inconsistencies.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Show Goal natural at natural`  
Available in coqtop. Displays a goal at a proof state using the goal ID number and the proof state ID number. It is primarily for use by tools such as Prooftree that need to fetch goal history in this way. Prooftree is a tool for visualizing a proof as a tree that runs in Proof General.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Guarded`  
Some tactics (e.g. [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine)) allow to build proofs using fixpoint or cofixpoint constructions. Due to the incremental nature of proof construction, the check of the termination (or guardedness) of the recursive calls in the fixpoint or cofixpoint constructions is postponed to the time of the completion of the proof.

The command [`Guarded`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Guarded) allows checking if the guard condition for fixpoint and cofixpoint is violated at some time of the construction of the proof without having to wait the completion of the proof.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Validate Proof`  
Checks that the current partial proof is well-typed. It is useful for finding tactic bugs since without it, such errors will only be detected at [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) time.

It does not check the guard condition. Use [`Guarded`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Guarded) for that.

## Showing differences between proof steps

Coq can automatically highlight the differences between successive proof steps and between values in some error messages. Coq can also highlight differences in the proof term. For example, the following screenshots of CoqIDE and coqtop show the application of the same [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) tactic. The tactic creates two new hypotheses, highlighted in green. The conclusion is entirely in pale green because although it’s changed, no tokens were added to it. The second screenshot uses the "removed" option, so it shows the conclusion a second time with the old text, with deletions marked in red. Also, since the hypotheses are new, no line of old text is shown for them.

> ![CoqIDE with Set Diffs on](../../_images/diffs-coqide-on.png)

> ![CoqIDE with Set Diffs removed](../../_images/diffs-coqide-removed.png)

> ![coqtop with Set Diffs on](../../_images/diffs-coqtop-on3.png)

This image shows an error message with diff highlighting in CoqIDE:

> ![CoqIDE error message with diffs](../../_images/diffs-error-message.png)

### How to enable diffs

*Option* `Diffs "on""off""removed"`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) is used to enable diffs. The “on” setting highlights added tokens in green, while the “removed” setting additionally reprints items with removed tokens in red. Unchanged tokens in modified items are shown with pale green or red. Diffs in error messages use red and green for the compared values; they appear regardless of the setting. (Colors are user-configurable.)

For coqtop, showing diffs can be enabled when starting coqtop with the `-diffs on|off|removed` command-line option or by setting the [`Diffs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:opt.Diffs) option within Coq. You will need to provide the `-color on|auto` command-line option when you start coqtop in either case.

Colors for coqtop can be configured by setting the `COQ_COLORS` environment variable. See section [Environment variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/practical-tools/coq-commands.html#customization-by-environment-variables). Diffs use the tags `diff.added`, `diff.added.bg`, `diff.removed` and `diff.removed.bg`.

In CoqIDE, diffs should be enabled from the `View` menu. Don’t use the `Set Diffs` command in CoqIDE. You can change the background colors shown for diffs from the `Edit | Preferences | Tags` panel by changing the settings for the `diff.added`, `diff.added.bg`, `diff.removed` and `diff.removed.bg` tags.
