This panel also lets you control other attributes of the highlights, such as the foreground color, bold, italic, underline and strikeout.

Proof General, VsCoq and Coqtail can also display Coq-generated proof diffs automatically. Please see the PG documentation section ["Showing Proof Diffs"](https://proofgeneral.github.io/doc/master/userman/Coq-Proof-General#Showing-Proof-Diffs) and Coqtail's ["Proof Diffs"](https://github.com/whonore/Coqtail#proof-diffs) for details.

### How diffs are calculated

Diffs are calculated as follows:

1.  Select the old proof state to compare to, which is the proof state before the last tactic that changed the proof. Changes that only affect the view of the proof, such as `all: swap 1 2`, are ignored.

2.  For each goal in the new proof state, determine what old goal to compare it to—the one it is derived from or is the same as. Match the hypotheses by name (order is ignored), handling compacted items specially.

3.  For each hypothesis and conclusion (the “items”) in each goal, pass them as strings to the lexer to break them into tokens. Then apply the Myers diff algorithm [\[Mye86\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#myers) on the tokens and add appropriate highlighting.

Notes:

- Aside from the highlights, output for the "on" option should be identical to the undiffed output.

- Goals completed in the last proof step will not be shown even with the "removed" setting.

This screenshot shows the result of applying a [`split`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.split) tactic that replaces one goal with 2 goals. Notice that the goal `P 1` is not highlighted at all after the split because it has not changed.

> ![coqide with Set Diffs on with multiple goals](../../_images/diffs-coqide-multigoal.png)

Diffs may appear like this after applying a [`intro`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intro) tactic that results in a compacted hypotheses:

> ![coqide with Set Diffs on with compacted hypotheses](../../_images/diffs-coqide-compacted.png)

### "Show Proof" differences

To show differences in the proof term:

- In coqtop and Proof General, use the [`Show Proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Show-Proof) `Diffs` command.

- In CoqIDE, position the cursor on or just after a tactic to compare the proof term after the tactic with the proof term before the tactic, then select `View / Show Proof` from the menu or enter the associated key binding. Differences will be shown applying the current `Show Diffs` setting from the `View` menu. If the current setting is `Don't show diffs`, diffs will not be shown.

  Output with the "added and removed" option looks like this:

  > ![coqide with Set Diffs on with compacted hypotheses](../../_images/diffs-show-proof.png)

## Delaying solving unification constraints

*Tactic* `solve_constraints`  

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Solve Unification Constraints`  
By default, after each tactic application, postponed typechecking unification problems are resolved using heuristics. Unsetting this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) disables this behavior, allowing tactics to leave unification constraints unsolved. Use the [`solve_constraints`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.solve_constraints) tactic at any point to solve the constraints.

## Proof maintenance

*Experimental.* Many tactics, such as [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros), can automatically generate names, such as "H0" or "H1" for a new hypothesis introduced from a goal. Subsequent proof steps may explicitly refer to these names. However, future versions of Coq may not assign names exactly the same way, which could cause the proof to fail because the new names don't match the explicit references in the proof.

The following [`Mangle Names`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:flag.Mangle-Names) settings let users find all the places where proofs rely on automatically generated names, which can then be named explicitly to avoid any incompatibility. These settings cause Coq to generate different names, producing errors for references to automatically generated names.

*Flag* `Mangle Names`  
When this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) is set (it is off by default), generated names use the prefix specified in the following option instead of the default prefix.

<!-- -->

*Option* `Mangle Names Prefix string`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) specifies the prefix to use when generating names.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Mangle Names Light`  
When this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) is set (it is off by default), the names generated by [`Mangle Names`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:flag.Mangle-Names) only add the [`Mangle Names Prefix`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:opt.Mangle-Names-Prefix) to the original name.

## Controlling proof mode

*Option* `Hyps Limit natural`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) controls the maximum number of hypotheses displayed in goals after the application of a tactic. All the hypotheses remain usable in the proof development. When unset, it goes back to the default mode which is to print all available hypotheses.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Nested Proofs Allowed`  
When turned on (it is off by default), this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) enables support for nested proofs: a new assertion command can be inserted before the current proof is finished, in which case Coq will temporarily switch to the proof of this *nested lemma*. When the proof of the nested lemma is finished (with [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) or [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined)), its statement will be made available (as if it had been proved before starting the previous proof) and Coq will switch back to the proof of the previous assertion.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Printing Goal Names`  
When this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) is turned on, the name of the goal is printed in proof mode, which can be useful in cases of cross references between goals.

<!-- -->

*Flag* `Printing Goal Tags`  
Internal flag used to implement Proof General's proof-tree mode.

## Controlling memory usage

*Command* `Print Debug GC`  
Prints heap usage statistics, which are values from the `stat` type of the `Gc` module described [here](https://caml.inria.fr/pub/docs/manual-ocaml/libref/Gc.html#TYPEstat) in the OCaml documentation. The `live_words`, `heap_words` and `top_heap_words` values give the basic information. Words are 8 bytes or 4 bytes, respectively, for 64- and 32-bit executables.

When experiencing high memory usage the following commands can be used to force Coq to optimize some of its internal data structures.

*Command* `Optimize Proof`  
Shrink the data structure used to represent the current proof.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Optimize Heap`  
Perform a heap compaction. This is generally an expensive operation. See: [OCaml Gc.compact](http://caml.inria.fr/pub/docs/manual-ocaml/libref/Gc.html#VALcompact) There is also an analogous tactic [`optimize_heap`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.optimize_heap).

Memory usage parameters can be set through the [OCAMLRUNPARAM](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/practical-tools/coq-commands.html#ocamlrunparam) environment variable.

# Tactics

Tactics specify how to transform the [proof state](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-proof-state) of an incomplete proof to eventually generate a complete proof.

Proofs can be developed in two basic ways: In forward reasoning, the proof begins by proving simple statements that are then combined to prove the theorem statement as the last step of the proof. With forward reasoning, for example, the proof of `A /\ B` would begin with proofs of `A` and `B`, which are then used to prove `A /\ B`. Forward reasoning is probably the most common approach in human-generated proofs.

In backward reasoning, the proof begins with the theorem statement as the goal, which is then gradually transformed until every subgoal generated along the way has been proven. In this case, the proof of `A /\ B` begins with that formula as the goal. This can be transformed into two subgoals, `A` and `B`, followed by the proofs of `A` and `B`. Coq and its tactics primarily use backward reasoning.

A tactic may fully prove a goal, in which case the goal is removed from the proof state. More commonly, a tactic replaces a goal with one or more [subgoals](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-subgoal). (We say that a tactic reduces a goal to its subgoals.)

Most tactics require specific elements or preconditions to reduce a goal; they display error messages if they can't be applied to the goal. A few tactics, such as [`auto`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/auto.html#coq:tacn.auto), don't fail even if the proof state is unchanged.

Goals are identified by number. The current goal is number 1. Tactics are applied to the current goal by default. (The default can be changed with the [`Default Goal Selector`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:opt.Default-Goal-Selector) option.) They can be applied to another goal or to multiple goals with a [goal selector](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#goal-selectors) such as `2: `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic).

This chapter describes many of the most common built-in tactics. Built-in tactics can be combined to form tactic expressions, which are described in the [Ltac](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#ltac) chapter. Since tactic expressions can be used anywhere that a built-in tactic can be used, "tactic" may refer to both built-in tactics and tactic expressions.

## Common elements of tactics

### Reserved keywords

The tactics described in this chapter reserve the following keywords:

    by using

Thus, these keywords cannot be used as identifiers. It also declares the following character sequences as tokens:

    ** [= |-

### Invocation of tactics

Tactics may be preceded by a goal selector (see Section [Goal selectors](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#goal-selectors)). If no selector is specified, the default selector is used.

> ``` ebnf
> tactic_invocation        ::=     toplevel_selector : ? tactic .
> ```

*Option* `Default Goal Selector "toplevel_selector"`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) controls the default selector, used when no selector is specified when applying a tactic. The initial value is 1, hence the tactics are, by default, applied to the first goal.

Using value `all` will make it so that tactics are, by default, applied to every goal simultaneously. Then, to apply a tactic tac to the first goal only, you can write `1:tac`.

Using value `!` enforces that all tactics are used either on a single focused goal or with a local selector (’’strict focusing mode’’).

Although other selectors are available, only `all`, `!` or a single natural number are valid default goal selectors.

### Bindings

Tactics that take a term as an argument may also accept [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) to specify the values to assign unbound variables in a term. Bindings can be given by position or name. Generally these appear in the form [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings) or `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings), depending on the tactic.

> ``` ebnf
> one_term_with_bindings   ::=     one_term with bindings ?
> bindings                 ::=     one_term +
>                          |       ( ident  natural := term ) +
> ```

- [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings)`?` — bindings for variables in [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) are typically determined by unifying [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) with a tactic-dependent part of the context, with any remaining unbound variables provided by the [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings).

- [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)`+` — binds free variables in the left-to-right order of their first appearance in the relevant term.

  For some tactics, bindings for all free variables must be provided, such as for [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction), [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct), [`elim`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.elim) and [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case). Other tactics automatically generate some or all of the bindings from the conclusion or a hypothesis, such as [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) and [`constructor`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.constructor) and its variants. In this case, only instances for the [dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) that are not bound in the conclusion of the relevant term are required (and permitted).

- `( `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)``[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` )+` — binds variables by name (if [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is given), or by unifying with the `n`-th [premise](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-premise) of the relevant term (if [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is given).

*Error* `No such binder.`  
[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is 0 or more than the number of unbound variables.

<!-- -->

*Error* `No such bound variable ident (no bound variables at all in the expression).`  

<!-- -->

*Error* `No such bound variable ident1 (possible names are: ident2 ...).`  
The specified binder name [`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is not used in the [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). [`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` ...` lists all the valid binder names.

<!-- -->

*Error* `Not the right number of missing arguments (expected natural).`  
Generated when the first form of [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) doesn't have the expected number of arguments.

### Intro patterns

Intro patterns let you specify the name to assign to variables and hypotheses introduced by tactics. They also let you split an introduced hypothesis into multiple hypotheses or subgoals. Common tactics that accept intro patterns include [`assert`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.assert), [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) and [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct).

``` ebnf
intropattern             ::=     *
                         |       **
                         |       simple_intropattern
simple_intropattern      ::=     simple_intropattern_closed % term0 *
simple_intropattern_closed ::=   naming_intropattern
                         |       _
                         |       or_and_intropattern
                         |       equality_intropattern
naming_intropattern      ::=     ident
                         |       ?
                         |       ? ident
or_and_intropattern      ::=     [ intropattern * * | ]
                         |       ( simple_intropattern * , )
                         |       ( simple_intropattern * & )
equality_intropattern    ::=     ->
                         |       <-
                         |       [= intropattern * ]
```

Note that the intro pattern syntax varies between tactics. Most tactics use [`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern) in the grammar. [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct), [`edestruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.edestruct), [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction), [`einduction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.einduction), [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case), [`ecase`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.ecase) and the various [`inversion`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.inversion) tactics use [`or_and_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-or_and_intropattern), while [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) and [`eintros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eintros) use [`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern)`*`. The `eqn:` construct in various tactics uses [`naming_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-naming_intropattern).

**Naming patterns**

Use these elementary patterns to specify a name:

- [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) — use the specified name

- `?` — let Coq generate a fresh name

- `?`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) — generate a name that begins with [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)

- `_` — discard the matched part (unless it is required for another hypothesis)

- if a disjunction pattern omits a name, such as `[|H2]`, Coq will choose a name

**Splitting patterns**

The most common splitting patterns are:

- split a hypothesis in the form `A /\ B` into two hypotheses `H1: A` and `H2: B` using the pattern `(H1 & H2)` or `(H1, H2)` or `[H1 H2]`. [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-conj-ex). This also works on `A <-> B`, which is just a notation representing `(A -> B) /\ (B -> A)`.

- split a hypothesis in the form `A \/ B` into two subgoals using the pattern `[H1|H2]`. The first subgoal will have the hypothesis `H1: A` and the second subgoal will have the hypothesis `H2: B`. [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-disj-ex)

- split a hypothesis in either of the forms `A /\ B` or `A \/ B` using the pattern `[]`.

Patterns can be nested: `[[Ha|Hb] H]` can be used to split `(A \/ B) /\ C`.

Note that there is no equivalent to intro patterns for goals. For a goal `A /\ B`, use the [`split`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.split) tactic to replace the current goal with subgoals `A` and `B`. For a goal `A \/ B`, use [`left`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.left) to replace the current goal with `A`, or [`right`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.right) to replace the current goal with `B`.

- `( `[`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern)`+,` ) — matches a product over an inductive type with a [single constructor](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-cons-note). If the number of patterns equals the number of constructor arguments, then it applies the patterns only to the arguments, and `( `[`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern)`+, )` is equivalent to `[`[`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern)`+]`. If the number of patterns equals the number of constructor arguments plus the number of `let-ins`, the patterns are applied to the arguments and `let-in` variables.

- `( `[`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern)`+& )` — matches a right-hand nested term that consists of one or more nested binary inductive types such as `a1 OP1 a2 OP2 …` (where the `OPn` are right-associative). (If the `OPn` are left-associative, additional parentheses will be needed to make the term right-hand nested, such as `a1 OP1 (a2 OP2 …)`.) The splitting pattern can have more than 2 names, for example `(H1 & H2 & H3)` matches `A /\ B /\ C`. The inductive types must have a [single constructor with two parameters](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-cons-note). [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-ampersand-ex)

- `[ `[`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern)`*+| ]` — splits an inductive type that has [multiple constructors](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-cons-note) such as `A \/ B` into multiple subgoals. The number of [`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern)s must be the same as the number of constructors for the matched part.

- `[ `[`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern)`+ ]` — splits an inductive type that has a [single constructor with multiple parameters](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-cons-note) such as `A /\ B` into multiple hypotheses. Use `[H1 [H2 H3]]` to match `A /\ B /\ C`.

- `[]` — splits an inductive type: If the inductive type has multiple constructors, such as `A \/ B`, create one subgoal for each constructor. If the inductive type has a single constructor with multiple parameters, such as `A /\ B`, split it into multiple hypotheses.

**Equality patterns**

These patterns can be used when the hypothesis is an equality:

- `->` — replaces the right-hand side of the hypothesis with the left-hand side of the hypothesis in the conclusion of the goal; the hypothesis is cleared; if the left-hand side of the hypothesis is a variable, it is substituted everywhere in the context and the variable is removed. [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-rarrow-ex)

- `<-` — similar to `->`, but replaces the left-hand side of the hypothesis with the right-hand side of the hypothesis.

- `[= `[`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern)`*, ]` — If the product is over an equality type, applies either [`injection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.injection) or [`discriminate`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.discriminate). If [`injection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.injection) is applicable, the intropattern is used on the hypotheses generated by [`injection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.injection). If the number of patterns is smaller than the number of hypotheses generated, the pattern `?` is used to complete the list. [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-inj-discr-ex)

**Other patterns**

- `*` — introduces one or more [dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) from the result until there are no more. [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-star-ex)

- `**` — introduces one or more [dependent](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) or [non-dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-non-dependent-premise) from the result until there are no more premises. `intros **` is equivalent to `intros`. [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-2stars-ex)

- [`simple_intropattern_closed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern_closed)` % `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`*` — first applies each of the terms with the [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) tactic on the hypothesis to be introduced, then it uses [`simple_intropattern_closed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern_closed). [Example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropattern-injection-ex)

Note

`A \/ B` and `A /\ B` use infix notation to refer to the inductive types `or` and `and`. `or` has multiple constructors (`or_introl` and `or_intror`), while `and` has a single constructor (`conj`) with multiple parameters (`A` and `B`). These are defined in `theories/Init/Logic.v`. The "where" clauses define the infix notation for "or" and "and".

``` coq
Inductive or (A B:Prop) : Prop :=
  | or_introl : A -> A \/ B
  | or_intror : B -> A \/ B
where "A \/ B" := (or A B) : type_scope.

Inductive and (A B:Prop) : Prop :=
  conj : A -> B -> A /\ B
where "A /\ B" := (and A B) : type_scope.
```

Note

[`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) `p+` is not always equivalent to `intros p; … ; intros p` if some of the `p` are `_`. In the first form, all erasures are done at once, while they're done sequentially for each tactic in the second form. If the second matched term depends on the first matched term and the pattern for both is `_` (i.e., both will be erased), the first `intros` in the second form will fail because the second matched term still has the dependency on the first.

Examples:

> Example: intro pattern for /\\
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   H : A /\ B
>   ============================
>   True
>
> destruct H as (HA & HB).
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   HA : A
>   HB : B
>   ============================
>   True
> ```

> Example: intro pattern for \\
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   H : A \/ B
>   ============================
>   True
>
> destruct H as [HA|HB]. all: swap 1 2.
> 2 goals
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   HA : A
>   ============================
>   True
>
> goal 2 is:
>  True
>
> 2 goals
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   HB : B
>   ============================
>   True
>
> goal 2 is:
>  True
> ```

> Example: -\> intro pattern
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y, z : nat
>   H : x = y
>   ============================
>   y = z -> x = z
>
> intros ->.
> 1 goal
>
>   x, z : nat
>   H : x = z
>   ============================
>   x = z
> ```

> Example: \[=\] intro pattern
>
> The first [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) `[=]` uses [`injection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.injection) to strip `(S …)` from both sides of the matched equality. The second uses [`discriminate`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.discriminate) on the contradiction `1 = 2` (internally represented as `(S O) = (S (S O))`) to complete the goal.
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   n, m : nat
>   ============================
>   S n = S m -> 1 = 2 -> False
>
> intros [= H].
> 1 goal
>
>   n, m : nat
>   H : n = m
>   ============================
>   1 = 2 -> False
>
> intros [=].
> No more goals.
> ```

> Example: (A & B & …) intro pattern
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   A /\ (exists x : nat, B x /\ C) -> True
>
> intros (a & x & b & c).
> 1 goal
>
>   a : A
>   x : nat
>   b : B x
>   c : C
>   ============================
>   True
> ```

> Example: \* intro pattern
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   forall A B : Prop, A -> B
>
> intros *.
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   ============================
>   A -> B
> ```

> Example: \*\* pattern ("intros \*\*" is equivalent to "intros")
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   forall A B : Prop, A -> B
>
> intros **.
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   H : A
>   ============================
>   B
> ```
>
> Example: compound intro pattern
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   forall A B C : Prop, A \/ B /\ C -> (A -> C) -> C
>
> intros * [a | (_,c)] f.
> 2 goals
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   a : A
>   f : A -> C
>   ============================
>   C
>
> goal 2 is:
>  C
> 2 goals
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   c : C
>   f : A -> C
>   ============================
>   C
>
> goal 2 is:
>  C
> ```

> Example: combined intro pattern using \[=\] -\> and %
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A : Type
>   xs, ys : list A
>   ============================
>   S (length ys) = 1 -> xs ++ ys = xs
>
> intros [=->%length_zero_iff_nil].
> 1 goal
>
>   A : Type
>   xs : list A
>   ============================
>   xs ++ nil = xs
> ```
>
> - `intros` would add `H : S (length ys) = 1`
>
> - `intros [=]` would additionally apply [`injection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.injection) to `H` to yield `H0 : length ys = 0`
>
> - `intros [=->%length_zero_iff_nil]` applies the theorem, making H the equality `l=nil`, which is then applied as for `->`.
>
> ``` coq
> Theorem length_zero_iff_nil (l : list A):
>    length l = 0 <-> l=nil.
> ```
>
> The example is based on [Tej Chajed's coq-tricks](https://github.com/tchajed/coq-tricks/blob/8e6efe4971ed828ac8bdb5512c1f615d7d62691e/src/IntroPatterns.v)

### Occurrence clauses

An occurrence is a subterm of a goal or hypothesis that matches a pattern provided by a tactic. Occurrence clauses select a subset of the ocurrences in a goal and/or in one or more of its hypotheses.

> ``` ebnf
> occurrences              ::=     at occs_nums
>                          |       in goal_occurrences
> simple_occurrences       ::=     occurrences
> occs_nums                ::=     - ? nat_or_var +
> nat_or_var               ::=     natural  ident
> goal_occurrences         ::=     hyp_occs + , |- concl_occs ? ?
>                          |       * |- concl_occs ?
>                          |       |- concl_occs ?
>                          |       concl_occs ?
> hyp_occs                 ::=     hypident at occs_nums ?
> hypident                 ::=     ident
>                          |       ( type of ident )
>                          |       ( value of ident )
> concl_occs               ::=     * at occs_nums ?
> ```
>
> [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)  
> The first form of [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) selects occurrences in the conclusion of the goal. The second form can select occurrences in the goal conclusion and in one or more hypotheses.
>
> [`simple_occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_occurrences)  
> A semantically restricted form of [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) that doesn't allow the `at` clause anywhere within it.
>
> `-? `[`nat_or_var`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-nat_or_var)`+`  
> Selects the specified occurrences within a single goal or hypothesis. Occurrences are numbered starting with 1 following a depth-first traversal of the term's expression, including occurrences in [implicit arguments](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/implicit-arguments.html#implicitarguments) and [coercions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/implicit-coercions.html#coercions) that are not displayed by default. (Set the [`Printing All`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Printing-All) flag to show those in the printed term.)
>
> For example, when matching the pattern `_ + _` in the term `(a + b) + c`, occurrence 1 is `(…) + c` and occurrence 2 is `(a + b)`. When matching that pattern with term `a + (b + c)`, occurrence 1 is `a + (…)` and occurrence 2 is `b + c`.
>
> Specifying `-` includes all occurrences *except* the ones listed.
>
> [`hyp_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-hyp_occs)`*, |- `[`concl_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-concl_occs)`??`  
> Selects occurrences in the specified hypotheses and the specified occurrences in the conclusion.
>
> `* |- `[`concl_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-concl_occs)`?`  
> Selects all occurrences in all hypotheses and the specified occurrences in the conclusion.
>
> `|- `[`concl_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-concl_occs)`?`  
> Selects the specified occurrences in the conclusion.
>
> [`goal_occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-goal_occurrences)` ::= `[`concl_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-concl_occs)`?`  
> Selects all occurrences in all hypotheses and in the specified occurrences in the conclusion.
>
> [`hypident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-hypident)` at `[`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums)`?`  
> Omiting [`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums) selects all occurrences within the hypothesis.
>
> [`hypident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-hypident)` ::= `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)  
> Selects the hypothesis named [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).
>
> `( type of `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` )`  
> Selects the type part of the named hypothesis (e.g. `: nat`).
>
> `( value of `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` )`  
> Selects the value part of the named hypothesis (e.g. `:= 1`).
>
> [`concl_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-concl_occs)` ::= * at `[`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums)`?`  
> Selects occurrences in the conclusion. '\*' by itself selects all occurrences. [`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums) selects the specified occurrences.
>
> Use `in *` to select all occurrences in all hypotheses and the conclusion, which is equivalent to `in * |- *`. Use `* |-` to select all occurrences in all hypotheses.
>
> When rewriting in multiple hypotheses, they must not appear in the term to rewrite. For instance `rewrite H in H,H'` is an error. If an hypothesis appears only through a hole, it will be removed from that hole's context.
>
> With `rewrite term in *`, hypotheses on which the dependency cannot be avoided are skipped, for instance `rewrite H in *` skips rewriting in `H`. This is the case even if only one hypothesis ends up rewritten.
>
> If multiple occurrences are given, such as in [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite) `H at 1 2 3`, the tactic must match at least one occurrence in order to succeed. The tactic will fail if no occurrences match. Occurrence numbers that are out of range (e.g. `at 1 3` when there are only 2 occurrences in the hypothesis or conclusion) are ignored.
>
> Tactics that use occurrence clauses include [`set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.set), [`remember`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.remember), [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) and [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct).
>
> *Error* `No such hypothesis: ident.`  

See also

[Managing the local context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#managingthelocalcontext), [Case analysis](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#caseanalysisandinduction), [Printing constructions in full](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#printing-constructions-full).

## Applying theorems

*Tactic* `exact one_term`  
Directly gives the exact proof term for the goal. `exact p` succeeds if and only if [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) and the type of `p` are unifiable (see [Conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#conversion-rules)).

*Error* `Not an exact proof.`  

*Tactic* `eexact one_term`  
Behaves like [`exact`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact) but can handle terms and goals with existential variables.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `assumption`  
This tactic looks in the local context for a hypothesis whose type is convertible to the goal. If it is the case, the subgoal is proved. Otherwise, it fails.

*Error* `No such assumption.`  

*Tactic* `eassumption`  
Behaves like [`assumption`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.assumption) but is able to process goals and hypotheses with existential variables. It can also resolve existential variables, which [`assumption`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.assumption) will not.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `simple? notypeclasses? refine one_term`  
Behaves like [`exact`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact) but allows holes (denoted by `_` or `(_ : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)`)`) in [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) generates as many subgoals as there are remaining holes in the elaborated term. Any subgoal that occurs in other subgoals is automatically shelved, as if calling [`shelve_unifiable`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.shelve_unifiable).

`simple`  
If specified, don't shelve any subgoals or perform beta reduction.

`notypeclasses`  
If specified, do checking without resolving typeclasses. The generated subgoals (shelved or not) are *not* candidates for typeclass resolution, even if they have a typeclass type as their conclusion.

Example

``` coq
Inductive Option : Set :=
| Fail : Option
| Ok : bool -> Option.
Option is defined
Option_rect is defined
Option_ind is defined
Option_rec is defined
Option_sind is defined
1 goal

  ============================
  forall x : Option, x <> Fail -> bool
1 goal

  x : Option
  ============================
  Fail <> Fail -> bool
No more goals.
```

*Error* `Cannot infer a term for this placeholder.`  
There is a hole in the term you gave whose type cannot be inferred. Put a cast around it.

Setting [`Debug`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Debug) `"unification"` enables printing traces of unification steps used during elaboration/typechecking and the [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) tactic. `"ho-unification"` prints information about higher order heuristics.

*Tactic* `apply one_term_with_bindings+, in_hyp_as?`  
``` ebnf
in_hyp_as                ::=     in ident as_ipat ? + ,
as_ipat                  ::=     as simple_intropattern
```

Uses unification to match the type of each [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (in [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings)) with the goal (to do [backward reasoning](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#term-backward-reasoning)) or with a hypothesis (to do [forward reasoning](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#term-forward-reasoning)). Specifying multiple [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings) is equivalent to giving each one serially, left to right, as separate `apply` tactics.

The type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) contains zero or more [premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-premise) followed by a [conclusion](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#conclusion-meaning-2), i.e. it typically has the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? `[`term`<sub>`premise`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` ->* `[`term`<sub>`conclusion`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). (The `forall`s may also be interleaved with the premises, but common usage is to equivalently gather them at the beginning of the [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).) Backward reasoning with a [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) whose type is, for example, `A -> B` replaces an as-yet unproven goal `B` with `A`. Forward reasoning with the same [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) changes a hypothesis with type `A` to `B`. (Hypotheses are considered proven propositions within the context that contains them.)

Unification creates a map from the variables in the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) to matching subterms of the goal or hypothesis. The matching subterms are then substituted into the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) when generating the updated goal or hypothesis. Unmatched premises become new subgoals with similar substitutions. If no match is found, the tactic fails.

Setting [`Debug`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Debug) `"tactic-unification"` enables printing traces of unification steps in tactic unification. Tactic unification is used in tactics such as [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) and [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite).

The goal and hypothesis cases are described separately for clarity.

> [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (inside [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings))  
> If [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is an [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), it is the name of a theorem, lemma or hypothesis whose type is given in the theorem statement or shown in the context. Otherwise it is a proof term whose type can be displayed with [`Check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Check) [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).
>
> Without [`in_hyp_as`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-in_hyp_as) (the goal case)  
> If the goal matches all of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (both premises and the conclusion), the tactic proves the goal. Otherwise, the tactic matches the goal against the conclusion of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) and, if possible, one or more premises (from right to left). If the match succeeds, the tactic replaces the current goal with a subgoal for each unmatched premise of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). This [example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-backward) matches only the conclusion, while this [one](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-backward-w-premises) also matches a premise.
>
> If the conclusion of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) does not match the goal *and* the conclusion is an inductive type with a single constructor, then each premise in the constructor is recursively matched to the goal in right-to-left order and the first match is used. In this case, the tactic will not match premises that would result in applying a lemma of the form `forall A, … -> A`. See example [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-with-iff).

> > The goal case uses first-order unification with dependent types unless the conclusion of the type of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is of the form `P t`<sub>`1`</sub>` … t`<sub>`n`</sub> with `P` to be instantiated. In the latter case, the behavior depends on the form of the target. If the target is of the form `Q u`<sub>`1`</sub>` … u`<sub>`n`</sub> and the `t`<sub>`i`</sub> and `u`<sub>`i`</sub> unify, then `P` is instantiated into `Q`. Otherwise, [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) tries to define `P` by abstracting over `t`<sub>`1`</sub>` … t`<sub>`n`</sub> in the target. You can use [`pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.pattern) to transform the target so that it gets the form `(fun x`<sub>`1`</sub>` … x`<sub>`n`</sub>` => Q) u`<sub>`1`</sub>` … u`<sub>`n`</sub>. See the example [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#example-apply-pattern).
>
> [`in_hyp_as`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-in_hyp_as) (the hypothesis case)  
> Proceeding from *right to left*, find the first premise of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) that matches the specified hypothesis. If a match is found, the hypothesis is replaced with the conclusion of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (substituting for the unified variables) and the tactic creates a new subgoal for each unmatched premise. See the example [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-forward).
>
> If specified, `as `[`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern) is applied to the conclusion of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). In this case, the selected hypothesis is left unchanged if its name is not reused.
>
> If the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is an inductive type with a single constructor, then each premise in the constructor is recursively matched to the conclusion of the hypothesis in right-to-left order and the first match is used. See example [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-with-iff).
>
> For the hypothesis case, matching is done only with first-order unification.
>
> `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) (in [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings))  
> Gives explicit instantiations for variables used in the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). There are 3 cases:
>
> - Bindings for variables can be provided in a list of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s in the left-to-right order of their first appearance in the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). For the goal case ([example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-with-binding-goal)), the list should give bindings only for variables that aren't bound by unification. However, in the hypothesis case ([example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-with-binding-hyp)), the list must include bindings for *all* variables.
>
> - Bindings for unbound variables can be given by name with the `(`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)` form.
>
> - The form `(`[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)` binds additional variables by unifying the Nth premise of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) with [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). (Use `1` for the first premise.)
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Unable to unify one_term with one_term.`  
> The [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) tactic failed to match the conclusion of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). You can help [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) by transforming your goal with the [`change`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change) or [`pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.pattern) tactics.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Unable to apply lemma of type "..." on hypothesis of type "...".`  
> This happens if the conclusion of [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) does not match any of the premises of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `Unable to find an instance for the variables ident+.`  
> This occurs when some instantiations of the premises of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) are not deducible from the unification. This is the case, for instance, when you want to apply a transitivity property. To fix this, add bindings for the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s using to `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) or use [`eapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eapply).
>
> Example: Backward reasoning in the goal with `apply`
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   H : A -> B -> C
>   ============================
>   C
>
> apply H. (* replace goal with new goals for unmatched premises of H *)
> 2 goals
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   H : A -> B -> C
>   ============================
>   A
>
> goal 2 is:
>  B
> ```
>
> Example: Backward reasoning in the goal with `apply` including a premise
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   H : A -> B -> C
>   ============================
>   B -> C
>
> apply H. (* match on "B -> C", replace goal with "A" *)
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   H : A -> B -> C
>   ============================
>   A
> ```
>
> Example: Forward reasoning in hypotheses with `apply`
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   H0 : B
>   H1 : A -> B -> C
>   ============================
>   True
>
> apply H1 in H0. (* change H0, create new goals for unmatched premises of H1 *)
> 2 goals
>
>   A, B, C : Prop
>   H0 : C
>   H1 : A -> B -> C
>   ============================
>   True
>
> goal 2 is:
>  A
> ```
>
> Example: Apply a theorem with a binding in a goal
>
> [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) unifies the conclusion `n <= p` of the theorem `le_trans : forall n m p, n <= m -> m <= p -> n <= p` with the goal, assigning `x * x` and `y * y` in the goal to, repectively, `n` and `p` in theorem (backward reasoning). The `with` clause provides the binding for `m`:
>
> ``` coq
> Require Import PeanoNat.
>
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y : nat
>   H0 : x <= y
>   ============================
>   x * x <= y * y
>
> apply Nat.le_trans with (y * x).
> 2 goals
>
>   x, y : nat
>   H0 : x <= y
>   ============================
>   x * x <= y * x
>
> goal 2 is:
>  y * x <= y * y
> ```
>
> Example: Apply a theorem with a binding in a hypothesis
>
> When applying a theorem in a hypothesis, [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) unifies the hypothesis with one of the premises of the theorem `le_trans : forall n m p, n <= m -> m <= p -> n <= p`. In this case, it unifies with the first premise (`n <= m`) and assigns `x * x` and `y * y` to, respectively, `n` and `m` in the theorem (forward reasoning). The `with` clause provides the binding for `p`.
>
> In addition, [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) in a hypothesis isn't as flexible as [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) in the goal: for hypotheses, the unbound variable can be bound by name (as shown) or values for all the variables can be given positionally, i.e. `apply Nat.le_trans with (x * x) (y * y) (y * x) in H.`
>
> ``` coq
> Require Import PeanoNat.
>
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y : nat
>   H : x * x <= y * y
>   ============================
>   x <= y
>
> apply Nat.le_trans with (p := y * x) in H.
> 2 goals
>
>   x, y : nat
>   H : x * x <= y * x
>   ============================
>   x <= y
>
> goal 2 is:
>  y * y <= y * x
> ```
>
> Example: Applying theorems with `<->`
>
> `A <-> B` is defined as `(A -> B) /\ (B -> A)`. `/\` represents an inductive type with a single constructor: `Inductive and (C D:Prop) : Prop := conj : C -> D -> D /\ C`. The premises of `conj` are `C` and `D`. The tactic uses the first matching constructor premise in right-to-left order.
>
> Theorems that use `<->` to state a logical equivalence behave consistently when applied to goals and hypotheses.
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   H1 : A <-> B
>   H : A
>   ============================
>   A
>
> apply H1.
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   H1 : A <-> B
>   H : A
>   ============================
>   B
> 1 goal
>
>   A, B : Prop
>   H1 : A <-> B
>   H : B
>   ============================
>   B
> ```
>
> Example: Special case of second-order unification in apply
>
> Shows the use of the special case second-order unification described [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-with-second-order-unification) (after "unless").
>
> Note that we usually use [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) rather than applying `nat_ind` directly.
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y : nat
>   ============================
>   x + y = y + x
>
> Check nat_ind.
> nat_ind
>      : forall P : nat -> Prop,
>        P 0 -> (forall n : nat, P n -> P (S n)) -> forall n : nat, P n
> 2 goals
>
>   x, y : nat
>   ============================
>   x + y = 0
>
> goal 2 is:
>  forall n : nat, x + y = n -> x + y = S n
> (fun x y : nat => nat_ind (eq (x + y)) ?Goal ?Goal0 (y + x))
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y : nat
>   ============================
>   x + y = y + x
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y : nat
>   ============================
>   (fun n : nat => n + y = y + n) x
> 2 goals
>
>   x, y : nat
>   ============================
>   0 + y = y + 0
>
> goal 2 is:
>  forall n : nat, n + y = y + n -> S n + y = y + S n
> (fun x y : nat =>
>  nat_ind (fun n : nat => n + y = y + n) ?Goal ?Goal0 x : x + y = y + x)
> ```
>
> *Tactic* `eapply one_term_with_bindings+, in_hyp_as?`  
> Behaves like [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply), but creates [existential variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#existential-variables) when Coq is unable to deduce instantiations for variables, rather than failing.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Tactic* `rapply one_term`  
> Behaves like [`eapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eapply) but uses the proof engine of [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) to handle existential variables, holes and conversion problems. This may result in slightly different behavior regarding which conversion problems are solvable. However, [`rapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.rapply) fails if any holes remain in [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) itself after typechecking and typeclass resolution but before unification with the goal. Note that [`rapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.rapply) tries to instantiate as many hypotheses of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) as possible. As a result, if it is possible to apply [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) to arbitrarily many arguments without getting a type error, [`rapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.rapply) will loop.
>
> Note that you must `Require Import Coq.Program.Tactics` to use [`rapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.rapply).
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Tactic* `simple apply one_term_with_bindings+, in_hyp_as?`  
> Behaves like [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) but it reasons modulo conversion only on subterms that contain no variables to instantiate and does not traverse tuples. For instance, the following example fails because it would require converting `id ?foo` and `O`.
>
> Example
>
> ``` coq
> Definition id (x : nat) := x.
> id is defined
> H is declared
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   0 = 0
> The command has indeed failed with message:
> Unable to unify "id ?M150 = ?M151" with "0 = 0".
> ```
>
> Because it reasons modulo a limited amount of conversion, [`simple apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.simple-apply) fails faster than [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) and it is thus well-suited for use in user-defined tactics that backtrack often.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Tactic* `simple eapply one_term_with_bindings+, in_hyp_as?`  
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Tactic* `lapply one_term`  
> Splits a [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) in the goal reducible to the form `A -> B`, replacing it with two new subgoals `A` and `B -> G`. `lapply H` (where `H` is `A -> B` and `B` does not start with a product) is equivalent to [`cut`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.cut) `B. 2:apply H.`.
>
> *Error* `lapply needs a non-dependent product.`  

Example

Assume we have a transitive relation `R` on `nat`:

``` coq
Parameter R : nat -> nat -> Prop.
```

Consider the goal `(R n p)` provable using the transitivity of `R`:

``` coq
Goal R n p.
```

The direct application of `Rtrans` with `apply` fails because no value for `y` in `Rtrans` is found by `apply`:

``` coq
apply Rtrans.
Toplevel input, characters 6-12:
> apply Rtrans.
>       ^^^^^^
Error: Unable to find an instance for the variable y.
```

A solution is to `apply (Rtrans n m p)` or `(Rtrans n m)`.

``` coq
apply (Rtrans n m p).
2 goals

  ============================
  R n m

goal 2 is:
 R m p
```

Note that `n` can be inferred from the goal, so the following would work too.

``` coq
apply (Rtrans _ m).
```

More elegantly, `apply Rtrans with (y:=m)` allows only mentioning the unknown m:

``` coq
apply Rtrans with (y := m).
```

Another solution is to mention the proof of `(R x y)` in `Rtrans`

``` coq
apply Rtrans with (1 := Rnm).
1 goal

  ============================
  R m p
```

… or the proof of `(R y z)`.

``` coq
apply Rtrans with (2 := Rmp).
1 goal

  ============================
  R n m
```

On the opposite, one can use `eapply` which postpones the problem of finding `m`. Then one can apply the hypotheses `Rnm` and `Rmp`. This instantiates the existential variable and completes the proof.

``` coq
eapply Rtrans.
2 focused goals (shelved: 1)

  ============================
  R n ?y

goal 2 is:
 R ?y p
1 goal

  ============================
  R m p
No more goals.
```

## Managing the local context

*Tactic* `intro ident? where?`  
Applies the [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) tactic until it finds an item that can be introduced in the context by removing certain constructs in the goal. If no item is found, the tactic fails. The name used is [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) (if specified) or from the construct, except that if the name from the construct already exists in the [local context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-local-context), Coq uses a fresh name instead. The constructs have these forms: (See examples [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intro-examples).)

`forall x : T, `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)  
`x : T` is a [dependent premise](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise). Removes `forall x : T,` from the goal and adds `x : T` to the context.

`A -> …`  
`A` is a [non-dependent premise](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-non-dependent-premise). Removes `A ->` from the goal and adds `H : A` to the context.

`let x := c, `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)  
Removes `let x := c,` from the goal and adds `x := c : T` to the context.

> We recommend always specifying [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) so that the names of hypotheses don't change as the proof is updated, making your proof easier to maintain. For example, if H exists in the context, Coq will consider using `H0`, `H1`, ... until it finds an unused name. Modifications to a proof can change automatically assigned names that subsequent tactics likely refer to, making the proofs harder to maintain. The [`Mangle Names`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:flag.Mangle-Names) flag gives some control over how fresh names are generated (see [Proof maintenance](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#proof-maintenance)).
>
> Note that [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) lets you introduce multiple items into the context with a single tactic.
>
> [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)  
> The name to give to the introduced item. If not given, Coq uses the variable name from the `forall` or `H` for premises. If a name such as `H` is already in use, Coq will consider using `H0`, `H1`, ... until it finds a fresh name.
>
> Note
>
> If a hypothesis name hides the base name of a global constant then the latter can still be referred to by a qualified name (see [Qualified names](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#qualified-names)).
>
> [`where`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-where)  
> Indicates where to place the introduced hypothesis: at the top or bottom of the context or before or after another specified hypothesis. The default is `at bottom`.
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `ident is already used.`  
> The provided [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is already used in the [local context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-local-context).
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `No product even after head-reduction.`  
> There is nothing to introduce even after [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) has been completely applied.
>
> Example: `intro` and `intros`
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   forall m n : nat, m < n -> let x := 0 in True
>
> intro m.
> 1 goal
>
>   m : nat
>   ============================
>   forall n : nat, m < n -> let x := 0 in True
> 1 goal
>
>   m, n : nat
>   ============================
>   m < n -> let x := 0 in True
> 1 goal
>
>   m, n : nat
>   H : m < n
>   ============================
>   let x := 0 in True
> 1 goal
>
>   m, n : nat
>   H : m < n
>   x := 0 : nat
>   ============================
>   True
> ```
>
> This single `intros` tactic is equivalent to the 4 preceding `intro` tactics:
>
> ``` coq
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   forall m n : nat, m < n -> let x := 0 in True
>
> intros m n H x.
> 1 goal
>
>   m, n : nat
>   H : m < n
>   x := 0 : nat
>   ============================
>   True
> ```

*Tactic* `intros intropattern*`\
*Tactic* `intros until identnatural`  
The first form introduces zero or more items into the context from the constructs listed in [`intro`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intro). If [`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern) is not specified, the tactic introduces items until it reaches the [head constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head-constant); it never fails and may leave the context unchanged.

If [`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern) is specified, the [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) tactic is applied until it finds an item that can be introduced into the context. The [`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern) is often just a list of [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s, but other forms can also be specified in order to, for example, introduce all [dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) (`*`); introduce all dependent and [non-dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-non-dependent-premise) (`**`); split terms such as `A /\ B` (`[]`) and pick a fresh name with a given prefix (`?X`). See [Intro patterns](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropatterns).

The second form repeats `intro` until it has introduced a [dependent premise](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) with the name [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) or has introduced [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) [premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-premise) (like `A` in `A -> B`).

We recommend explicitly naming items with [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) instead of using `intros until `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural). See the explanation [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#warn-should-give-name-in-intro).

Example: intros until

``` coq
1 goal

  ============================
  forall x y : nat, x = y -> y = x

intros until y.
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  ============================
  x = y -> y = x
```

Or:

``` coq
1 goal

  ============================
  forall x y : nat, x = y -> y = x

intros until 1.
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  H : x = y
  ============================
  y = x
```

*Error* `No quantified hypothesis named ident in current goal even after head-reduction.`  
The [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the `until` clause doesn't appear as a [dependent premise](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise).

*Error* `No natural-th non dependent hypothesis in current goal even after head-reduction.`  
There are fewer than [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) premises in the goal.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `eintros intropattern*`  
Works just like [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) except that it creates existential variables for any unresolved variables rather than failing. Typically this happens when using a `%` intropattern (see [`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern)).

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `clear -? ident+?`  
Erases *unneeded* hypotheses from the context of the current goal. "Unneeded" means that the unselected hypotheses and the goal don't depend directly or indirectly on the erased hypotheses. That means the hypotheses will no longer appear in the context and therefore can't be used in subsequent proof steps. Note that erasing an uneeded hypothesis may turn a goal that was provable into an unprovable goal.

`clear`  
All unneeded hypotheses are erased. This may leave the context unchanged; this form never fails.

`clear `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+`  
Erases the named hypotheses if they are unneeded and fails otherwise.

> *Error* `ident is used in the conclusion.`  
>
> <!-- -->
>
> *Error* `ident is used in the hypothesis ident.`  

`clear - `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+`  
Selects all hypotheses that are not named by the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s, then erases those that are unneeded. This may leave the context unchanged; this form never fails as long as the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s name hypotheses in the context.

*Tactic* `clearbody ident+`  
This tactic expects [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+` to be [local definitions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) and clears their respective bodies. In other words, it turns the given definitions into assumptions.

*Error* `ident is not a local definition.`  

*Tactic* `clear dependent ident`  
Clears the hypothesis [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and all the hypotheses that depend on it.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `revert ident+`  
Moves the specified hypotheses and [local definitions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) to the goal, if this respects dependencies. This is the inverse of [`intro`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intro).

*Tactic* `revert dependent ident`  
Deprecated since version 8.18.

An alias for [`generalize dependent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.generalize-dependent).

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `move identfrom where`  
``` ebnf
where                    ::=     at top
                         |       at bottom
                         |       before ident
                         |       after ident
```

Moves a hypothesis [`ident`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and hypotheses that directly or indirectly refer to [`ident`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) that appear between [`ident`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). `at top` and `at bottom` are equivalent to giving the name of the first or last hypotheses in the context. The dependent hypotheses will appear after [`ident`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), appearing in dependency order. This lets users show and group hypotheses in the order they prefer. It doesn't change the goal or the proof term.

Note

Perhaps confusingly, "before" and "after" are interpeted with respect to the direction in which the hypotheses are moved rather than in the order of the resulting list of hypotheses. If [`ident`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is before [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the context, these notions are the same: for hypotheses `A B C`, `move A after B` gives `B A C`, whereas if [`ident`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is after [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the context, they are the opposite: `move C after A` gives `C A B` because the direction of movement is reversed.

*Error* `Cannot move identfrom after ident: it occurs in the type of ident.`
