*Error* `Cannot move identfrom after ident: it depends on ident.`  

Example: move

``` coq
1 goal

  x : nat
  Hx : x = 0
  y, z : nat
  Hy : y = y
  ============================
  0 = x

(*                    x Hx y z Hy *)
```

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `rename ident1 into ident2+,`  
Renames hypothesis [`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) into [`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) for each pair of [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s. Renaming is done simultaneously, which permits swapping the names of 2 hypotheses. (Note that the renaming is applied in the context and the existential variables, but the proof term doesn't change.)

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `set alias_definition occurrences?`\
*Tactic* `set one_term as_name? occurrences?`  
``` ebnf
alias_definition         ::=     ( ident simple_binder * := term )
simple_binder            ::=     name
                         |       ( name + : term )
as_name                  ::=     as ident
```

The first form adds a new local definition [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := …`. If [`simple_binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder) is not specified, the definition body is [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) and otherwise `fun `[`simple_binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder)`* => `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). Then the tactic replaces the body expression with the new variable [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the goal or as specified by [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences). The tactic may succeed and add the local definition even if no replacements are made.

The second form is equivalent to `set (`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)`) `[`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)`?` using [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), if present, or an auto-generated name if not provided.

If [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) or [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) has holes (i.e. subexpressions with the form “`_`”), the tactic first checks that all subterms matching the pattern are compatible before doing the replacement using the leftmost subterm matching the pattern.

*Error* `The variable ident is already declared.`  

Example: set with a [`simple_binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder)

`set` does a simple syntactic replacement in the goal:

``` coq
1 goal

  n : nat
  ============================
  n = 0

pattern n. (* without this, "set" won't replace anything in the goal *)
1 goal

  n : nat
  ============================
  (fun n0 : nat => n0 = 0) n
1 goal

  n : nat
  f := fun x : nat => x = 0 : nat -> Prop
  ============================
  f n
```

*Tactic* `eset alias_definition occurrences?`\
*Tactic* `eset one_term as_name? occurrences?`  
Similar to [`set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.set), but instead of failing because of uninstantiated variables, generates existential variables for them. In practice, this is relevant only when [`eset`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eset) is used as a synonym of [`epose`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.epose), i.e. when the [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) does not occur in the goal.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `remember one_term as_name? eqn : naming_intropattern? in goal_occurrences?`  
Similar to `set (`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)`) in *` but creates a hypothesis using [Leibniz equality](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-Leibniz-equality) to remember the relation between the introduced variable and the term rather than creating a [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition). If [`as_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_name) is not specified a fresh name is used. Use [`naming_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-naming_intropattern) to name the new equation.

*Tactic* `eremember one_term as_name? eqn : naming_intropattern? in goal_occurrences?`  
Similar to [`remember`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.remember), but instead of failing because of uninstantiated variables, generates existential variables for them.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `pose alias_definition`\
*Tactic* `pose one_term as_name?`  
Similar to [`set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.set). Adds a [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) to the context but without doing any replacement.

*Tactic* `epose alias_definition`\
*Tactic* `epose one_term as_name?`  
Similar to [`pose`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.pose), but instead of failing because of uninstantiated variables, generates existential variables for them.

## Controlling the proof flow

*Tactic* `assert ( ident : type ) by ltac_expr3?`\
*Tactic* `assert ( ident := term )`\
*Tactic* `assert one_type as_ipat? by ltac_expr3?`  
Adds a new hypothesis to the current subgoal and a new subgoal before it to prove the hypothesis. Then, if [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3) is specified, it applies that tactic to fully prove the new subgoal (and otherwise fails).

The first form adds a new hypothesis named [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) of type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type). (This corresponds to the cut rule of sequent calculus.)

The second form is equivalent to `assert (`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)`) by exact (`[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)` where [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) is the type of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). It is also equivalent to using [`pose proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.pose-proof). If the head of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), the tactic is equivalent to [`specialize`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.specialize).

In the third form, if [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) isn't specified, the tactic adds the hypothesis [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) with a fresh name. Otherwise, it transforms the hypothesis as specified by [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) and adds the resulting new hypotheses and goals. See [Intro patterns](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#intropatterns).

*Error* `The term "type" has type "type1" which should be Set, Prop or Type.`  
Occurs when the argument [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) (in the first form) or [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) (in the third form) is not of type `Prop`, `Set` nor `Type`.

*Error* `Proof is not complete.`  
[`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3) was not able to prove the new hypothesis.

*Tactic* `eassert ( ident : type ) by ltac_expr3?`\
*Tactic* `eassert ( ident := term )`\
*Tactic* `eassert one_type as_ipat? by ltac_expr3?`  
Unlike [`assert`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.assert), the [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type), [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) or [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) in [`eassert`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eassert) may contain holes, denoted by `_`, for which the tactic will create existential variables. This lets you avoid specifying the asserted statement completely before starting to prove it.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `enough ( ident : type ) by ltac_expr3?`\
*Tactic* `enough one_type as_ipat? by ltac_expr3?`  
Adds a new hypothesis to the current subgoal and a new subgoal after it to prove the hypothesis.

The first form adds a new hypothesis [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) and [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) as the new subgoal. Then, if [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3) is specified, it applies that tactic to prove the current subgoal with the added hypothesis (and otherwise fails).

In the second form, if [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) isn't specified, the tactic adds a new hypothesis [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) with a name chosen by Coq. Otherwise, it transforms [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) as specified by [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) and adds the resulting new hypotheses. The [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) may also expand the current subgoal into multiple subgoals. Then, if [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3) is specified, it is applied to and must succeed on all of them.

*Tactic* `eenough ( ident : type ) by ltac_expr3?`\
*Tactic* `eenough one_type as_ipat? by ltac_expr3?`  
Unlike [`enough`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.enough), the [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) and [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) in [`eenough`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eenough) may contain [holes](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#term-hole), denoted by `_`, for which the tactic will create existential variables. This lets you avoid specifying the asserted statement completely until you start to use the hypothesis or later start to prove the statement.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `cut one_type`  
Implements the non-dependent case of the [App](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/cic.html#app-rule) typing rule, the Modus Ponens inference rule. It is equivalent to `enough (`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`: `[`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type)`). revert `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`.` This tactic is generally considered obsolete but it is still widely used in old scripts.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `pose proof term as_ipat?`\
*Tactic* `pose proof ( ident := term )`  
The first form behaves like `assert `[`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type)` `[`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat)`? by exact `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) where [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) is the type of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

The second form is equivalent to `assert (`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)`)`.

*Tactic* `epose proof term as_ipat?`\
*Tactic* `epose proof ( ident := term )`  
While [`pose proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.pose-proof) expects that no existential variables are generated by the tactic, [`epose proof`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.epose-proof) removes this constraint.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `specialize one_term_with_bindings as_ipat?`  
Specializes a term (typically a hypothesis or a lemma) by applying arguments to it.

*First*, the tactic generates a modified term: If the [head constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head-constant) of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (in [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings)) has the type `forall ...`, the tactic replaces one or more of the quantified variables in the type with arguments provided by [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings), either in the form of a [function application](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#function-application) (which may be partial), such as `(H 1)`, or with named or numbered binders, such as `H with (n:=1)`.

If the [head constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head-constant) has a [non-dependent product](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-non-dependent-product) type such as `A -> B -> C`, the tactic eliminates one or more of the premises (doing [forward reasoning](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#term-forward-reasoning)).

Uninstantiated arguments are inferred by unification, if possible, or otherwise left quantified in the resulting term.

*Then*, If the [head constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head-constant) is a hypothesis `H`, the resulting term replaces that hypothesis. Specifying [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) will leave the original hypothesis unchanged and will introduce new hypotheses as specified by the [`simple_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_intropattern). If `H` appears in the conclusion or another hypothesis, you must use [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) to give a fresh hypothesis name.

If the head constant is a lemma or theorem, the resulting term is added as a new premise of the goal so that the behavior is similar to that of [`generalize`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.generalize). In this case, you can use [`as_ipat`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_ipat) to immediately introduce the modified term as one or more hypotheses.

*Error* `Cannot change ident, it is used in hypothesis ident.`  

*Error* `Cannot change ident, it is used in conclusion.`  

Example: partial application in [`specialize`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.specialize)

``` coq
1 goal

  H : forall n m : nat, n + m = m + n
  ============================
  True

specialize (H 1). (* equivalent to: specialize H with (n := 1) *)
1 goal

  H : forall m : nat, 1 + m = m + 1
  ============================
  True
```

Example: [`specialize`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.specialize) with a non-dependent product

Compare this to a similar [example](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#apply-forward) that uses [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply). [`specialize`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.specialize) won't introduce new goals as [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) can.

``` coq
1 goal

  A, B, C : Prop
  H0 : B
  H1 : A -> B -> C
  ============================
  True

specialize H1 with (2:=H0).
1 goal

  A, B, C : Prop
  H0 : B
  H1 : A -> C
  ============================
  True
```

*Tactic* `specialize_eqs ident`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `generalize one_term+`\
*Tactic* `generalize pattern_occs as_name?+,`  
For each [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (which may be in the [`pattern_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-pattern_occs)), replaces the goal `G` with `forall (x:T), G'`, where [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is a subterm of `G` of type `T` and `G'` is obtained by replacing all occurrences of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) with `x` within `G`. `x` is a fresh variable chosen based on `T`. Specifying multiple [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s is equivalent to `generalize `[`one_term`<sub>`n`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)`; … ; generalize `[`one_term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). (Note they are processed *right to left*.)

[`as_name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-as_name)  
The name to use for `x` instead of a fresh name.

Example

``` coq
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  ============================
  0 <= x + y + y

generalize (x + y + y). (* get a simpler goal that can be proven by induction *)
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  ============================
  forall n : nat, 0 <= n
```

*Tactic* `generalize dependent one_term`  
Generalizes [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) and all hypotheses that depend on [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). It clears the generalized hypotheses.

*Tactic* `dependent generalize_eqs ident`  

*Tactic* `dependent generalize_eqs_vars ident`  

*Tactic* `generalize_eqs ident`  

*Tactic* `generalize_eqs_vars ident`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `evar ( ident : type )`\
*Tactic* `evar one_type`  
The `evar` tactic creates a new [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) named [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with type [`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type) or [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) in the context. The body of this binding is a fresh existential variable. If the second form is used, Coq chooses the name.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `instantiate ( ident := term )`\
*Tactic* `instantiate ( natural := term ) hloc?`  
``` ebnf
hloc                     ::=     in |- *
                         |       in ident
                         |       in ( type of ident )
                         |       in ( value of ident )
```

The first form refines (see [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine)) an existential variable [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with the term [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). It is equivalent to `only [`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`]: refine `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

Note

To be able to refer to an existential variable by name, the user must have given the name explicitly (see [Existential variables](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/evars.html#existential-variables)).

Note

When you are referring to hypotheses which you did not name explicitly, be aware that Coq may make a different decision on how to name the variable in the current goal and in the context of the existential variable. This can lead to surprising behaviors.

The second form refines an existential variable selected by its position. The [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) argument is the position of the existential variable *from right to left* in the goal. (Use the [`hloc`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-hloc) clause to select an existential variable in a hypothesis.) Counting starts at 1 and multiple occurrences of the same existential variable are counted multiple times. Using this form is discouraged because slight changes to the goal may change the needed index, causing a maintenance issue.

Advanced users may want to define and use an Ltac tactic to get more consistent behavior, such as:

``` coq
Ltac instantiate_ltac_variable ev term :=
  let H := fresh in
  pose ev as H;
  instantiate (1 := term) in (value of H);
  clear H.
```

`in `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)  
Selects the hypothesis [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

`in |- *`  
Selects the goal. This is the default behavior.

`in ( type of `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` )`  
Selects existential variables in the type of the [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). (The body is not included.)

`in ( value of `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` )`  
Selects existential variables in the body of the [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). (The type is not included.)

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `absurd one_type`  
[`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) is any proposition `P` of type `Prop`. This tactic applies False elimination, that is it deduces the current goal from False, and generates as subgoals `∼P` and `P`. It is very useful in proofs by cases, where some cases are impossible. In most cases, `P` or `∼P` is one of the hypotheses of the local context.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `contradiction one_term_with_bindings?`  
Tries to prove the current goal by finding a contradiction.

If [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings) is not provided (the most common use case), the tactic first does an [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros). The tactic then proves the goal if

- the updated context has a pair of hypotheses where one is the negation of the other (e.g. `P` and not `~P`), or

- there is a hypothesis with an empty inductive type (e.g. `False`), or

- there is a hypothesis `~P` where `P` is a singleton inductive type (e.g. `True` or `x=x`) provable by `Goal P. constructor.`

If [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings) is provided, its type must be a negation, such as `~P`, or an empty inductive type, such as `False`. If the type is a negation and `P` is a hypothesis in the context, the goal is proven. If the type is a negation and `P` is not in the context, the goal is replaced with `P`. If the type is `False` or another empty inductive type, the goal is proven. Otherwise the tactic fails. (If there is a hypothesis `P` and you want to replace the goal with `~P`, use the [`contradict`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.contradict) tactic. If there are hypotheses `H1 : P` and `H2 : ~P`, use `contradiction` without arguments or `contradiction H2` since `contradiction H1` won't work.)

Use the [`discriminate`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.discriminate) tactic to prove the current goal when there is a hypothesis with an impossible structural equality such as `0 = 1`.

Example: [`contradiction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.contradiction) tactic

Simple examples. To see more detail, add `intros` after each `Goal`.

``` coq
Inductive F :=. (* Another empty inductive type *)
```

Apply a fact from the standard library:

``` coq
Require Import Arith.

intros.
1 goal

  A : Prop
  H : 0 < 0
  ============================
  A
No more goals.
```

*Tactic* `contradict ident`  
Transforms the specified hypothesis [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and the goal in order to prove that the hypothesis is false. For `contradict H`, the current goal and context are transformed as shown. (For brevity, `⊢` is used to separate hypotheses from the goal; it is equivalent to the dividing line shown in a context.):

- `H: ~A ⊢ B` becomes `⊢ A`

- `H: ~A ⊢ ~B` becomes `H: B ⊢ A`

- `H: A ⊢ B` becomes `⊢ ~A`

- `H: A ⊢ ~B` becomes `H: B ⊢ ~A`

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `exfalso`  
Implements the “ex falso quodlibet” logical principle: an elimination of False is performed on the current goal, and the user is then required to prove that False is indeed provable in the current context.

## Classical tactics

In order to ease the proving process, when the `Classical` module is loaded, a few more tactics are available. Make sure to load the module using the [`Require Import`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Require-Import) command.

*Tactic* `classical_left`\
*Tactic* `classical_right`  
These tactics are the analog of [`left`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.left) and [`right`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.right) but using classical logic. They can only be used for disjunctions. Use [`classical_left`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.classical_left) to prove the left part of the disjunction with the assumption that the negation of right part holds. Use [`classical_right`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.classical_right) to prove the right part of the disjunction with the assumption that the negation of left part holds.

## Performance-oriented tactic variants

*Tactic* `exact_no_check one_term`  
For advanced usage. Similar to [`exact`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact) [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), but as an optimization, it skips checking that [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) has the goal's type, relying on the kernel check instead. See [`change_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change_no_check) for more explanation.

Example

``` coq
Goal False.
1 goal

  ============================
  False
No more goals.
The command has indeed failed with message:
The term "I" has type "True" while it is expected to have type "False".
```

*Tactic* `vm_cast_no_check one_term`  
For advanced usage. Similar to [`exact_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact_no_check) [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), but additionally instructs the kernel to use [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) to compare the goal's type with the [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)'s type.

Example

``` coq
Goal False.
1 goal

  ============================
  False
No more goals.
The command has indeed failed with message:
The term "I" has type "True" while it is expected to have type "False".
```

*Tactic* `native_cast_no_check one_term`  
for advanced usage. similar to [`exact_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.exact_no_check) [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), but additionally instructs the kernel to use [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) to compare the goal's type with the [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)'s type.

Example

``` coq
Goal False.
1 goal

  ============================
  False
No more goals.
The command has indeed failed with message:
Native compiler is disabled, falling back to VM conversion test.
[native-compiler-disabled,native-compiler,default]
```

# Reasoning with equalities

There are multiple notions of equality in Coq:

- Leibniz equality is the standard way to define equality in Coq and the Calculus of Inductive Constructions, which is in terms of a binary relation, i.e. a binary function that returns a `Prop`. The standard library defines `eq` similar to this:

  > ``` coq
  > Inductive eq {A : Type} (x : A) : A -> Prop := eq_refl : eq x x.
  > ```

  The notation `x = y` represents the term `eq x y`. The notation `x = y :> A` gives the type of x and y explicitly.

- Setoid equality defines equality in terms of an equivalence relation. A setoid is a set that is equipped with an equivalence relation (see <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Setoid>). These are needed to form a quotient set or quotient (see <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equivalence_class>). In Coq, users generally work with setoids rather than constructing quotients, for which there is no specific support.

- Definitional equality is equality based on the [conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#conversion-rules), which Coq can determine automatically. When two terms are definitionally equal, Coq knows it can replace one with the other, such as with [`change`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change) `X with Y`, among many other advantages. "[Convertible](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-convertible)" is another way of saying that two terms are definitionally equal.

Tactics for dealing with equality of inductive types such as [`injection`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.injection) and [`inversion`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.inversion) are described [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#equality-inductive-types).

## Tactics for simple equalities

*Tactic* `reflexivity`  
For a goal with the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? t = u`, verifies that `t` and `u` are [definitionally equal](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-definitional-equality), and if so, solves the goal (by applying `eq_refl`). If not, it fails.

The tactic may also be applied to goals with the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? R `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) where `R` is a reflexive relation registered with the `Equivalence` or `Reflexive` typeclasses. See [`Class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/type-classes.html#coq:cmd.Class) and [`Instance`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/type-classes.html#coq:cmd.Instance).

*Error* `The relation ident is not a declared reflexive relation. Maybe you need to require the Coq.Classes.RelationClasses library`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `symmetry simple_occurrences?`  
Changes a goal that has the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? t = u` into `u = t`. [`simple_occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_occurrences) may be used to apply the change in the selected hypotheses and/or the conclusion.

The tactic may also be applied to goals with the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? R `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) where `R` is a symmetric relation registered with the `Equivalence` or `Symmetric` typeclasses. See [`Class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/type-classes.html#coq:cmd.Class) and [`Instance`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/type-classes.html#coq:cmd.Instance).

*Error* `The relation ident is not a declared symmetric relation. Maybe you need to require the Coq.Classes.RelationClasses library`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `transitivity one_term`  
Changes a goal that has the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? t = u` into the two subgoals `t = `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) and [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` = u`.

The tactic may also be applied to goals with the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? R `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) where `R` is a transitive relation registered with the `Equivalence` or `Transitivity` typeclasses. See [`Class`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/type-classes.html#coq:cmd.Class) and [`Instance`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/type-classes.html#coq:cmd.Instance).

*Tactic* `etransitivity`  
This tactic behaves like [`transitivity`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.transitivity), using a fresh evar instead of a concrete [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).

*Error* `The relation ident is not a declared transitive relation. Maybe you need to require the Coq.Classes.RelationClasses library`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `f_equal`  
For a goal with the form `f a`<sub>`1`</sub>` ... a`<sub>`n`</sub>` = g b`<sub>`1`</sub>` ... b`<sub>`n`</sub>, creates subgoals `f = g` and `a`<sub>`i`</sub>` = b`<sub>`i`</sub> for the `n` arguments. Subgoals that can be proven by [`reflexivity`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.reflexivity) or [`congruence`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/logic.html#coq:tacn.congruence) are solved automatically.

## Rewriting with Leibniz and setoid equality

*Tactic* `rewrite oriented_rewriter+, occurrences? by ltac_expr3?`  
``` ebnf
oriented_rewriter        ::=     ->  <- ? natural ? ?  ! ? one_term_with_bindings
```

Replaces subterms with other subterms that have been proven to be equal. The type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) must have the form:

> `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? EQ `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)

where `EQ` is the [Leibniz equality](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-Leibniz-equality) `eq` or a registered [setoid equality](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-setoid-equality). Note that `eq `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is typically written with the infix notation [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` = `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). You must `Require Setoid` to use the tactic with a setoid equality or with [setoid rewriting](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#generalizedrewriting).

`rewrite `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) finds subterms matching [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) in the goal, and replaces them with [`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) (or the reverse if `<-` is given). Some of the variables `x`<sub>i</sub> are solved by unification, and some of the types `A`<sub>`1`</sub>`, …, A`<sub>`n`</sub> may become new subgoals. [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite) won't find occurrences inside `forall` that refer to variables bound by the `forall`; use the more advanced [`setoid_rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#coq:tacn.setoid_rewrite) if you want to find such occurrences.

[`oriented_rewriter`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-oriented_rewriter)`+,`  
The [`oriented_rewriter`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-oriented_rewriter)s are applied sequentially to the first goal generated by the previous [`oriented_rewriter`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-oriented_rewriter). If any of them fail, the tactic fails.

`-><-?`  
For `->` (the default), [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is rewritten into [`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). For `<-`, [`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is rewritten into [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`? ?!?`  
[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is the number of rewrites to perform. If `?` is given, [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is the maximum number of rewrites to perform; otherwise [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) is the exact number of rewrites to perform.

`?` (without [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)) performs the rewrite as many times as possible (possibly zero times). This form never fails. `!` (without [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)) performs the rewrite as many times as possible and at least once. The tactic fails if the requested number of rewrites can't be performed. [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)` !` is equivalent to [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural).

[`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)  
If [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) specifies multiple occurrences, the tactic succeeds if any of them can be rewritten. If not specified, only the first occurrence in the conclusion is replaced.

Note

If `at `[`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums) is specified, rewriting is always done with [setoid rewriting](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#generalizedrewriting), even for Leibniz equality, which means that you must `Require Setoid` to use that form. However, note that [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite) (even when using setoid rewriting) and [`setoid_rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#coq:tacn.setoid_rewrite) don't behave identically (as is noted above and below).

`by `[`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3)  
If specified, is used to resolve all side conditions generated by the tactic.

Note

For each selected hypothesis and/or the conclusion, [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite) finds the first matching subterm in depth-first search order. Only subterms identical to that first matched subterm are rewritten. If the `at` clause is specified, only these subterms are considered when counting occurrences. To select a different set of matching subterms, you can specify how some or all of the free variables are bound by using a `with` clause (see [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings)).

For instance, if we want to rewrite the right-hand side in the following goal, this will not work:

``` coq
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  ============================
  x + y = y + x

rewrite Nat.add_comm at 2.
Toplevel input, characters 0-25:
> rewrite Nat.add_comm at 2.
> ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Error: Invalid occurrence number: 2.
```

One can explicitly specify how some variables are bound to match a different subterm:

``` coq
rewrite Nat.add_comm with (m := x).
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  ============================
  x + y = x + y
```

Note that the more advanced [`setoid_rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#coq:tacn.setoid_rewrite) tactic behaves differently, and thus the number of occurrences available to rewrite may differ between the two tactics.

*Error* `Tactic failure: Setoid library not loaded.`  

*Error* `Cannot find a relation to rewrite.`  

*Error* `Tactic generated a subgoal identical to the original goal.`  

*Error* `Found no subterm matching term in ident.`\
*Error* `Found no subterm matching term in the current goal.`  
This happens if [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) does not occur in, respectively, the named hypothesis or the goal.

*Tactic* `erewrite oriented_rewriter+, occurrences? by ltac_expr3?`  
Works like [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite), but turns unresolved bindings, if any, into existential variables instead of failing. It has the same parameters as [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite).

*Flag* `Keyed Unification`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) makes higher-order unification used by [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite) rely on a set of keys to drive unification. The subterms, considered as rewriting candidates, must start with the same key as the left- or right-hand side of the lemma given to rewrite, and the arguments are then unified up to full reduction.

*Command* `Declare Equivalent Keys one_term one_term`  

*Command* `Print Equivalent Keys`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `rewrite * -><-? one_term in ident? at rewrite_occs? by ltac_expr3?`\
*Tactic* `rewrite * -><-? one_term at rewrite_occs in ident by ltac_expr3?`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `replace one_termfrom with one_termto occurrences? by ltac_expr3?`\
*Tactic* `replace -><-? one_termfrom occurrences?`  
The first form replaces all free occurrences of [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) in the current goal with [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) and generates an equality [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` = `[`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) as a subgoal. (Note the generated equality is reversed with respect to the order of the two terms in the tactic syntax; see issue [\#13480](https://github.com/coq/coq/issues/13480).) When `by `[`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3) is not present, this equality is automatically solved if it occurs among the hypotheses, or if its symmetric form occurs.

The second form, with `->` or no arrow, replaces [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) with [`term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) using the first hypothesis whose type has the form [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` = `[`term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). If `<-` is given, the tactic uses the first hypothesis with the reverse form, i.e. [`term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` = `[`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).

[`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)  
The `type of` and `value of` forms are not supported. Note you must `Require Setoid` to use the `at` clause in [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences).

`by `[`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3)  
Applies the [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3) to solve the generated equality.

*Error* `Terms do not have convertible types.`  

*Tactic* `cutrewrite -><-? one_type in ident?`  
Where [`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type) is an equality.

Deprecated since version 8.5: Use [`replace`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.replace) instead.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `substitute -><-? one_term_with_bindings`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `subst ident*`  
For each [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), in order, for which there is a hypothesis in the form [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) or [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` = `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), replaces [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) everywhere in the hypotheses and the conclusion and clears [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and the hypothesis from the context. If there are multiple hypotheses that match the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), the first one is used. If no [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is given, replacement is done for all hypotheses in the appropriate form in top to bottom order.

If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) of the form [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), it is also unfolded and cleared.

If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a section variable it must have no indirect occurrences in the goal, i.e. no global declarations implicitly depending on the section variable may be present in the goal.

Note

If the hypothesis is itself dependent in the goal, it is replaced by the proof of reflexivity of equality.

*Flag* `Regular Subst Tactic`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) controls the behavior of [`subst`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.subst). When it is activated (it is by default), [`subst`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.subst) also deals with the following corner cases:

- A context with ordered hypotheses [`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = `[`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and [`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = t`, or `t′ = `[`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with `t′` not a variable, and no other hypotheses of the form [`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = u` or `u = `[`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident); without the flag, a second call to subst would be necessary to replace [`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) by `t` or `t′` respectively.

- The presence of a recursive equation which without the flag would be a cause of failure of [`subst`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.subst).

- A context with cyclic dependencies as with hypotheses [`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = f `[`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and [`ident`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = g `[`ident`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) which without the flag would be a cause of failure of [`subst`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.subst).

Additionally, it prevents a [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) such as [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := t` from being unfolded which otherwise would exceptionally unfold in configurations containing hypotheses of the form [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` = u`, or `u′ = `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with `u′` not a variable. Finally, it preserves the initial order of hypotheses, which without the flag it may break.

*Error* `Cannot find any non-recursive equality over ident.`  

*Error* `Section variable ident occurs implicitly in global declaration qualid present in hypothesis ident.`\
*Error* `Section variable ident occurs implicitly in global declaration qualid present in the conclusion.`  
Raised when the variable is a section variable with indirect dependencies in the goal. If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a section variable, it must not have any indirect occurrences in the goal, i.e. no global declarations implicitly depending on the section variable may be present in the goal.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `simple subst`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `stepl one_term by ltac_expr?`  
For chaining rewriting steps. It assumes a goal in the form `R `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) where `R` is a binary relation and relies on a database of lemmas of the form `forall x y z, R x y -> eq x z -> R z y` where `eq` is typically a setoid equality. The application of `stepl `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) then replaces the goal by `R `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) and adds a new goal stating `eq `[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` `[`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

If [`ltac_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr) is specified, it is applied to the side condition.

*Command* `Declare Left Step one_term`  
Adds [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) to the database used by [`stepl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.stepl).

This tactic is especially useful for parametric setoids which are not accepted as regular setoids for [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite) and [`setoid_replace`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#coq:tacn.setoid_replace) (see [Generalized rewriting](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/addendum/generalized-rewriting.html#generalizedrewriting)).

*Tactic* `stepr one_term by ltac_expr?`  
This behaves like [`stepl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.stepl) but on the right hand side of the binary relation. Lemmas are expected to be in the form `forall x y z, R x y -> eq y z -> R x z`.

*Command* `Declare Right Step one_term`  
Adds [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) to the database used by [`stepr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.stepr).

## Rewriting with definitional equality

*Tactic* `change one_termfrom at occs_nums? with? one_termto occurrences?`  
Replaces terms with other [convertible](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-convertible) terms. If [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is not specified, then [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) replaces the conclusion and/or the specified hypotheses. If [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is specified, the tactic replaces occurrences of [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) within the conclusion and/or the specified hypotheses.

[`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` at `[`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums)`? with?`  
Replaces the occurrences of [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) specified by [`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums) with [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term), provided that the two [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s are convertible. [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) may contain pattern variables such as `?x`, whose value which will substituted for `x` in [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term), such as in `change (f ?x ?y) with (g (x, y))` or `change (fun x => ?f x) with f`.

The `at … with …` form is deprecated in 8.14; use `with … at …` instead. For `at … with … in H |-`, use `with … in H at … |-`.

[`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)  
If `with` is not specified, [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) must only specify entire hypotheses and/or the goal; it must not include any `at `[`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums) clauses.

*Error* `Not convertible.`  

*Error* `Found an "at" clause without "with" clause`  

*Tactic* `now_show one_type`  
A synonym for `change `[`one_type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_type). It can be used to make some proof steps explicit when refactoring a proof script to make it readable.

See also

[Applying conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#applyingconversionrules)

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `change_no_check one_termfrom at occs_nums? with? one_termto occurrences?`  
For advanced usage. Similar to [`change`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change), but as an optimization, it skips checking that [`one_term`<sub>`to`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is convertible with the goal or [`one_term`<sub>`from`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).

Recall that the Coq kernel typechecks proofs again when they are concluded to ensure correctness. Hence, using [`change`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change) checks convertibility twice overall, while [`change_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change_no_check) can produce ill-typed terms, but checks convertibility only once. Hence, [`change_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change_no_check) can be useful to speed up certain proof scripts, especially if one knows by construction that the argument is indeed convertible to the goal.

In the following example, [`change_no_check`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change_no_check) replaces `False` with `True`, but [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) then rejects the proof, ensuring consistency.

Example

``` coq
Goal False.
1 goal

  ============================
  False
1 goal

  ============================
  True
No more goals.
Toplevel input, characters 0-4:
> Qed.
> ^^^^
Error:
The term "I" has type "True" while it is expected to have type "False".
```

Example

``` coq
Goal True -> False.
1 goal

  ============================
  True -> False
1 goal

  H : True
  ============================
  False
1 goal

  H : False
  ============================
  False
No more goals.
Toplevel input, characters 0-4:
> Qed.
> ^^^^
Error:
The term "fun H : True => H" has type "True -> True"
while it is expected to have type "True -> False".
```

## Applying conversion rules

These tactics apply reductions and expansions, replacing [convertible](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-convertible) subterms with others that are equal by definition in CIC. They implement different specialized uses of the [`change`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change) tactic. Other ways to apply these reductions are through the [`Eval`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Eval) command, the `Eval` clause in the [`Definition`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Definition)/[`Example`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Example) command and the [`eval`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.eval) tactic.

Tactics described in this section include:

- [`lazy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.lazy) and [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv), which allow precise selection of which reduction rules to apply

- [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) and [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn), which are "clever" tactics meant to give the most readable result

- [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) and [`red`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.red), which apply reduction rules only to the head of the term

- [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) and [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute), which are performance-oriented.

Conversion tactics, with two exceptions, only change the types and contexts of existential variables and leave the proof term unchanged. (The [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) and [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) tactics change existential variables in a way similar to other conversions while also adding a single explicit cast to the proof term to tell the kernel which reduction engine to use. See [Type cast](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#type-cast).) For example:

> ``` coq
> Goal 3 + 4 = 7.
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   3 + 4 = 7
> ?Goal
> Existential 1 = ?Goal : [ |- 3 + 4 = 7]
> 1 goal
>
>   ============================
>   7 = 7
> (?Goal : 3 + 4 = 7)
> Existential 1 = ?Goal : [ |- 7 = 7]
> ```

*Tactic* `lazy reductions? simple_occurrences`\
*Tactic* `cbv reductions? simple_occurrences`  
``` ebnf
reductions               ::=     reduction +
                         |       head ? delta_reductions
reduction                ::=     head
                         |       beta
                         |       delta delta_reductions ?
                         |       match
                         |       fix
                         |       cofix
                         |       iota
                         |       zeta
delta_reductions         ::=     - ? [ reference + ]
```

Normalize the goal as specified by [`reductions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reductions). If no reductions are specified by name, all reductions are applied. If any reductions are specified by name, then only the named reductions are applied. The reductions include:

`head`  
Do only head reduction, without going under binders. Supported by [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl), [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv), [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) and [`lazy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.lazy). If this is the only specified reduction, all other reductions are applied.

`beta`  
[beta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-beta-reduction) of functional application

`delta `[`delta_reductions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-delta_reductions)`?`  
[delta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-delta-reduction): unfolding of transparent constants, see [Controlling reduction strategies and the conversion algorithm](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#controlling-the-reduction-strategies). The form in [`reductions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reductions) without the keyword `delta` includes `beta`, `iota` and `zeta` reductions in addition to `delta` using the given [`delta_reductions`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-delta_reductions).

`-? [ `[`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference)`+ ]`  
without the `-`, limits delta unfolding to the listed constants. If the `-` is present, unfolding is applied to all constants that are not listed. Notice that the `delta` doesn't apply to variables bound by a let-in construction inside the term itself (use `zeta` to inline these). Opaque constants are never unfolded except by [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) and [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) (see [\#4476](https://github.com/coq/coq/issues/4476) and [Controlling reduction strategies and the conversion algorithm](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#controlling-the-reduction-strategies)).

`iota`  
[iota-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-iota-reduction) of pattern matching (`match`) over a constructed term and reduction of `fix` and `cofix` expressions. Shorthand for `match fix cofix`.

`zeta`  
[zeta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-zeta-reduction): reduction of [let-in definitions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#let-in)

Normalization is done by first evaluating the head of the expression into weak-head normal form, i.e. until the evaluation is blocked by a variable, an opaque constant, an axiom, such as in `x u`<sub>`1`</sub>` … u`<sub>`n`</sub>, `match x with … end`, `(fix f x {struct x} := …) x`, a constructed form (a \\\lambda\\-expression, constructor, cofixpoint, inductive type, product type or sort) or a redex for which flags prevent reduction of the redex. Once a weak-head normal form is obtained, subterms are recursively reduced using the same strategy.

There are two strategies for reduction to weak-head normal form: *lazy* (the [`lazy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.lazy) tactic), or *call-by-value* (the [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv) tactic). The lazy strategy is a [call by need](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaluation_strategy#Call_by_need) strategy, with sharing of reductions: the arguments of a function call are weakly evaluated only when necessary, and if an argument is used several times then it is weakly computed only once. This reduction is efficient for reducing expressions with dead code. For instance, the proofs of a proposition `exists x. P(x)` reduce to a pair of a witness `t` and a proof that `t` satisfies the predicate `P`. Most of the time, `t` may be computed without computing the proof of `P(t)`, thanks to the lazy strategy.

*Flag* `Kernel Term Sharing`  
Turning this flag off disables the sharing of computations in [`lazy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.lazy), making it a call-by-name reduction. This also affects the reduction procedure used by the kernel when typechecking. By default sharing is activated.

The call-by-value strategy is the one used in ML languages: the arguments of a function call are systematically weakly evaluated first. The lazy strategy is similar to how Haskell reduces terms. Although the lazy strategy always does fewer reductions than the call-by-value strategy, the latter is generally more efficient for evaluating purely computational expressions (i.e. with little dead code).

*Tactic* `compute delta_reductions? simple_occurrences`  
A variant form of [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv).

Setting [`Debug`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Debug) `"Cbv"` makes [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv) (and its derivative [`compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.compute)) print information about the constants it encounters and the unfolding decisions it makes.
