*Tactic* `simpl head? delta_reductions? reference_occspattern_occs? simple_occurrences`  
``` ebnf
reference_occs           ::=     reference at occs_nums ?
pattern_occs             ::=     one_term at occs_nums ?
```

Reduces a term to something still readable instead of fully normalizing it. It performs a sort of strong normalization with two key differences:

- It unfolds constants only if they lead to an ι-reduction, i.e. reducing a match or unfolding a fixpoint.

- When reducing a constant unfolding to (co)fixpoints, the tactic uses the name of the constant the (co)fixpoint comes from instead of the (co)fixpoint definition in recursive calls.

[`occs_nums`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occs_nums)  
Selects which occurrences of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) to process (counting from left to right on the expression printed using the [`Printing All`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Printing-All) flag)

[`simple_occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_occurrences)  
Permits selecting whether to reduce the conclusion and/or one or more hypotheses. While the `at` option of [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) is not allowed here, [`reference_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reference_occs) and [`pattern_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-pattern_occs) have a somewhat less flexible `at` option for selecting specific occurrences.

[`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) can unfold transparent constants whose name can be reused in recursive calls as well as those designated by [`Arguments`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#coq:cmd.Arguments) [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference)` … /` commands. For instance, a constant `plus' := plus` may be unfolded and reused in recursive calls, but a constant such as `succ := plus (S O)` is not unfolded unless it was specifically designated in an [`Arguments`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#coq:cmd.Arguments) command such as `Arguments succ /.`.

[`reference_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reference_occs)``[`pattern_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-pattern_occs) can limit the application of [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) to:

- applicative subterms whose [head](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head) is the constant [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) or is the constant used in the notation [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string) (see [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference))

- subterms matching a pattern [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `cbn reductions? simple_occurrences`  
[`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) was intended to be a more principled, faster and more predictable replacement for [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl).

The main difference between [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) and [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) is that [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) may unfold constants even when they cannot be reused in recursive calls: in the previous example, `succ t` is reduced to `S t`.

Setting [`Debug`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Debug) `"RAKAM"` makes [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) print various debugging information. `RAKAM` is the Refolding Algebraic Krivine Abstract Machine.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `hnf simple_occurrences`  
Replaces the current goal with its weak-head normal form according to the βδιζ-reduction rules, i.e. it reduces the [head](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head) of the goal until it becomes a product or an irreducible term. All inner βι-redexes are also reduced. While [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) behaves similarly to [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) and [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn), unlike them, it does not recurse into subterms. The behavior of [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) can be tuned using the [`Arguments`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#coq:cmd.Arguments) command.

Example: The term `fun n : nat => S n + S n` is not reduced by `hnf`.

Note

The δ rule only applies to transparent constants (see [Controlling reduction strategies and the conversion algorithm](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#controlling-the-reduction-strategies) on transparency and opacity).

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `red simple_occurrences`  
βιζ-reduces the [head constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head-constant) of `T`, if possible, in the selected hypotheses and/or the goal which have the form:

> `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? T`

(where `T` does not begin with a `forall`) to `c t`<sub>`1`</sub>` … t`<sub>`n`</sub> where `c` is a constant. If `c` is transparent then it replaces `c` with its definition and reduces again until no further reduction is possible.

In the term `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? t`<sub>`1`</sub>` ... t`<sub>`n`</sub>, where `t`<sub>`1`</sub> is not a [`term_application`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-term_application), `t`<sub>`1`</sub> is the head of the term. In a term with the form `forall `[`open_binders`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-open_binders)` ,? c t`<sub>`1`</sub>` ... t`<sub>`n`</sub>, where `c` is a [constant](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#term-constant), `c` is the head constant.

*Error* `No head constant to reduce.`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `unfold reference_occs+, occurrences?`  
Applies [delta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-delta-reduction) to the constants specified by each [`reference_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reference_occs). The selected hypotheses and/or goals are then reduced to βιζ-normal form. Use the general reduction tactics if you want to only apply the δ rule, for example [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv) `delta [ `[`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference)` ]`.

[`reference_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reference_occs)  
If [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) is a [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid), it must be a defined transparent constant or [local definition](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-context-local-definition) (see [Top-level definitions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#gallina-definitions) and [Controlling reduction strategies and the conversion algorithm](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#controlling-the-reduction-strategies)).

If [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) is a [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string)` `[`scope_key`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/user-extensions/syntax-extensions.html#grammar-token-scope_key)`?`, the [`string`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-string) is the discriminating symbol of a notation (e.g. "+") or an expression defining a notation (e.g. `"_ + _"`) and the notation is an application whose head symbol is an unfoldable constant, then the tactic unfolds it.

[`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)  
If [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) is specified, the specified occurrences will be replaced in the selected hypotheses and/or goal. Otherwise every occurrence of the constants in the goal is replaced. If multiple [`reference_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reference_occs) are given, any `at` clauses must be in the [`reference_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-reference_occs) rather than in [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences).

*Error* `Cannot turn inductiveconstructor into an evaluable reference.`  
Occurs when trying to unfold something that is defined as an inductive type (or constructor) and not as a definition.

Example

``` coq
Goal 0 <= 1.
1 goal

  ============================
  0 <= 1
Toplevel input, characters 7-9:
> unfold le.
>        ^^
Error: Cannot turn inductive le into an evaluable reference.
```

*Error* `ident is opaque.`  
Raised if you are trying to unfold a definition that has been marked opaque.

Example

``` coq
Opaque Nat.add.
1 goal

  ============================
  1 + 0 = 1
Toplevel input, characters 0-14:
> unfold Nat.add.
> ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Error: Nat.add is opaque.
```

*Error* `Bad occurrence number of qualid.`  

*Error* `qualid does not occur.`

*Tactic* `fold one_term+ simple_occurrences`  
First, this tactic reduces each [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) using the [`red`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.red) tactic. Then, every occurrence of the resulting terms in the selected hypotheses and/or goal will be replaced by its associated [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). This tactic is particularly useful for reversing undesired unfoldings, which may make the goal very hard to read. The undesired unfoldings may be due to the limited capabilities of other reduction tactics. On the other hand, when an unfolded function applied to its argument has been reduced, the [`fold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.fold) tactic doesn't do anything.

[`fold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.fold) [`one_term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)` `[`one_term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) is equivalent to `fold `[`one_term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)`; fold `[`one_term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).

Example: [`fold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.fold) doesn't always undo [`unfold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.unfold)

``` coq
Goal ~0=0.
1 goal

  ============================
  0 <> 0
1 goal

  ============================
  0 = 0 -> False
```

This [`fold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.fold) doesn't undo the preceeding [`unfold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.unfold) (it makes no change):

``` coq
fold not.
1 goal

  ============================
  0 = 0 -> False
```

However, this [`pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.pattern) followed by [`fold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.fold) does:

``` coq
pattern (0 = 0).
1 goal

  ============================
  (fun P : Prop => P -> False) (0 = 0)
1 goal

  ============================
  0 <> 0
```

Example: Use [`fold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.fold) to reverse unfolding of `fold_right`

``` coq
Goal forall x xs, fold_right and True (x::xs).
1 goal

  ============================
  forall (x : Prop) (xs : list Prop), fold_right and True (x :: xs)
1 goal

  ============================
  forall (x : Prop) (xs : list Prop),
  x /\
  (fix fold_right (l : list Prop) : Prop :=
     match l with
     | nil => True
     | b :: t => b /\ fold_right t
     end) xs
1 goal

  ============================
  forall (x : Prop) (xs : list Prop), x /\ fold_right and True xs
```

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `pattern pattern_occs+, occurrences?`  
Performs beta-expansion (the inverse of [beta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-beta-reduction)) for the selected hypotheses and/or goals. The [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s in [`pattern_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-pattern_occs) must be free subterms in the selected items. The expansion is done for each selected item `T` for a set of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s in the [`pattern_occs`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-pattern_occs) by:

- replacing all selected occurrences of the [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s in `T` with fresh variables

- abstracting these variables

- applying the abstracted goal to the [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term)s

For instance, if the current goal `T` is expressible as `φ(t`<sub>`1`</sub>` … t`<sub>`n`</sub>`)` where the notation captures all the instances of the `t`<sub>`i`</sub> in φ, then [`pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.pattern) `t`<sub>`1`</sub>`, …, t`<sub>`n`</sub> generates the equivalent goal `(fun (x`<sub>`1`</sub>`:A`<sub>`1`</sub>` … (x`<sub>`n`</sub>`:A`<sub>`n`</sub>`) => φ(x`<sub>`1`</sub>` … x`<sub>`n`</sub>`)) t`<sub>`1`</sub>` … t`<sub>`n`</sub>. If `t`<sub>`i`</sub> occurs in one of the generated types `A`<sub>`j`</sub> (for `j > i`), occurrences will also be considered and possibly abstracted.

This tactic can be used, for instance, when the tactic [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) fails on matching or to better control the behavior of [`rewrite`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.rewrite).

See the example [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#example-apply-pattern).

### Fast reduction tactics: vm_compute and native_compute

[`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) is a brute-force but efficient tactic that first normalizes the terms before comparing them. It is based on a bytecode representation of terms similar to the bytecode representation used in the ZINC virtual machine [\[Ler90\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#leroy90). It is especially useful for intensive computation of algebraic values, such as numbers, and for reflection-based tactics.

[`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) is based on on converting the Coq code to OCaml.

Note that both these tactics ignore [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque) markings (see issue [\#4776](https://github.com/coq/coq/issues/4776)), nor do they apply unfolding strategies such as from [`Strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Strategy).

[`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) is typically two to five times faster than [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) at applying conversion rules when Coq is running native code, but [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) requires considerably more overhead. We recommend using [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) when all of the following are true (otherwise use [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute)):

- the running time in [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute) at least 5-10 seconds

- the size of the input term is small (e.g. hand-generated code rather than automatically-generated code that may have nested destructs on inductives with dozens or hundreds of constructors)

- the output is small (e.g. you're returning a boolean, a natural number or an integer rather than a large abstract syntax tree)

These tactics change existential variables in a way similar to other conversions while also adding a single explicit cast (see [Type cast](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#type-cast)) to the proof term to tell the kernel which reduction engine to use.

*Tactic* `vm_compute reference_occspattern_occs? occurrences?`  
Evaluates the goal using the optimized call-by-value evaluation bytecode-based virtual machine described in [\[GregoireL02\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#compiledstrongreduction). This algorithm is dramatically more efficient than the algorithm used for the [`cbv`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbv) tactic, but it cannot be fine-tuned. It is especially useful for full evaluation of algebraic objects. This includes the case of reflection-based tactics.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `native_compute reference_occspattern_occs? occurrences?`  
Evaluates the goal by compilation to OCaml as described in [\[BDenesGregoire11\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#fullreduction). Depending on the configuration, this tactic can either default to [`vm_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.vm_compute), recompile dependencies or fail due to some missing precompiled dependencies, see [the native-compiler option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/practical-tools/coq-commands.html#native-compiler-options) for details.

*Flag* `NativeCompute Timing`  
This [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) causes all calls to the native compiler to print timing information for the conversion to native code, compilation, execution, and reification phases of native compilation. Timing is printed in units of seconds of wall-clock time.

*Flag* `NativeCompute Profiling`  
On Linux, if you have the `perf` profiler installed, this [flag](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-flag) makes it possible to profile [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) evaluations.

*Option* `NativeCompute Profile Filename string`  
This [option](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#term-option) specifies the profile output; the default is `native_compute_profile.data`. The actual filename used will contain extra characters to avoid overwriting an existing file; that filename is reported to the user. That means you can individually profile multiple uses of [`native_compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.native_compute) in a script. From the Linux command line, run `perf report` on the profile file to see the results. Consult the `perf` documentation for more details.

### Computing in a term: eval and Eval

Evaluation of a term can be performed with:

*Tactic* `eval red_expr in term`  
``` ebnf
red_expr                 ::=     lazy reductions ?
                         |       cbv reductions ?
                         |       compute delta_reductions ?
                         |       vm _ compute reference_occs  pattern_occs ?
                         |       native _ compute reference_occs  pattern_occs ?
                         |       red
                         |       hnf
                         |       simpl head ? delta_reductions ? reference_occs  pattern_occs ?
                         |       cbn reductions ?
                         |       unfold reference_occs + ,
                         |       fold one_term +
                         |       pattern pattern_occs + ,
                         |       ident
```

[`eval`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.eval) is a [`value_tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-value_tactic). It returns the result of applying the conversion rules specified by [`red_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-red_expr). It does not change the proof state.

The [`red_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-red_expr) alternatives that begin with a keyword correspond to the tactic with the same name, though in several cases with simpler syntax than the tactic. [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a named reduction expression created with [`Declare Reduction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Declare-Reduction).

See also

Section [Applying conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#applyingconversionrules).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Eval red_expr in term`  
Performs the specified reduction on [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) and displays the resulting term with its type. If a proof is open, [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) may reference hypotheses of the selected goal. [`Eval`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Eval) is a [`query_command`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-query_command), so it may be prefixed with a goal selector.

*Command* `Compute term`  
Evaluates [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) using the bytecode-based virtual machine. It is a shortcut for [`Eval`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Eval) `vm_compute in `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). [`Compute`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Compute) is a [`query_command`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-query_command), so it may be prefixed with a goal selector.

<!-- -->

*Command* `Declare Reduction ident := red_expr`  
Declares a short name for the reduction expression [`red_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-red_expr), for instance `lazy beta delta [foo bar]`. This short name can then be used in `Eval `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` in` or `eval` constructs. This command accepts the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) attribute, which indicates that the reduction will be discarded at the end of the file or module. The name is not qualified. In particular declaring the same name in several modules or in several functor applications will be rejected if these declarations are not local. The name [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) cannot be used directly as an Ltac tactic, but nothing prevents the user from also performing a `Ltac `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`red_expr`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-red_expr).

## Controlling reduction strategies and the conversion algorithm

The commands to fine-tune the reduction strategies and the lazy conversion algorithm are described in this section. Also see [Effects of Arguments on unfolding](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/extensions/arguments-command.html#args-effect-on-unfolding), which supports additional fine-tuning.

*Command* `Opaque reference+`  
Marks the specified constants as [opaque](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-opaque) so tactics won't [unfold](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-unfold) them with [delta-reduction](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-delta-reduction). "Constants" are items defined by commands such as [`Definition`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/definitions.html#coq:cmd.Definition), [`Let`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/sections.html#coq:cmd.Let) (with an explicit body), [`Fixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#coq:cmd.Fixpoint), [`CoFixpoint`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/coinductive.html#coq:cmd.CoFixpoint) and [`Function`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/funind.html#coq:cmd.Function).

This command accepts the [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) attribute. By default, the scope of [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque) is limited to the current section or module.

[`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque) also affects Coq's conversion algorithm, causing it to delay unfolding the specified constants as much as possible when it has to check that two distinct applied constants are convertible. See Section [Conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#conversion-rules).

<!-- -->

*Command* `Transparent reference+`  
The opposite of [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque), it marks the specified constants as [transparent](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/conversion.html#term-transparent) so that tactics may unfold them. See [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque) above.

This command accepts the [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global) attribute. By default, the scope of [`Transparent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Transparent) is limited to the current section or module.

Note that constants defined by proofs ending with [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) are irreversibly opaque; [`Transparent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Transparent) will not make them transparent. This is consistent with the usual mathematical practice of *proof irrelevance*: what matters in a mathematical development is the sequence of lemma statements, not their actual proofs. This distinguishes lemmas from the usual defined constants, whose actual values are of course relevant in general.

*Error* `The reference qualid was not found in the current environment.`  
There is no constant named [`qualid`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#grammar-token-qualid) in the environment.

See also

[Applying conversion rules](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#applyingconversionrules), [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) and [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined)

*Command* `Strategy strategy_level [ reference+ ]+`  
``` ebnf
strategy_level           ::=     opaque
                         |       integer
                         |       expand
                         |       transparent
```

Generalizes the behavior of the [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque) and [`Transparent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Transparent) commands. It is used to fine-tune the strategy for unfolding constants, both at the tactic level and at the kernel level. This command associates a [`strategy_level`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#grammar-token-strategy_level) with the qualified names in the [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) sequence. Whenever two expressions with two distinct [head constants](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-head-constant) are compared (for example, typechecking `f x` where `f : A -> B` and `x : C` will result in converting `A` and `C`), the one with lower level is expanded first. In case of a tie, the second one (appearing in the cast type) is expanded.

This command accepts the [`local`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.local) attribute, which limits its effect to the current section or module, in which case the section and module behavior is the same as [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque) and [`Transparent`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Transparent) (without [`global`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/modules.html#coq:attr.global)).

Levels can be one of the following (higher to lower):

> - `opaque` : level of opaque constants. They cannot be expanded by tactics (behaves like +∞, see next item).
>
> - [`integer`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-integer) : levels indexed by an integer. Level 0 corresponds to the default behavior, which corresponds to transparent constants. This level can also be referred to as `transparent`. Negative levels correspond to constants to be expanded before normal transparent constants, while positive levels correspond to constants to be expanded after normal transparent constants.
>
> - `expand` : level of constants that should be expanded first (behaves like −∞)
>
> - `transparent` : Equivalent to level 0

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Strategy reference`  
This command prints the strategy currently associated with [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference). It fails if [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) is not an unfoldable reference, that is, neither a variable nor a constant.

*Error* `The reference is not unfoldable.`  

<!-- -->

*Command* `Print Strategies`  
Print all the currently non-transparent strategies.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `with_strategy strategy_level_or_var [ reference+ ] ltac_expr3`  
``` ebnf
strategy_level_or_var    ::=     strategy_level
                         |       ident
```

Executes [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3), applying the alternate unfolding behavior that the [`Strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Strategy) command controls, but only for [`ltac_expr3`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#grammar-token-ltac_expr3). This can be useful for guarding calls to reduction in tactic automation to ensure that certain constants are never unfolded by tactics like [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) and [`cbn`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.cbn) or to ensure that unfolding does not fail.

Example

``` coq
Opaque id.
1 goal

  ============================
  id 10 = 10
The command has indeed failed with message:
id is opaque.
1 goal

  ============================
  10 = 10
```

Warning

Use this tactic with care, as effects do not persist past the end of the proof script. Notably, this fine-tuning of the conversion strategy is not in effect during [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) nor [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined), so this tactic is most useful either in combination with [`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract), which will check the proof early while the fine-tuning is still in effect, or to guard calls to conversion in tactic automation to ensure that, e.g., [`unfold`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.unfold) does not fail just because the user made a constant [`Opaque`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:cmd.Opaque).

This can be illustrated with the following example involving the factorial function.

``` coq
Fixpoint fact (n : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 1
  | S n' => n * fact n'
  end.
```

Suppose now that, for whatever reason, we want in general to unfold the `id` function very late during conversion:

``` coq
Strategy 1000 [id].
```

If we try to prove `id (fact n) = fact n` by [`reflexivity`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.reflexivity), it will now take time proportional to \\n!\\, because Coq will keep unfolding `fact` and `*` and `+` before it unfolds `id`, resulting in a full computation of `fact n` (in unary, because we are using `nat`), which takes time \\n!\\. We can see this cross the relevant threshold at around \\n = 9\\:

``` coq
Goal True.
1 goal

  ============================
  True
Finished transaction in 0.498 secs (0.306u,0.179s) (successful)
1 goal

  H : id (fact 8) = fact 8
  ============================
  True
Finished transaction in 1.566 secs (1.533u,0.003s) (successful)
1 goal

  H : id (fact 8) = fact 8
  H0 : id (fact 9) = fact 9
  ============================
  True
```

Note that behavior will be the same if you mark `id` as `Opaque` because while most reduction tactics refuse to unfold `Opaque` constants, conversion treats `Opaque` as merely a hint to unfold this constant last.

We can get around this issue by using [`with_strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.with_strategy):

``` coq
Goal True.
1 goal

  ============================
  True
The command has indeed failed with message:
Timeout!
Finished transaction in 0.002 secs (0.001u,0.s) (successful)
1 goal

  H : id (fact 100) = fact 100
  ============================
  True
```

However, when we go to close the proof, we will run into trouble, because the reduction strategy changes are local to the tactic passed to [`with_strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.with_strategy).

``` coq
exact I.
No more goals.
Toplevel input, characters 0-18:
> Timeout 1 Defined.
> ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Error: Timeout!
```

We can fix this issue by using [`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract):

``` coq
Goal True.
1 goal

  ============================
  True
Finished transaction in 0.005 secs (0.005u,0.s) (successful)
1 goal

  H : id (fact 100) = fact 100
  ============================
  True
No more goals.
Finished transaction in 0.001 secs (0.001u,0.s) (successful)
```

On small examples this sort of behavior doesn't matter, but because Coq is a super-linear performance domain in so many places, unless great care is taken, tactic automation using [`with_strategy`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.with_strategy) may not be robustly performant when scaling the size of the input.

Warning

In much the same way this tactic does not play well with [`Qed`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Qed) and [`Defined`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Defined) without using [`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract) as an intermediary, this tactic does not play well with `coqchk`, even when used with [`abstract`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:tacn.abstract), due to the inability of tactics to persist information about conversion hints in the proof term. See [\#12200](https://github.com/coq/coq/issues/12200) for more details.

# Reasoning with inductive types

## Applying constructors

The tactics presented here specialize [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) and [`eapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eapply) to constructors of inductive types.

*Tactic* `constructor nat_or_var? with bindings?`  
First does `repeat intro; hnf` on the goal. If the result is an inductive type `I`, then apply the appropriate constructor(s), and otherwise fail. If [`nat_or_var`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-nat_or_var) is specified and has the value `i`, it uses `apply c`<sub>`i`</sub>, where `c`<sub>`i`</sub> is the i-th constructor of `I`. If not specified, the tactic tries all the constructors, which can result in more than one success (e.g. for `\/`) when using backtracking tactics such as `constructor; ...`. See [`ltac-seq`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.ltac-seq).

`with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings)`?`  
If specified, the `apply` is done as `apply … with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings).

Warning

The terms in [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) are checked in the context where constructor is executed and not in the context where [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply) is executed (the introductions are not taken into account).

*Error* `Not an inductive product.`  

*Error* `Not enough constructors.`  

*Error* `The type has no constructors.`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `split with bindings?`  
Equivalent to `constructor 1 with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings)`?` when the conclusion is an inductive type with a single constructor. The [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) specify any parameters required for the constructor. It is typically used to split conjunctions in the conclusion such as `A /\ B` into two new goals `A` and `B`.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `exists bindings*,`  
Equivalent to `constructor 1 with `[`bindings`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) for each set of bindings (or just `constructor 1` if there are no [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings)) when the conclusion is an inductive type with a single constructor. It is typically used on existential quantifications in the form `exists x, P x.`

*Error* `Not an inductive goal with 1 constructor.`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `left with bindings?`\
*Tactic* `right with bindings?`  
These tactics apply only if `I` has two constructors, for instance in the case of a disjunction `A \/ B`. Then they are respectively equivalent to `constructor 1 with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings)`?` and `constructor 2 with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings)`?`.

*Error* `Not an inductive goal with 2 constructors.`  

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `econstructor nat_or_var with bindings??`\
*Tactic* `eexists bindings*,`\
*Tactic* `esplit with bindings?`\
*Tactic* `eleft with bindings?`\
*Tactic* `eright with bindings?`  
These tactics behave like [`constructor`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.constructor), [`exists`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.exists), [`split`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.split), [`left`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.left) and [`right`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.right), but they introduce existential variables instead of failing when a variable can't be instantiated (cf. [`eapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eapply) and [`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.apply)).

Example: [`constructor`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.constructor), [`left`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.left) and [`right`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.right)

``` coq
Print or. (* or, represented by \/, has two constructors, or_introl and or_intror *)
Inductive or (A B : Prop) : Prop :=
    or_introl : A -> A \/ B | or_intror : B -> A \/ B.

Arguments or (A B)%type_scope
Arguments or_introl [A B]%type_scope _, [_] _ _
Arguments or_intror [A B]%type_scope _, _ [_] _
1 goal

  ============================
  forall P1 P2 : Prop, P1 -> P1 \/ P2
1 goal

  P1, P2 : Prop
  H : P1
  ============================
  P1
No more goals.
```

In contrast, we won't be able to complete the proof if we select constructor 2:

``` coq
constructor 2. (* equivalent to "right" *)
1 goal

  P1, P2 : Prop
  H : P1
  ============================
  P2
```

You can also apply a constructor by name:

``` coq
intros; apply or_introl. (* equivalent to "left" *)
1 goal

  P1, P2 : Prop
  H : P1
  ============================
  P1
```

## Case analysis

The tactics in this section implement case analysis on inductive or coinductive objects (see [Variants and the match construct](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/variants.html#variants)).

*Tactic* `destruct induction_clause+, induction_principle?`  
``` ebnf
induction_clause         ::=     induction_arg as or_and_intropattern ? eqn : naming_intropattern ? occurrences ?
induction_arg            ::=     one_term_with_bindings
                         |       natural
```

Performs case analysis by generating a subgoal for each constructor of the inductive or coinductive type selected by [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg). The selected subterm, after possibly doing an [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros), must have an inductive or coinductive type. Unlike [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction), `destruct` generates no induction hypothesis.

In each new subgoal, the tactic replaces the selected subterm with the associated constructor applied to its arguments, if any.

[`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause)`+,`  
Giving multiple [`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause)s is equivalent to applying `destruct` serially on each [`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause).

[`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg)  
- If [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (in [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings)) is an identifier [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident):

  - If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) denotes a `forall` variable in the goal, then `destruct `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) behaves like [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) `until `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`; destruct `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

  - If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is no longer dependent in the goal after application of `destruct`, it is erased. To avoid erasure, use parentheses, as in `destruct (`[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`)`.

- [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) may contain holes that are denoted by “\_”. In this case, the tactic selects the first subterm that matches the pattern and performs case analysis using that subterm.

- If [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg) is a [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural), then `destruct `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) behaves like `intros until `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) followed by `destruct` applied to the last introduced hypothesis.

`as `[`or_and_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-or_and_intropattern)  
Provides names for (or applies further transformations to) the variables and hypotheses introduced in each new subgoal. The [`or_and_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-or_and_intropattern) must have one [`intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-intropattern)`*` for each constructor, given in the order in which the constructors are defined. If there are not enough names, Coq picks fresh names. Inner `intropattern`s can also split introduced hypotheses into multiple hypotheses or subgoals.

`eqn : `[`naming_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-naming_intropattern)  
Generates a new hypothesis in each new subgoal that is an equality between the term being case-analyzed and the associated constructor (applied to its arguments). The name of the new item may be specified in the [`naming_intropattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-naming_intropattern).

`with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) (in [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings))  
Provides explicit instances for the [dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).

[`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)  
Selects specific subterms of the goal and/or hypotheses to apply the tactic to. See [Occurrence clauses](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#occurrenceclauses). If it occurs in the [`induction_principle`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_principle), then there can only be one [`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause), which can't have its own [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences) clause.

[`induction_principle`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_principle)  
Makes the tactic equivalent to [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) [`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause)`+, `[`induction_principle`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_principle).

Example: Using [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct) on an argument with premises

``` coq
Parameter A B C D : Prop.

Goal (A -> B \/ C) -> D.
1 goal

  ============================
  (A -> B \/ C) -> D
1 goal

  H : A -> B \/ C
  ============================
  D
3 goals

  ============================
  A

goal 2 is:
 D
goal 3 is:
 D
goal 2 is:

  H : B
  ============================
  D
goal 3 is:

  H : C
  ============================
  D
```

The single tactic `destruct 1` is equivalent to the [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) and [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct) used here.

*Tactic* `edestruct induction_clause+, induction_principle?`  
If the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (in [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg)) has [dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) whose values can't be inferred from the `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) clause, `edestruct` turns them into existential variables to be resolved later on.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `case induction_clause+, induction_principle?`  
An older, more basic tactic to perform case analysis without recursion. We recommend using [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct) instead where possible. `case` only modifies the goal; it does not modify the [local context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-local-context).

*Tactic* `ecase induction_clause+, induction_principle?`  
If the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (in [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg)) has [dependent premises](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) whose values can't be inferred from the `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) clause, `ecase` turns them into existential variables to be resolved later on.

*Tactic* `case_eq one_term`  
A variant of the `case` tactic that allows performing case analysis on a term without completely forgetting its original form. This is done by generating equalities between the original form of the term and the outcomes of the case analysis. We recommend using the [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct) tactic with an `eqn:` clause instead.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `simple destruct identnatural`  
Equivalent to [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) `until `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)``[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`; case `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) where [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a `forall` variable in the goal and otherwise fails.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `dependent destruction ident generalizing ident+? using one_term?`  
There is a long example of [`dependent destruction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.dependent-destruction) and an explanation of the underlying technique [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#dependent-induction-examples).

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `decompose [ one_term+ ] one_term`  
Recursively decomposes a complex proposition in order to obtain atomic ones.

Example

``` coq
Goal forall A B C:Prop, A /\ B /\ C \/ B /\ C \/ C /\ A -> C.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall A B C : Prop, A /\ B /\ C \/ B /\ C \/ C /\ A -> C
3 goals

  A, B, C : Prop
  H : A /\ B /\ C \/ B /\ C \/ C /\ A
  H1 : A
  H0 : B
  H3 : C
  ============================
  C

goal 2 is:
 C
goal 3 is:
 C
No more goals.
```

Note

[`decompose`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.decompose) does not work on right-hand sides of implications or products.

*Tactic* `decompose sum one_term`  
This decomposes sum types (like `or`).

*Tactic* `decompose record one_term`  
This decomposes record types (inductive types with one constructor, like `and` and `exists` and those defined with the [`Record`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/records.html#coq:cmd.Record) command.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `destauto in ident?`  
Reduces one `match t with ...` by doing `destruct t`. If `t` is not a variable, the tactic does `case_eq t;intros ... heq;rewrite heq in *|-`. `heq` is preserved.

## Induction

*Tactic* `induction induction_clause+, induction_principle?`  
``` ebnf
induction_principle      ::=     using one_term_with_bindings occurrences ?
```

Applies an [induction principle](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#term-induction-principle) to generate a subgoal for each constructor of an inductive type.

If the argument is [dependent](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-product) in the conclusion or some hypotheses of the goal, the argument is replaced by the appropriate constructor in each of the resulting subgoals and induction hypotheses are added to the local context using names whose prefix is **IH**. The tactic is similar to [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct), except that `destruct` doesn't generate induction hypotheses.

`induction` and [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct) are very similar. Aside from the following differences, please refer to the description of [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct) while mentally substituting `induction` for [`destruct`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.destruct).

[`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause)`+,`  
If no [`induction_principle`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_principle) clause is provided, this is equivalent to doing `induction` on the first [`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause) followed by `destruct` on any subsequent clauses.

[`induction_principle`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_principle)  
[`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) specifies which [induction principle](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#term-induction-principle) to use. The optional `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) gives any values that must be substituted into the induction principle. The number of [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) must be the same as the number of parameters of the induction principle.

If unspecified, the tactic applies the appropriate [induction principle](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/inductive.html#term-induction-principle) that was automatically generated when the inductive type was declared based on the sort of the goal.

*Error* `Cannot recognize a statement based on reference.`  
The type of the [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg) (in an [`induction_clause`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_clause)) must reduce to the [`reference`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#grammar-token-reference) which was inferred as the type the induction principle operates on. Note that it is not enough to be convertible, but you can work around that with [`change`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.change):

``` coq
Definition N := nat.
N is defined
strong is declared
P is declared
1 goal

  ============================
  forall n : nat, P n
1 goal

  n : nat
  ============================
  P n
The command has indeed failed with message:
Cannot recognize a statement based on N.
1 goal

  n : N
  ============================
  P n
1 goal

  n : N
  H : forall m : N, m < n -> P m
  ============================
  P n
```

*Error* `Unable to find an instance for the variables ident … ident.`  
Use the `with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) clause or the [`einduction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.einduction) tactic instead.

Example

``` coq
Lemma induction_test : forall n:nat, n = n -> n <= n.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall n : nat, n = n -> n <= n
1 goal

  n : nat
  H : n = n
  ============================
  n <= n
2 goals

  H : 0 = 0
  ============================
  0 <= 0

goal 2 is:
 S n <= S n
1 goal

  n : nat
  H : S n = S n
  IHn : n = n -> n <= n
  ============================
  S n <= S n
```

Example: `induction` with [`occurrences`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-occurrences)

``` coq
Lemma induction_test2 : forall n:nat, n = n -> n <= n.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall n : nat, n = n -> n <= n
1 goal

  n : nat
  H : n = n
  ============================
  n <= n
2 goals

  n : nat
  H : 0 = 0
  ============================
  n <= n

goal 2 is:
 n <= n
goal 2 is:

  n, n0 : nat
  H : S n0 = S n0
  IHn0 : n0 = n0 -> n <= n
  ============================
  n <= n
```

*Tactic* `einduction induction_clause+, induction_principle?`  
Behaves like [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) except that it does not fail if some [dependent premise](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#term-dependent-premise) of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) can't be inferred. Instead, the unresolved premises are posed as existential variables to be inferred later, in the same way as [`eapply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.eapply) does.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `elim one_term_with_bindings using one_term_with_bindings?`  
An older, more basic induction tactic. Unlike [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction), `elim` only modifies the goal; it does not modify the [local context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#term-local-context). We recommend using [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) instead where possible.

`with `[`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) (in [`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings))  
Explicitly gives instances to the premises of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) (see [Bindings](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#bindings)).

`using `[`one_term_with_bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-one_term_with_bindings)`?`  
Allows explicitly giving an induction principle [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) that is not the standard one for the underlying inductive type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term). The [`bindings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-bindings) clause allows instantiating premises of the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term).

*Tactic* `eelim one_term_with_bindings using one_term_with_bindings?`  
If the type of [`one_term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-one_term) has dependent premises, this turns them into existential variables to be resolved later on.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `simple induction identnatural`  
Behaves like `intros until `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)``[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`; elim `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) when [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a `forall` variable in the goal.

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `dependent induction ident generalizingin ident+? using one_term?`  
The *experimental* tactic [`dependent induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.dependent-induction) performs induction-inversion on an instantiated inductive predicate. One needs to first [`Require`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:cmd.Require) the `Coq.Program.Equality` module to use this tactic. The tactic is based on the BasicElim tactic by Conor McBride [\[McB00\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#dblp-conf-types-mcbride00) and the work of Cristina Cornes around inversion [\[CT95\]](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/zebibliography.html#dblp-conf-types-cornest95). From an instantiated inductive predicate and a goal, it generates an equivalent goal where the hypothesis has been generalized over its indexes which are then constrained by equalities to be the right instances. This permits to state lemmas without resorting to manually adding these equalities and still get enough information in the proofs.

`generalizingin `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`+`  
First generalizes the goal by the given variables so that they are universally quantified in the goal. This is generally what one wants to do with variables that are inside constructors in the induction hypothesis. The other ones need not be further generalized.

There is a long example of [`dependent induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.dependent-induction) and an explanation of the underlying technique [here](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#dependent-induction-examples).

Example

``` coq
Lemma lt_1_r : forall n:nat, n < 1 -> n = 0.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall n : nat, n < 1 -> n = 0
2 goals

  n : nat
  ============================
  n = 0

goal 2 is:
 n = 0
```

Here we did not get any information on the indexes to help fulfill this proof. The problem is that, when we use the `induction` tactic, we lose information on the hypothesis instance, notably that the second argument is 1 here. Dependent induction solves this problem by adding the corresponding equality to the context.

``` coq
Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall n : nat, n < 1 -> n = 0
2 goals

  ============================
  0 = 0

goal 2 is:
 n = 0
```

The subgoal is cleaned up as the tactic tries to automatically simplify the subgoals with respect to the generated equalities. In this enriched context, it becomes possible to solve this subgoal.

``` coq
reflexivity.
1 goal

  n : nat
  H : S n <= 0
  IHle : 0 = 1 -> n = 0
  ============================
  n = 0
```

Now we are in a contradictory context and the proof can be solved.

``` coq
inversion H.
No more goals.
```

This technique works with any inductive predicate. In fact, the [`dependent induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.dependent-induction) tactic is just a wrapper around the [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) tactic. One can make its own variant by just writing a new tactic based on the definition found in `Coq.Program.Equality`.

See also

[`functional induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/using/libraries/funind.html#coq:tacn.functional-induction)

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `fix ident natural with ( ident simple_binder* { struct name }? : type )+?`  
A primitive tactic that starts a proof by induction. Generally, higher-level tactics such as [`induction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.induction) or [`elim`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.elim) are easier to use.

The [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s (including the first one before the `with` clause) are the names of the induction hypotheses. [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) tells on which premise of the current goal the induction acts, starting from 1, counting both dependent and non-dependent products, but skipping local definitions. The current lemma must be composed of at least [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) products.

As in a fix expression, induction hypotheses must be used on structurally smaller arguments. The verification that inductive proof arguments are correct is done only when registering the lemma in the global environment. To know if the use of induction hypotheses is correct during the interactive development of a proof, use the command [`Guarded`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Guarded).

`with ( `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` `[`simple_binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder)`* { struct `[`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name)` }? : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` )+`  
Starts a proof by mutual induction. The statements to be proven are `forall `[`simple_binder`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder)`, `[`type`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type). The identifiers [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) (including the first one before the `with` clause) are the names of the induction hypotheses. The identifiers [`name`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/assumptions.html#grammar-token-name) (in the `{ struct ... }` clauses) are the respective names of the premises on which the induction is performed in the statements to be proved (if not given, Coq guesses what they are).

<!-- -->

*Tactic* `cofix ident with ( ident simple_binder* : type )+?`  
Starts a proof by coinduction. The [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)s (including the first one before the `with` clause) are the names of the coinduction hypotheses. As in a cofix expression, the use of induction hypotheses must be guarded by a constructor. The verification that the use of coinductive hypotheses is correct is done only at the time of registering the lemma in the global environment. To know if the use of coinduction hypotheses is correct at some time of the interactive development of a proof, use the command [`Guarded`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/proof-mode.html#coq:cmd.Guarded).

`with ( `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` `[`simple_binder`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder)`* : `[`type`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type)` )+`  
Starts a proof by mutual coinduction. The statements to be proven are `forall `[`simple_binder`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#grammar-token-simple_binder)`, `[`type`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-type). The identifiers [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) (including the first one before the `with` clause) are the names of the coinduction hypotheses.

## Equality of inductive types

This section describes some special purpose tactics to work with [Leibniz equality](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#term-Leibniz-equality) of inductive sets or types.

*Tactic* `discriminate induction_arg?`  
Proves any goal for which a hypothesis in the form [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` = `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) states an impossible structural equality for an inductive type. If [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg) is not given, it checks all the hypotheses for impossible equalities. For example, `(S (S O)) = (S O)` is impossible. If provided, [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg) is a proof of an equality, typically specified as the name of a hypothesis.

If no [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg) is provided and the goal is in the form [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term)` <> `[`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), then the tactic behaves like `intro `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`; discriminate `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

The tactic traverses the normal forms of [`term`<sub>`1`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) and [`term`<sub>`2`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), looking for subterms `u` and `w` placed in the same positions and whose head symbols are different constructors. If such subterms are present, the equality is impossible and the current goal is completed. Otherwise the tactic fails. Note that opaque constants are not expanded by δ reductions while computing the normal form.

[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) (in [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg))  
Checks the hypothesis [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) for impossible equalities. If [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is not already in the context, this is equivalent to `intros until `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)`; discriminate `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident).

[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) (in [`induction_arg`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#grammar-token-induction_arg))  
Equivalent to [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros) `until `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)`; discriminate `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), where [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is the identifier for the last introduced hypothesis.
