Wildcards may be interpreted as abstractions (see for example Sections [Definitions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#definitions-ssr) and [Structure](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#structure-ssr)), or their content can be inferred from the whole context of the goal (see for example Section [Abbreviations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#abbreviations-ssr)).

### Definitions

*Tactic* `pose`  
This tactic allows to add a defined constant to a proof context. SSReflect generalizes this tactic in several ways. In particular, the SSReflect [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) tactic supports *open syntax*: the body of the definition does not need surrounding parentheses. For instance:

``` coq
pose t := x + y.
```

is a valid tactic expression.

The [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) tactic is also improved for the local definition of higher-order terms. Local definitions of functions can use the same syntax as global ones. For example, the tactic [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) supports parameters:

Example

``` coq
Lemma test : True.
1 goal

  ============================
  True
1 goal

  f := fun x y : nat => x + y : nat -> nat -> nat
  ============================
  True
```

The SSReflect [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) tactic also supports (co)fixpoints, by providing the local counterpart of the `Fixpoint f := …` and `CoFixpoint f := …` constructs. For instance, the following tactic:

``` coq
pose fix f (x y : nat) {struct x} : nat :=
  if x is S p then S (f p y) else 0.
```

defines a local fixpoint `f`, which mimics the standard plus operation on natural numbers.

Similarly, local cofixpoints can be defined by a tactic of the form:

``` coq
pose cofix f (arg : T) := … .
```

The possibility to include wildcards in the body of the definitions offers a smooth way of defining local abstractions. The type of “holes” is guessed by type inference, and the holes are abstracted. For instance the tactic:

``` coq
pose f := _ + 1.
```

is shorthand for:

``` coq
pose f n := n + 1.
```

When the local definition of a function involves both arguments and holes, hole abstractions appear first. For instance, the tactic:

``` coq
pose f x := x + _.
```

is shorthand for:

``` coq
pose f n x := x + n.
```

The interaction of the [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) tactic with the interpretation of implicit arguments results in a powerful and concise syntax for local definitions involving dependent types. For instance, the tactic:

``` coq
pose f x y := (x, y).
```

adds to the context the local definition:

``` coq
pose f (Tx Ty : Type) (x : Tx) (y : Ty) := (x, y).
```

The generalization of wildcards makes the use of the [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) tactic resemble ML-like definitions of polymorphic functions.

### Abbreviations

*Tactic* `set ident : term? := occ_switch? term`  
The SSReflect `set` tactic performs abbreviations; it introduces a defined constant for a subterm appearing in the goal and/or in the context.

SSReflect extends the [`set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.set) tactic by supplying:

- an open syntax, similarly to the [`pose (ssreflect)`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.pose-(ssreflect)) tactic;

- a more aggressive matching algorithm;

- an improved interpretation of wildcards, taking advantage of the matching algorithm;

- an improved occurrence selection mechanism allowing to abstract only selected occurrences of a term.

``` ebnf
occ_switch               ::=     { +  - ? natural * }
```

where:

- [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is a fresh identifier chosen by the user.

- [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) 1 is an optional type annotation. The type annotation [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) 1 can be given in open syntax (no surrounding parentheses). If no [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) (described hereafter) is present, it is also the case for the second [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). On the other hand, in the presence of [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch), parentheses surrounding the second [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) are mandatory.

- In the occurrence switch [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch), if the first element of the list is a natural, this element should be a number, and not an Ltac variable. The empty list `{}` is not interpreted as a valid occurrence switch; it is rather used as a flag to signal the intent of the user to clear the name following it (see [Occurrence switches and redex switches](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#ssr-rewrite-occ-switch) and [Introduction in the context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#introduction-ssr)).

The tactic:

Example

``` coq
Lemma test x :  f x + f x = f x.
1 goal

  x : nat
  ============================
  f x + f x = f x
1 goal

  x : nat
  t := f x : nat
  ============================
  t + t = t

set t := {2}(f _).
1 goal

  x : nat
  t := f x : nat
  ============================
  f x + t = f x
```

The type annotation may contain wildcards, which will be filled with appropriate values by the matching process.

The tactic first tries to find a subterm of the goal matching the second [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) (and its type), and stops at the first subterm it finds. Then the occurrences of this subterm selected by the optional [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) are replaced by [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) and a definition [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` := `[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is added to the context. If no [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) is present, then all the occurrences are abstracted.

#### Matching

The matching algorithm compares a pattern [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) with a subterm of the goal by comparing their heads and then pairwise unifying their arguments (modulo conversion). Head symbols match under the following conditions.

- If the head of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is a constant, then it should be syntactically equal to the head symbol of the subterm.

- If this head is a projection of a canonical structure, then canonical structure equations are used for the matching.

- If the head of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is *not* a constant, the subterm should have the same structure (λ abstraction, `let…in` structure, etc.).

- If the head of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is a hole, the subterm should have at least as many arguments as [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

Example

``` coq
Lemma test (x y z : nat) :  x + y = z.
1 goal

  x, y, z : nat
  ============================
  x + y = z
1 goal

  x, y, z : nat
  t := Nat.add x : nat -> nat
  ============================
  t y = z
```

- In the special case where [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is of the form `(let f := t0 in f) t1 … tn` , then the pattern [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) is treated as `(_ t1 … tn)`. For each subterm in the goal having the form `(A u1 … um)` with m ≥ n, the matching algorithm successively tries to find the largest partial application `(A u1 … uj)` convertible to the head `t0` of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

  Example

  ``` coq
  Lemma test : (let f x y z := x + y + z in f 1) 2 3 = 6.
  1 goal

    ============================
    (let f := fun x y z : nat => x + y + z in f 1) 2 3 = 6
  1 goal

    t := unkeyed (fun y z : nat => S y + z) 2 : nat -> nat
    ============================
    t 3 = 6
  ```

  The notation `unkeyed` defined in `ssreflect.v` is a shorthand for the degenerate term `let x := … in x`.

Moreover:

- Multiple holes in [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) are treated as independent placeholders.

  Example

  ``` coq
  Lemma test x y z : x + y = z.
  1 goal

    x, y, z : nat
    ============================
    x + y = z
  1 goal

    x, y, z : nat
    t := x + y : nat
    ============================
    t = z
  ```

- The type of the subterm matched should fit the type (possibly casted by some type annotations) of the pattern [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

- The replacement of the subterm found by the instantiated pattern should not capture variables. In the example above, `x` is bound and should not be captured.

  Example

  ``` coq
  Lemma test : forall x : nat, x + 1 = 0.
  1 goal

    ============================
    forall x : nat, x + 1 = 0
  The command has indeed failed with message:
  The pattern (_ + 1) did not match and has holes. Did you mean pose?
  ```

- Typeclass inference should fill in any residual hole, but matching should never assign a value to a global existential variable.

#### Occurrence selection

SSReflect provides a generic syntax for the selection of occurrences by their position indexes. These *occurrence switches* are shared by all SSReflect tactics that require control on subterm selection like rewriting, generalization, …

An *occurrence switch* can be:

- A list of natural numbers `{+ n1 … nm}` of occurrences affected by the tactic.

  Example

  ``` coq
  Lemma test : f 2 + f 8 = f 2 + f 2.
  1 goal

    ============================
    f 2 + f 8 = f 2 + f 2
  1 goal

    x := f 2 : nat
    ============================
    x + f 8 = f 2 + x
  ```

  Notice that some occurrences of a given term may be hidden to the user, for example because of a notation. Setting the [`Printing All`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:flag.Printing-All) flag causes these hidden occurrences to be shown when the term is displayed. This setting should be used to find the correct coding of the occurrences to be selected [11](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id42).

  Example

  ``` coq
  Notation "a < b":= (le (S a) b).
  1 goal

    x, y : nat
    ============================
    x < y -> S x < S y
  1 goal

    x, y : nat
    t := S x : nat
    ============================
    t <= y -> t < S y
  ```

- A list of natural numbers `{n1 … nm}`. This is equivalent to the previous `{+ n1 … nm}`, but the list should start with a number, and not with an Ltac variable.

- A list `{- n1 … nm}` of occurrences *not* to be affected by the tactic.

  Example

  ``` coq
  Lemma test : f 2 + f 8 = f 2 + f 2.
  1 goal

    ============================
    f 2 + f 8 = f 2 + f 2
  1 goal

    x := f 2 : nat
    ============================
    x + f 8 = f 2 + x
  ```

  Note that, in this goal, it behaves like `set x := {1 3}(f 2).`

- In particular, the switch `{+}` selects *all* the occurrences. This switch is useful to turn off the default behavior of a tactic that automatically clears some assumptions (see Section [Discharge](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#discharge-ssr) for instance).

- The switch `{-}` imposes that *no* occurrences of the term should be affected by the tactic. The tactic: `set x := {-}(f 2).` leaves the goal unchanged and adds the definition `x := f 2` to the context. This kind of tactic may be used to take advantage of the power of the matching algorithm in a local definition, instead of copying large terms by hand.

It is important to remember that matching *precedes* occurrence selection.

> Example
>
> ``` coq
> Lemma test x y z : x + y = x + y + z.
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y, z : nat
>   ============================
>   x + y = x + y + z
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y, z : nat
>   a := x + y : nat
>   ============================
>   x + y = a + z
> ```

Hence, in the following goal, the same tactic fails since there is only one occurrence of the selected term.

> Example
>
> ``` coq
> Lemma test x y z : (x + y) + (z + z) = z + z.
> 1 goal
>
>   x, y, z : nat
>   ============================
>   x + y + (z + z) = z + z
> The command has indeed failed with message:
> Only 1 < 2 occurrence of (x + y + (z + z))
> ```

### Basic localization

It is possible to define an abbreviation for a term appearing in the context of a goal thanks to the `in` tactical.

*Variant* `set ident := term in ident+`  
> This variant of [`set`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.set-(ssreflect)) introduces a defined constant called [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the context, and folds it in the context entries mentioned on the right hand side of `in`. The body of [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is the first subterm matching these context entries (taken in the given order).

Example

``` coq
Lemma test x t (Hx : x = 3) : x + t = 4.
1 goal

  x, t : nat
  Hx : x = 3
  ============================
  x + t = 4
1 goal

  x, t : nat
  z := 3 : nat
  Hx : x = z
  ============================
  x + t = 4
```

<!-- -->

*Variant* `set ident := term in ident+ *`  
> This variant matches [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) and then folds [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) similarly in all the given context entries but also folds [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) in the goal.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test x t (Hx : x = 3) : x + t = 4.
1 goal

  x, t : nat
  Hx : x = 3
  ============================
  x + t = 4
1 goal

  x, t : nat
  z := 3 : nat
  Hx : x = z
  ============================
  x + t = S z
```

Indeed, remember that 4 is just a notation for (S 3).

The use of the `in` tactical is not limited to the localization of abbreviations: for a complete description of the `in` tactical, see Section [Bookkeeping](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#bookkeeping-ssr) and [Localization](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#localization-ssr).

## Basic tactics

A sizable fraction of proof scripts consists of steps that do not "prove" anything new, but instead perform menial bookkeeping tasks such as selecting the names of constants and assumptions or splitting conjuncts. Although they are logically trivial, bookkeeping steps are extremely important because they define the structure of the data-flow of a proof script. This is especially true for reflection-based proofs, which often involve large numbers of constants and assumptions. Good bookkeeping consists in always explicitly declaring (i.e., naming) all new constants and assumptions in the script, and systematically pruning irrelevant constants and assumptions in the context. This is essential in the context of an interactive development environment (IDE), because it facilitates navigating the proof, allowing to instantly "jump back" to the point at which a questionable assumption was added, and to find relevant assumptions by browsing the pruned context. While novice or casual Coq users may find the automatic name selection feature convenient, the usage of such a feature severely undermines the readability and maintainability of proof scripts, much like automatic variable declaration in programming languages. The SSReflect tactics are therefore designed to support precise bookkeeping and to eliminate name generation heuristics. The bookkeeping features of SSReflect are implemented as tacticals (or pseudo-tacticals), shared across most SSReflect tactics, and thus form the foundation of the SSReflect proof language.

### Bookkeeping

During the course of a proof, Coq always presents the user with a *sequent* whose general form is:

    ci : Ti
    …
    dj := ej : Tj
    …
    Fk : Pk
    …
    =================
    forall (xl : Tl) …,
    let ym := bm in … in
    Pn -> … -> C

The *goal* to be proved appears below the double line; above the line is the *context* of the sequent, a set of declarations of *constants* `ci` , *defined constants* `dj` , and *facts* `Fk` that can be used to prove the goal (usually, `Ti` , `Tj : Type` and `Pk : Prop`). The various kinds of declarations can come in any order. The top part of the context consists of declarations produced by the Section commands `Variable`, `Let`, and `Hypothesis`. This *section context* is never affected by the SSReflect tactics: they only operate on the lower part — the *proof context*. As in the figure above, the goal often decomposes into a series of (universally) quantified *variables* `(xl : Tl)`, local *definitions* `let ym := bm in`, and *assumptions* `Pn ->`, and a *conclusion* `C` (as in the context, variables, definitions, and assumptions can appear in any order). The conclusion is what actually needs to be proved — the rest of the goal can be seen as a part of the proof context that happens to be “below the line”.

However, although they are logically equivalent, there are fundamental differences between constants and facts, on the one hand, and variables and assumptions, on the other. Constants and facts are *unordered*, but *named* explicitly in the proof text; variables and assumptions are *ordered*, but *unnamed*: the display names of variables may change at any time because of α-conversion.

Similarly, basic deductive steps such as `apply` can only operate on the goal because the Gallina terms that control their action (e.g., the type of the lemma used by `apply`) only provide unnamed bound variables. [12](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id43) Since the proof script can only refer directly to the context, it must constantly shift declarations from the goal to the context and conversely in between deductive steps.

In SSReflect, these moves are performed by two *tacticals*, `=>` and `:`, so that the bookkeeping required by a deductive step can be directly associated with that step, and that tactics in an SSReflect script correspond to actual logical steps in the proof rather than merely shuffle facts. Still, some isolated bookkeeping is unavoidable, such as naming variables and assumptions at the beginning of a proof. SSReflect provides a specific `move` tactic for this purpose.

Now, `move` does essentially nothing: it is mostly a placeholder for `=>` and `:`. The `=>` tactical moves variables, local definitions, and assumptions to the context, while the `:` tactical moves facts and constants to the goal.

Example

For example, the proof of [13](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id44)

``` coq
Lemma subnK : forall m n, n <= m -> m - n + n = m.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall m n : nat, n <= m -> m - n + n = m
```

might start with

``` coq
move=> m n le_n_m.
1 goal

  m, n : nat
  le_n_m : n <= m
  ============================
  m - n + n = m
```

where `move` does nothing, but `=> m n le_m_n` changes the variables and assumption of the goal in the constants `m n : nat` and the fact `le_n_m : n <= m`, thus exposing the conclusion `m - n + n = m`.

The `:` tactical is the converse of `=>`; indeed it removes facts and constants from the context by turning them into variables and assumptions.

``` coq
move: m le_n_m.
1 goal

  n : nat
  ============================
  forall m : nat, n <= m -> m - n + n = m
```

turns back `m` and `le_m_n` into a variable and an assumption, removing them from the proof context, and changing the goal to `forall m, n <= m -> m - n + n = m`, which can be proved by induction on `n` using `elim: n`.

Because they are tacticals, `:` and `=>` can be combined, as in

``` coq
move: m le_n_m => p le_n_p.
```

which simultaneously renames `m` and `le_m_n` into `p` and `le_n_p`, respectively, by first turning them into unnamed variables, then turning these variables back into constants and facts.

Furthermore, SSReflect redefines the basic Coq tactics `case`, `elim`, and `apply` so that they can take better advantage of `:` and `=>`. In these SSReflect variants, these tactics operate on the first variable or constant of the goal and they do not use or change the proof context. The `:` tactical is used to operate on an element in the context.

Example

> For instance, the proof of `subnK` could continue with `elim: n`. Instead of `elim n` (note, no colon), this has the advantage of removing n from the context. Better yet, this `elim` can be combined with previous `move` and with the branching version of the `=>` tactical (described in [Introduction in the context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#introduction-ssr)), to encapsulate the inductive step in a single command:

``` coq
Lemma subnK : forall m n, n <= m -> m - n + n = m.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall m n : nat, n <= m -> m - n + n = m
1 goal

  m, n : nat
  le_n_m : n <= m
  ============================
  m - n + n = m
2 goals

  m : nat
  ============================
  m - 0 + 0 = m

goal 2 is:
 m - S n + S n = m
```

which breaks down the proof into two subgoals, the second one having in its context `lt_n_m : S n <= m` and `IHn : forall m, n <= m -> m - n + n = m`.

The `:` and `=>` tacticals can be explained very simply if one views the goal as a stack of variables and assumptions piled on a conclusion:

- `tactic : a b c` pushes the context constants `a`, `b`, `c` as goal variables *before* performing the tactic;

- `tactic => a b c` pops the top three goal variables as context constants `a`, `b`, `c`, *after* the tactic has been performed.

These pushes and pops do not need to balance out as in the examples above; so `move: m le_n_m => p` would rename `m` into `p`, but leave an extra assumption `n <= p` in the goal.

Basic tactics like `apply` and `elim` can also be used without the ’:’ tactical: for example, we can directly start a proof of `subnK` by induction on the top variable `m` with

``` coq
elim=> [|m IHm] n le_n.
```

The general form of the localization tactical `in` is also best explained in terms of the goal stack:

    tactic in a H1 H2 *.

is basically equivalent to

``` coq
move: a H1 H2; tactic => a H1 H2.
```

with two differences: the `in` tactical will preserve the body of `a`, if `a` is a defined constant, and if the `*` is omitted, it will use a temporary abbreviation to hide the statement of the goal from `tactic`.

The general form of the `in` tactical can be used directly with the `move`, `case` and `elim` tactics, so that one can write

``` coq
elim: n => [|n IHn] in m le_n_m *.
```

instead of

``` coq
elim: n m le_n_m => [|n IHn] m le_n_m.
```

This is quite useful for inductive proofs that involve many facts.

See Section [Localization](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#localization-ssr) for the general syntax and presentation of the `in` tactical.

### The defective tactics

In this section, we briefly present the three basic tactics performing context manipulations and the main backward chaining tool.

#### The move tactic.

*Tactic* `move`  
This tactic, in its defective form, behaves like the [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) tactic.

Example

``` coq
Require Import ssreflect.
1 goal

  ============================
  ~ False
1 goal

  ============================
  False -> False
```

More precisely, the [`move`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.move-(ssreflect)) tactic inspects the goal and does nothing ([`idtac`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ltac.html#coq:tacn.idtac)) if an introduction step is possible, i.e., if the goal is a product or a `let … in`, and performs [`hnf`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.hnf) otherwise.

Of course this tactic is most often used in combination with the bookkeeping tacticals (see Sections [Introduction in the context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#introduction-ssr) and [Discharge](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#discharge-ssr)). These combinations mostly subsume the [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros), [`generalize`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.generalize), [`revert`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.revert), [`rename`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.rename), [`clear`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.clear) and [`pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.pattern) tactics.

#### The case tactic

*Tactic* `case`  
This tactic performs *primitive case analysis* on (co)inductive types; specifically, it destructs the top variable or assumption of the goal, exposing its constructor(s) and its arguments, as well as setting the value of its type family indices if it belongs to a type family (see Section [Type families](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#type-families-ssr)).

The SSReflect `case` tactic has a special behavior on equalities. If the top assumption of the goal is an equality, the `case` tactic “destructs” it as a set of equalities between the constructor arguments of its left and right hand sides, as per the tactic injection. For example, `case` changes the goal:

    (x, y) = (1, 2) -> G.

into:

    x = 1 -> y = 2 -> G.

The [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case) can generate the following warning:

*Warning* `SSReflect: cannot obtain new equations out of ...`  
The tactic was run on an equation that cannot generate simpler equations, for example `x = 1`.

The warning can be silenced or made fatal by using the [`Warnings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Warnings) option and the `spurious-ssr-injection` key.

Finally, the [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case) tactic of SSReflect performs `False` elimination, even if no branch is generated by this case operation. Hence the tactic [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case) on a goal of the form `False -> G` will succeed and prove the goal.

#### The elim tactic

*Tactic* `elim`  
This tactic performs inductive elimination on inductive types. In its defective form, the tactic performs inductive elimination on a goal whose top assumption has an inductive type.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test m : forall n : nat, m <= n.
1 goal

  m : nat
  ============================
  forall n : nat, m <= n
2 goals

  m : nat
  ============================
  m <= 0

goal 2 is:
 forall n : nat, m <= n -> m <= S n
```

#### The apply tactic

*Tactic* `apply term?`  
This is the main backward chaining tactic of the proof system. It takes as argument any [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) and applies it to the goal. Assumptions in the type of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) that don’t directly match the goal may generate one or more subgoals.

In its defective form, this tactic is a synonym for:

    intro top; first [refine top | refine (top _) | refine (top _ _) | …]; clear top.

where `top` is a fresh name, and the sequence of [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) tactics tries to catch the appropriate number of wildcards to be inserted. Note that this use of the [`refine`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.refine) tactic implies that the tactic tries to match the goal up to expansion of constants and evaluation of subterms.

[`apply`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.apply-(ssreflect)) has a special behavior on goals containing existential metavariables of sort `Prop`.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test : forall y, 1 < y -> y < 2 -> exists x : { n | n < 3 }, 0 < proj1_sig x.
1 goal

  ============================
  forall y : nat,
  1 < y -> y < 2 -> exists x : {n : nat | n < 3}, 0 < proj1_sig x
2 goals

  y : nat
  y_gt1 : 1 < y
  y_lt2 : y < 2
  ============================
  y < 3

goal 2 is:
 forall Hyp0 : y < 3, 0 < proj1_sig (exist (fun n : nat => n < 3) y Hyp0)
1 goal

  y : nat
  y_gt1 : 1 < y
  y_lt2 : y < 2
  ============================
  forall Hyp0 : y < 3, 0 < proj1_sig (exist (fun n : nat => n < 3) y Hyp0)
No more goals.
```

Note that the last `_` of the tactic `apply: (ex_intro _ (exist _ y _))` represents a proof that `y < 3`. Instead of generating the goal:

    0 < proj1_sig (exist (fun n : nat => n < 3) y ?Goal).

the system tries to prove `y < 3` calling the trivial tactic. If it succeeds, let’s say because the context contains `H : y < 3`, then the system generates the following goal:

    0 < proj1_sig (exist (fun n => n < 3) y H).

Otherwise the missing proof is considered to be irrelevant, and is thus discharged, generating the two goals shown above.

Last, the user can replace the trivial tactic by defining an Ltac expression named `ssrautoprop`.

### Discharge

The general syntax of the discharging tactical `:` is:

*Tactic* `tactic ident? : d_item+ clear_switch?`  

``` ebnf
d_item                   ::=     occ_switch  clear_switch ? term
```

``` ebnf
clear_switch             ::=     { ident + }
```

with the following requirements.

- [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic) must be one of the four basic tactics described in [The defective tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#the-defective-tactics-ssr), i.e., `move`, `case`, `elim` or `apply`, the `exact` tactic (section [Terminators](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#terminators-ssr)), the `congr` tactic (Section [Congruence](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#congruence-ssr)), or the application of the *view* tactical ‘/’ (Section [Interpreting assumptions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#interpreting-assumptions-ssr)) to one of `move`, `case`, or `elim`.

- The optional [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) specifies *equation generation* (Section [Generation of equations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#generation-of-equations-ssr)), and is only allowed if [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic) is `move`, `case` or `elim`, or the application of the view tactical ‘/’ (Section [Interpreting assumptions](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#interpreting-assumptions-ssr)) to `case` or `elim`.

- An [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) selects occurrences of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), as in [Abbreviations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#abbreviations-ssr); [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) is not allowed if [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic) is `apply` or `exact`.

- A clear item [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) specifies facts and constants to be deleted from the proof context (as per the `clear` tactic).

The `:` tactical first *discharges* all the [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item), right to left, and then performs the tactic, i.e., for each [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item), starting with the last one :

1.  The SSReflect matching algorithm described in Section [Abbreviations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#abbreviations-ssr) is used to find occurrences of [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term) in the goal, after filling any holes ‘\_’ in the term; however if [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic) is `apply` or `exact`, a different matching algorithm, described below, is used [14](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id45).

2.  These occurrences are replaced by a new variable; in particular, if the term is a fact, this adds an assumption to the goal.

3.  If the term is *exactly* the name of a constant or fact in the proof context, it is deleted from the context, unless there is an [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch).

Finally, the tactic is performed just after the first [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) has been generalized — that is, between steps 2 and 3. The names listed in the final [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) (if it is present) are cleared first, before [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) n is discharged.

Switches affect the discharging of a [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) as follows.

- An [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) restricts generalization (step 2) to a specific subset of the occurrences of the term, as per Section [Abbreviations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#abbreviations-ssr), and prevents clearing (step 3).

- All the names specified by a [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) are deleted from the context in step 3, possibly in addition to the term.

For example, the tactic:

``` coq
move: n {2}n (refl_equal n).
```

- first generalizes `(refl_equal n : n = n)`;

- then generalizes the second occurrence of `n`.

- finally generalizes all the other occurrences of `n`, and clears `n` from the proof context (assuming `n` is a proof constant).

Therefore, this tactic changes any goal `G` into

``` coq
forall n n0 : nat, n = n0 -> G.
```

where the name `n0` is picked by the Coq display function, and assuming `n` appeared only in `G`.

Finally, note that a discharge operation generalizes defined constants as variables, and not as local definitions. To override this behavior, prefix the name of the local definition with a `@`, like in `move: @n`.

This is in contrast with the behavior of the `in` tactical (see Section [Localization](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#localization-ssr)), which preserves local definitions by default.

#### Clear rules

The clear step will fail if the term is a proof constant that appears in other facts; in that case, either the facts should be cleared explicitly with a [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch), or the clear step should be disabled. The latter can be done by adding an [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) or simply by putting parentheses around term: both `move: (n).` and `move: {+}n.` generalize `n` without clearing `n` from the proof context.

The clear step will also fail if the [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) contains a [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) that is not in the *proof* context. Note that SSReflect never clears a section constant.

If the tactic is `move` or `case` and an equation [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is given, then clearing (step 3) for [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) is suppressed (see Section [Generation of equations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#generation-of-equations-ssr)).

Intro patterns (see Section [Introduction in the context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#introduction-ssr)) and the `rewrite` tactic (see Section [Rewriting](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#rewriting-ssr)) let one place a [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) in the middle of other items (namely identifiers, views and rewrite rules). This can trigger the addition of proof context items to the ones being explicitly cleared, and in turn this can result in `clear` errors (e.g., if the context item automatically added occurs in the goal). The relevant sections describe ways to avoid the unintended clearing of context items.

#### Matching for apply and exact

The matching algorithm for [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) of the SSReflect `apply` and `exact` tactics exploits the type of the first [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) to interpret wildcards in the other [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) and to determine which occurrences of these should be generalized. Therefore, occur switches are not needed for `apply` and `exact`.

Indeed, the SSReflect tactic `apply: H x` is equivalent to `refine (@H _ … _ x); clear H x`, with an appropriate number of wildcards between `H` and `x`.

Note that this means that matching for `apply` and `exact` has much more context to interpret wildcards; in particular, it can accommodate the `_` [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item), which would always be rejected after `move:`.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test (Hfg : forall x, f x = g x) a b : f a = g b.
1 goal

  Hfg : forall x : nat, f x = g x
  a, b : nat
  ============================
  f a = g b
1 goal

  Hfg : forall x : nat, f x = g x
  a, b : nat
  ============================
  g a = g b
```

This tactic is equivalent (see Section [Bookkeeping](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#bookkeeping-ssr)) to: `refine (trans_equal (Hfg _) _).` and this is a common idiom for applying transitivity on the left hand side of an equation.

#### The abstract tactic

*Tactic* `abstract: d_item+`  
This tactic assigns an abstract constant previously introduced with the `[: `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` ]` intro pattern (see Section [Introduction in the context](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#introduction-ssr)).

In a goal like the following:

    m : nat
    abs : <hidden>
    n : nat
    =============
    m < 5 + n

The tactic `abstract: abs n` first generalizes the goal with respect to `n` (that is not visible to the abstract constant `abs`) and then assigns abs. The resulting goal is:

    m : nat
    n : nat
    =============
    m < 5 + n

Once this subgoal is closed, all other goals having `abs` in their context see the type assigned to `abs`. In this case:

    m : nat
    abs : forall n, m < 5 + n
    =============
    …

For a more detailed example, the reader should refer to Section [Structure](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#structure-ssr).

### Introduction in the context

The application of a tactic to a given goal can generate (quantified) variables, assumptions, or definitions, which the user may want to *introduce* as new facts, constants or defined constants, respectively. If the tactic splits the goal into several subgoals, each of them may require the introduction of different constants and facts. Furthermore it is very common to immediately decompose or rewrite with an assumption instead of adding it to the context, as the goal can often be simplified and even proved after this.

All these operations are performed by the introduction tactical `=>`, whose general syntax is

*Tactic* `tactic => i_item+`  

``` ebnf
i_item                   ::=     i_pattern  s_item  clear_switch  i_view  i_block
```

``` ebnf
s_item                   ::=     /=  //  //=
```

``` ebnf
i_view                   ::=     { } ? / term  /ltac:( tactic )
```

``` ebnf
i_pattern                ::=     ident  >  _  ?  *  +  occ_switch ? ->  <-  [ i_item ? | ]  -  [: ident + ]
```

``` ebnf
i_block                  ::=     [^ ident ]  [^~ ident  natural ]
```

The `=>` tactical first executes [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic), then the [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item)s, left to right. An [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item) specifies a simplification operation; a [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) specifies context pruning as in [Discharge](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#discharge-ssr). The [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern)s can be seen as a variant of *intro patterns* (see [`intros`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.intros)); each performs an introduction operation, i.e., pops some variables or assumptions from the goal.

#### Simplification items

An [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item) can simplify the set of subgoals or the subgoals themselves.

- `//` removes all the “trivial” subgoals that can be resolved by the SSReflect tactic [`done`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.done) described in [Terminators](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#terminators-ssr), i.e., it executes `try done`.

- `/=` simplifies the goal by performing partial evaluation, as per the tactic [`simpl`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/equality.html#coq:tacn.simpl) [15](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id46).

- `//=` combines both kinds of simplification; it is equivalent to `/= //`, i.e., `simpl; try done`.

When an [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item) immediately precedes a [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch), then the [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) is executed *after* the [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item), e.g., `{IHn}//` will solve some subgoals, possibly using the fact `IHn`, and will erase `IHn` from the context of the remaining subgoals.

#### Views

The first entry in the [`i_view`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_view) grammar rule, `/`[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term), represents a view (see Section [Views and reflection](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#views-and-reflection-ssr)). It interprets the top of the stack with the view [`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term). It is equivalent to `move/`[`term`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-term).

A [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) that immediately precedes an [`i_view`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_view) is complemented with the name of the view if an only if the [`i_view`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_view) is a simple proof context entry [20](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id51). E.g., `{}/v` is equivalent to `/v{v}`. This behavior can be avoided by separating the [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) from the [`i_view`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_view) with the `-` intro pattern or by putting parentheses around the view.

A [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) that immediately precedes an [`i_view`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_view) is executed after the view application.

If the next [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) is a view, then the view is applied to the assumption in top position once all the previous [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) have been performed.

The second entry in the [`i_view`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_view) grammar rule, `/ltac:(` [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic) `)`, executes [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic). Notations can be used to name tactics, for example

``` coq
Notation "'myop'" := (ltac:(my ltac code)) : ssripat_scope.
```

lets one write just `/myop` in the intro pattern. Note the scope annotation: views are interpreted opening the `ssripat` scope. We provide the following ltac views: `/[dup]` to duplicate the top of the stack, `/[swap]` to swap the two first elements and `/[apply]` to apply the top of the stack to the next.

#### Intro patterns

SSReflect supports the following [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern)s.

[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)  
pops the top variable, assumption, or local definition into a new constant, fact, or defined constant [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident), respectively. Note that defined constants cannot be introduced when δ-expansion is required to expose the top variable or assumption. A [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) (even an empty one) immediately preceding an [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) is complemented with that [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) if and only if the identifier is a simple proof context entry [20](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id51). As a consequence, by prefixing the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with `{}` one can *replace* a context entry. This behavior can be avoided by separating the [`clear_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-clear_switch) from the [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) with the `-` intro pattern.

Thus, trying to clear an [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) `H` with `{H}H` triggers the following warning:

*Warning* `Duplicate clear of H. Use { }H instead of { H }H`  
The warning can be silenced or made fatal with the [`Warnings`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/vernacular-commands.html#coq:opt.Warnings) option with the `duplicate-clear` key.

`>`  
pops every variable occurring in the rest of the stack. Type class instances are popped even if they don't occur in the rest of the stack. The tactic `move=> >` is equivalent to `move=> ? ?` on a goal such as:

    forall x y, x < y -> G

A typical use if `move=>> H` to name `H` the first assumption, in the example above `x < y`.

`?`  
pops the top variable into an anonymous constant or fact, whose name is picked by the tactic interpreter. SSReflect only generates names that cannot appear later in the user script [16](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id47).

`_`  
pops the top variable into an anonymous constant that will be deleted from the proof context of all the subgoals produced by the `=>` tactical. They should thus never be displayed, except in an error message if the constant is still actually used in the goal or context after the last [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) has been executed ([`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item) can erase goals or terms where the constant appears).

`*`  
pops all the remaining apparent variables/assumptions as anonymous constants/facts. Unlike `?` and `move`, the `*` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) does not expand definitions in the goal to expose quantifiers, so it may be useful to repeat a `move=> *` tactic, e.g., on the goal:

    forall a b : bool, a <> b

a first `move=> *` adds only `_a_ : bool` and `_b_ : bool` to the context; it takes a second `move=> *` to add `_Hyp_ : _a_ = _b_`.

`+`  
temporarily introduces the top variable. It is discharged at the end of the intro pattern. For example `move=> + y` on a goal:

    forall x y, P

is equivalent to `move=> _x_ y; move: _x_` that results in the goal:

    forall x, P

`occ_switch? ->`  
(resp. [`occ_switch`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-occ_switch) `<-`) pops the top assumption (which should be a rewritable proposition) into an anonymous fact, rewrites (resp. rewrites right to left) the goal with this fact (using the SSReflect `rewrite` tactic described in Section [Rewriting](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#rewriting-ssr), and honoring the optional occurrence selector), and finally deletes the anonymous fact from the context.

`[` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) \* `| … |` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) \* `]`  
when it is the very *first* [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) after tactic `=>` tactical *and* the tactic is not a move, is a *branching* [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern). It executes the sequence [`i_item`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) on the i-th subgoal produced by the tactic. The execution of the tactic should thus generate exactly m subgoals, unless the `[…]` [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) comes after an initial `//` or `//=` [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item) that closes some of the goals produced by the tactic, in which case exactly m subgoals should remain after the [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item), or we have the trivial branching [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) \[\], which always does nothing, regardless of the number of remaining subgoals.

`[` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) \* `| … |` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) \* `]`  
when it is *not* the first [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) or when the tactic is a `move`, is a *destructing* [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern). It starts by destructing the top variable, using the SSReflect `case` tactic described in [The defective tactics](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#the-defective-tactics-ssr). It then behaves as the corresponding branching [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern), executing the sequence [`i_item`<sub>`i`</sub>](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) in the i-th subgoal generated by the case analysis; unless we have the trivial destructing [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) `[]`, the latter should generate exactly m subgoals, i.e., the top variable should have an inductive type with exactly m constructors [17](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id48). While it is good style to use the [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) i \* to pop the variables and assumptions corresponding to each constructor, this is not enforced by SSReflect.

`-`  
does nothing, but counts as an intro pattern. It can also be used to force the interpretation of `[` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) \* `| … |` [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) \* `]` as a case analysis like in `move=> -[H1 H2]`. It can also be used to indicate explicitly the link between a view and a name like in `move=> /eqP-H1`. Last, it can serve as a separator between views. Section [Views and reflection](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#views-and-reflection-ssr) [19](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#id50) explains in which respect the tactic `move=> /v1/v2` differs from the tactic `move=> /v1-/v2`.

`[:` [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) `…]`  
introduces in the context an abstract constant for each [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). Its type has to be fixed later on by using the `abstract` tactic. Before then the type displayed is `<hidden>`.

Note that SSReflect does not support the syntax `(ipat, …, ipat)` for destructing intro patterns.

#### Clear switch

Clears are deferred until the end of the intro pattern.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test x y : Nat.leb 0 x = true -> (Nat.leb 0 x) && (Nat.leb y 2) = true.
1 goal

  x, y : nat
  ============================
  Nat.leb 0 x = true -> Nat.leb 0 x && Nat.leb y 2 = true
1 goal

  y : nat
  ============================
  true && Nat.leb y 2 = true
```

If the cleared names are reused in the same intro pattern, a renaming is performed behind the scenes.

Facts mentioned in a clear switch must be valid names in the proof context (excluding the section context).

#### Branching and destructuring

The rules for interpreting branching and destructing [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) are motivated by the fact that it would be pointless to have a branching pattern if the tactic is a `move`, and in most of the remaining cases the tactic is `case` or `elim`, which implies destructuring. The rules above imply that:

- `move=> [a b].`

- `case=> [a b].`

- `case=> a b.`

are all equivalent, so which one to use is a matter of style; `move` should be used for casual decomposition, such as splitting a pair, and `case` should be used for actual decompositions, in particular for type families (see [Type families](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#type-families-ssr)) and proof by contradiction.

The trivial branching [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern) can be used to force the branching interpretation, e.g.:

- `case=> [] [a b] c.`

- `move=> [[a b] c].`

- `case; case=> a b c.`

are all equivalent.

#### Block introduction

SSReflect supports the following [`i_block`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_block)s.

`[^ `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` ]`  
*block destructing* [`i_pattern`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_pattern). It performs a case analysis on the top variable and introduces, in one go, all the variables coming from the case analysis. The names of these variables are obtained by taking the names used in the inductive type declaration and prefixing them with [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident). If the intro pattern immediately follows a call to `elim` with a custom eliminator (see [Interpreting eliminations](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#custom-elim-ssr)), then the names are taken from the ones used in the type of the eliminator.

Example

``` coq
Record r := { a : nat; b := (a, 3); _ : bool; }.
r is defined
a is defined
b is defined
1 goal

  ============================
  r -> True
1 goal

  xa : nat
  xb := (xa, 3) : nat * nat
  _x?_ : bool
  ============================
  True
```

`[^~ `[`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident)` ]`  
*block destructing* using [`ident`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-ident) as a suffix.

`[^~ `[`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural)` ]`  
*block destructing* using [`natural`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-natural) as a suffix.

Only a [`s_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-s_item) is allowed between the elimination tactic and the block destructing.

### Generation of equations

The generation of named equations option stores the definition of a new constant as an equation. The tactic:

``` coq
move En: (size l) => n.
```

where `l` is a list, replaces `size l` by `n` in the goal and adds the fact `En : size l = n` to the context. This is quite different from:

``` coq
pose n := (size l).
```

which generates a definition `n := (size l)`. It is not possible to generalize or rewrite such a definition; on the other hand, it is automatically expanded during computation, whereas expanding the equation `En` requires explicit rewriting.

The use of this equation name generation option with a `case` or an `elim` tactic changes the status of the first [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item), in order to deal with the possible parameters of the constants introduced.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test (a b :nat) : a <> b.
1 goal

  a, b : nat
  ============================
  a <> b
2 goals

  a, b : nat
  E : a = 0
  ============================
  0 <> b

goal 2 is:
 S n <> b
```

If the user does not provide a branching [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) as first [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item), or if the [`i_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-i_item) does not provide enough names for the arguments of a constructor, then the constants generated are introduced under fresh SSReflect names.

Example

``` coq
Lemma test (a b :nat) : a <> b.
1 goal

  a, b : nat
  ============================
  a <> b
2 goals

  a, b : nat
  E : a = 0
  H : 0 = b
  ============================
  False

goal 2 is:
 False
goal 2 is:

  a, b, _n_ : nat
  E : a = S _n_
  H : S _n_ = b
  ============================
  False
```

Combining the generation of named equations mechanism with the [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case) tactic strengthens the power of a case analysis. On the other hand, when combined with the [`elim`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.elim) tactic, this feature is mostly useful for debug purposes, to trace the values of decomposed parameters and pinpoint failing branches.

### Type families

When the top assumption of a goal has an inductive type, two specific operations are possible: the case analysis performed by the [`case`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.case) tactic, and the application of an induction principle, performed by the [`elim`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.elim) tactic. When this top assumption has an inductive type, which is moreover an instance of a type family, Coq may need help from the user to specify which occurrences of the parameters of the type should be substituted.

*Variant* `case: d_item+ / d_item+`\
*Variant* `elim: d_item+ / d_item+`  
A specific `/` switch indicates the type family parameters of the type of a [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) immediately following this `/` switch. The [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) on the right side of the `/` switch are discharged as described in Section [Discharge](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#discharge-ssr). The case analysis or elimination will be done on the type of the top assumption after these discharge operations.

Every [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) preceding the `/` is interpreted as an argument of this type, which should be an instance of an inductive type family. These terms are not actually generalized, but rather selected for substitution. Occurrence switches can be used to restrict the substitution. If a term is left completely implicit (e.g., writing just `_`), then a pattern is inferred by looking at the type of the top assumption. This allows for the compact syntax:

``` coq
case: {2}_ / eqP.
```

where `_` is interpreted as `(_ == _)`, since `eqP T a b : reflect (a = b) (a == b)` and `reflect` is a type family with one index.

Moreover, if the [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) list is too short, it is padded with an initial sequence of `_` of the right length.

Example

Here is a small example on lists. We define first a function that adds an element at the end of a given list.

``` coq
Require Import List.
A is declared
add_last is defined
add_last is recursively defined (guarded on 2nd argument)
```

Then we define an inductive predicate for case analysis on lists according to their last element:

``` coq
Inductive last_spec : list A -> Type :=
| LastSeq0 : last_spec nil
| LastAdd s x : last_spec (add_last x s).
last_spec is defined
last_spec_rect is defined
last_spec_ind is defined
last_spec_rec is defined
last_spec_sind is defined
1 goal

  A : Type
  ============================
  forall l, last_spec l
lastP is declared
```

We are now ready to use `lastP` in conjunction with `case`.

``` coq
Lemma test l : (length l) * 2 = length (l ++ l).
1 goal

  A : Type
  l : list A
  ============================
  length l * 2 = length (l ++ l)
2 goals

  A : Type
  l : list A
  ============================
  length nil * 2 = length (nil ++ nil)

goal 2 is:
 forall (s : list A) (x : A),
 length (add_last x s) * 2 = length (add_last x s ++ add_last x s)
```

Applied to the same goal, the tactic `case: l / (lastP l)` generates the same subgoals, but `l` has been cleared from both contexts:

``` coq
case: l / (lastP l).
2 goals

  A : Type
  ============================
  length nil * 2 = length (nil ++ nil)

goal 2 is:
 forall (s : list A) (x : A),
 length (add_last x s) * 2 = length (add_last x s ++ add_last x s)
```

Again applied to the same goal:

``` coq
case: {1 3}l / (lastP l).
2 goals

  A : Type
  l : list A
  ============================
  length nil * 2 = length (l ++ nil)

goal 2 is:
 forall (s : list A) (x : A),
 length (add_last x s) * 2 = length (l ++ add_last x s)
```

Note that the selected occurrences on the left of the `/` switch have been substituted with `l` instead of being affected by the case analysis.

The equation name generation feature combined with a type family `/` switch generates an equation for the *first* dependent [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) specified by the user. Again starting with the above goal, the command:

Example

``` coq
Lemma test l : (length l) * 2 = length (l ++ l).
1 goal

  A : Type
  l : list A
  ============================
  length l * 2 = length (l ++ l)
2 goals

  A : Type
  l : list A
  E : l = nil
  ============================
  length nil * 2 = length (l ++ nil)

goal 2 is:
 length (add_last x s) * 2 = length (l ++ add_last x s)
goal 2 is:

  A : Type
  l, s : list A
  x : A
  E : l = add_last x s
  ============================
  length (add_last x s) * 2 = length (l ++ add_last x s)
```

There must be at least one [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) to the left of the `/` switch; this prevents any confusion with the view feature. However, the [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) to the right of the `/` are optional, and if they are omitted, the first assumption provides the instance of the type family.

The equation always refers to the first [`d_item`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#grammar-token-d_item) in the actual tactic call, before any padding with initial `_`. Thus, if an inductive type has two family parameters, it is possible to have SSReflect generate an equation for the second one by omitting the pattern for the first; note however that this will fail if the type of the second parameter depends on the value of the first parameter.

## Control flow

### Indentation and bullets

A linear development of Coq scripts gives little information on the structure of the proof. In addition, replaying a proof after some changes in the statement to be proved will usually not display information to distinguish between the various branches of case analysis for instance.

To help the user in this organization of the proof script at development time, SSReflect provides some bullets to highlight the structure of branching proofs. The available bullets are `-`, `+` and `*`. Combined with tabulation, this lets us highlight four nested levels of branching; the most we have ever needed is three. Indeed, the use of “simpl and closing” switches, of terminators (see Section [Terminators](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#terminators-ssr)) and selectors (see Section [Selectors](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#selectors-ssr)) is powerful enough to avoid most of the time more than two levels of indentation.

Here is a fragment of such a structured script:

    case E1: (abezoutn _ _) => [[| k1] [| k2]].
    - rewrite !muln0 !gexpn0 mulg1 => H1.
      move/eqP: (sym_equal F0); rewrite -H1 orderg1 eqn_mul1.
      by case/andP; move/eqP.
    - rewrite muln0 gexpn0 mulg1 => H1.
      have F1: t %| t * S k2.+1 - 1.
        apply: (@dvdn_trans (orderg x)); first by rewrite F0; exact: dvdn_mull.
        rewrite orderg_dvd; apply/eqP; apply: (mulgI x).
        rewrite -{1}(gexpn1 x) mulg1 gexpn_add leq_add_sub //.
        by move: P1; case t.
      rewrite dvdn_subr in F1; last by exact: dvdn_mulr.
      + rewrite H1 F0 -{2}(muln1 (p ^ l)); congr (_ * _).
        by apply/eqP; rewrite -dvdn1.
      + by move: P1; case: (t) => [| [| s1]].
    - rewrite muln0 gexpn0 mul1g => H1.
    ...

### Terminators

To further structure scripts, SSReflect supplies *terminating* tacticals to explicitly close off tactics. When replaying scripts, we then have the nice property that an error immediately occurs when a closed tactic fails to prove its subgoal.

It is hence recommended practice that the proof of any subgoal should end with a tactic that *fails if it does not solve the current goal*, like [`discriminate`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/writing-proofs/reasoning-inductives.html#coq:tacn.discriminate), [`contradiction`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.contradiction) or [`assumption`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/tactics.html#coq:tacn.assumption).

In fact, SSReflect provides a generic tactical that turns any tactic into a closing one (similar to [`now`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/auto.html#coq:tacn.now)). Its general syntax is:

*Tactic* `by tactic`  

The Ltac expression `by [`[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)` | `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)` | …]` is equivalent to `do [done | by `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)` | by `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)` | …]`, which corresponds to the standard Ltac expression `first [done | `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)`; done | `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)`; done | …]`.

In the script provided as example in Section [Indentation and bullets](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#indentation-ssr), the paragraph corresponding to each sub-case ends with a tactic line prefixed with a `by`, like in:

``` coq
by apply/eqP; rewrite -dvdn1.
```

*Tactic* `done`  
The [`by`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.by) tactical is implemented using the user-defined, and extensible, [`done`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.done) tactic. This [`done`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.done) tactic tries to solve the current goal by some trivial means and fails if it doesn’t succeed. Indeed, the tactic expression `by `[`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic) is equivalent to [`tactic`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/language/core/basic.html#grammar-token-tactic)`; done`.

Conversely, the tactic `by [ ]` is equivalent to [`done`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.done).

The default implementation of the [`done`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#coq:tacn.done) tactic, in the `ssreflect.v` file, is:

``` coq
Ltac done :=
  trivial; hnf; intros; solve
   [ do ![solve [trivial | apply: sym_equal; trivial]
         | discriminate | contradiction | split]
   | case not_locked_false_eq_true; assumption
   | match goal with H : ~ _ |- _ => solve [case H; trivial] end ].
```

The lemma `not_locked_false_eq_true` is needed to discriminate *locked* boolean predicates (see Section [Locking, unlocking](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#locking-ssr)). The iterator tactical `do` is presented in Section [Iteration](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#iteration-ssr). This tactic can be customized by the user, for instance to include an [`auto`](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proofs/automatic-tactics/auto.html#coq:tacn.auto) tactic.

A natural and common way of closing a goal is to apply a lemma that is the exact one needed for the goal to be solved. The defective form of the tactic:

``` coq
exact.
```

is equivalent to:

``` coq
do [done | by move=> top; apply top].
```

where `top` is a fresh name assigned to the top assumption of the goal. This applied form is supported by the `:` discharge tactical, and the tactic:

``` coq
exact: MyLemma.
```

is equivalent to:

``` coq
by apply: MyLemma.
```

(see Section [Discharge](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/V8.19.0/refman/proof-engine/ssreflect-proof-language.html#discharge-ssr) for the documentation of the apply: combination).

Warning

The list of tactics (possibly chained by semicolons) that follows the `by` keyword is considered to be a parenthesized block applied to the current goal. Hence for example if the tactic:

``` coq
by rewrite my_lemma1.
```

succeeds, then the tactic:

``` coq
by rewrite my_lemma1; apply my_lemma2.
```

usually fails since it is equivalent to:

``` coq
by (rewrite my_lemma1; apply my_lemma2).
```

### Selectors

*Tactic* `last`\
*Tactic* `first`
